#1993. Lens vs Como - prediction, team news, lineups

By Jonathan O'Shea | 02 Nov 2026 15:38, Last updated: 04 Nov 2026 13:45

Languishing outside the Champions League's top 24, Lens will aim to move level with Como when they meet at Stade Bollaert-Delelis on Wednesday night.

Following their historic defeat of Manchester United, the Italian debutants have put six points on the board, while their hosts only have three and lie below the playoff zone.

Since Lens started their fourth Champions League campaign with a thrilling 3-2 comeback win over Slavia Prague, the French club have come away empty-handed from their subsequent fixtures.

Les Sang et Or were first beaten 2-0 at home by Sporting Lisbon, then suffered another defeat on their travels, going down 3-0 to Club Brugge.

Remarkably, 16 games and some 28 years have now passed since they last kept a clean sheet in the Champions League.

Lens returned to Europe's top table by finishing second in Ligue 1 last term but, after a slow start, new boss Dino Toppmoller swiftly made way for Yannick Cahuzac.

Though Toppmoller's former assistant started positively with three straight league wins, his side were beaten by their bitter local rivals last time out.

With a late Olivier Giroud goal, Lille snatched victory in the 125th Derby du Nord on Friday night, leaving Lens ninth in the French top flight.

Now, Cahuzac's side must try to respond with maximum points, as they surely need at least two more wins from five remaining Champions League matches.

Como took one step closer to the knockout phase last month, thumping Manchester United 4-1 on a memorable night at Stadio Sinigaglia, where main man Nico Paz bagged a brace.

Regardless of United's dire state, that marked an incredible achievement for a club promoted back to Italy's top tier only two years earlier - and they were down in Serie D as recently as 2019.

Expertly led by Cesc Fabregas, 10 goals from their first three games is the best haul of any debutant in UEFA's elite competition since 1973 - and each one has been scored from open play.

Paz and top scorer Tasos Douvikas already have five Champions League strikes between them, and the pair have been even more productive in Serie A, with 11 goal involvements combined.

Since losing 3-2 to Feyenoord on matchday two, Como have embarked on a streak of five consecutive wins across all competitions, scoring 13 goals and conceding just three.

New France cap Lucas Da Cunha was decisive from the spot in Sunday's 1-0 victory against rock-bottom Venezia, taking the Lariani up to a club-record tally of 23 points from their opening 10 games.

Now occupying fourth place - where they finished last term - Como are closely in touch with Italy's current top three, and few would rule them out of the Scudetto race.

Lens will be missing several men on Wednesday, with defensive duo Ismaelo Ganiou and Maik Nawrocki joining forwards Abdalllah Sima and Odsonne Edouard on the sidelines.

The latter has undergone surgery for an adductor injury and could be ruled out until 2027, so Franjo Ivanovic is expected to lead the home side's attack.

Still struggling with a hamstring problem, Ecuadorian wing-back Jhoanner Chavez is also a doubt.

While veteran playmaker Florian Thauvin has created the most chances across the Champions League's opening three matchdays (15), Como star Paz has been directly involved in five goals.

Douvikas has scored in all three of the Lariani's league-phase appearances, so they are both integral parts of the Fabregas plan.

The Catalan coach will still be without Moise Kean, Trevoh Chalobah, Jesus Rodriguez and Assane Diao due to injury.

Sometimes rotated with Chelsea loanee Robert Sanchez, goalkeeper Jean Butez recently replaced Robin Risser of Lens in the France squad.

Risser; Aguilar, Baidoo, Todibo; Abdulhamid, Cuisance, Haidara, Udol; Thauvin, Kadile; Ivanovic

Butez; Couto, Kempf, Ramon, Valle; Perrone, Ricci; Da Cunha, Paz, Baturina; Douvikas

Although the sample size is small, Como tend to start sharply in Europe, having scored first - and during the first half - in all three of their Champions League matches.

The Lariani also possess a potency that Lens simply cannot withstand, so they will move up to nine points and leave their hosts stranded on three.

#1991. Amorim analyses how Milan were able to overpower Inter: “High pressure and low blocking”

AC Milan head coach Ruben Amorim refused to be drawn into discussions about the Scudetto, even if he does see improvements from his side.

Milan were in dreamland after 45 minutes of their derby clash against Inter, going in 3-1 up at the break thanks to goals from Christian Pulisic, Adrien Rabiot and Diego Moreira. As it would turn out, that would be enough to win the bragging rights.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

It marked a fourth straight win for Milan in the derby and it reduces the gap to the city rivals back down to four points. While there is still work to be done for the Rossoneri, it feels like a big step forward mentally for the squad.

Amorim spoke to Sky after the full-time whistle to reflect on what was a memorable night for him as a head coach and for the team, with his words relayed by MilanNews.

Is this the most important victory of the start of the season?

“It’s important. The atmosphere is fantastic, and you can tell after a match like that, especially on a Wednesday like this. It’s clear, even more so after the defeat against Bologna, we wanted to celebrate even more.

“I’m really proud of what my players did, and with so little rest between matches, and especially once again after Bologna, they really fought for the entire match. I’m really proud.”

A nearly perfect team: do you have anything to complain about? You seemed calmer today…

“I try to read and interpret what the team tells me: from the first minute I had the feeling that we were ready to be competitive. The team has always been focused and calm, and so I always had this confidence.”

Is AC Milan a different Milan with Modric, Rabiot, and Pulisic?

“It’s not just those three players, I think it’s the whole atmosphere, the team’s focus. I like the way everyone plays and expresses themselves. For example, I’d like to talk a little about Pavlović and De Vrij.

“They performed well in every game, especially against such a strong team, even in the penalty area. And then, obviously, players like Rabiot, Pulisic, Moreira… they all did very well. All together, I have to say, we were a better team.”

Why Gila on the right and De Winter in the centre?

“Looking at Inter’s stats, we didn’t know if Dimarco would play. They play and cross a lot from the wings and come to create a lot of density in the box, so I think Pavlović and De Winter are the best for crossing.

“That’s the idea: to match our defenders with their attackers, so everyone can play in slightly different defensive roles.”

How did you manage not to concede anything to Inter in the second half?

“I think the lines were closer together; you could see that throughout the match in terms of high pressure and low blocking. The lines were always close together, so the distances were shorter, which obviously also allowed us to run less and stay fresher throughout the game.

“We were very aggressive on the outside, intercepting many crosses before they were launched, which is very difficult against a team like Inter. We defended well by pressing high up, but we also defended well on the sides. We were more aggressive than we usually are.”

“What Cardinale was saying is that the objective is the Scudetto, but it’s important to win these games to make the fans understand that things won’t change in a month, two months, or a year.

“We have to go through this process: you can’t just hire a new coach, replace all the players, and have a new squad for each new coach; that takes time. Then we’ll need magical nights and evenings, and obviously we’ll need to get through difficulties like Wednesday’s and the joy of tonight.

“I want to say that the situation won’t change overnight; it’s not possible. Is the Scudetto possible? I don’t know when, but we still have to be very honest with the fans, and I know that people aren’t stupid; they understand and know the growth this team and this club are in.”

#1990. Portsmouth vs Swansea City - prediction, team news, lineups

By Calum Burrowes | 02 Nov 2026 15:44, Last updated: 02 Nov 2026 16:50

Portsmouth and Swansea City meet at Fratton Park on Tuesday night, with both sides looking to build on their encouraging starts to the 2026-27 Championship campaign.

Pompey were held to a 0-0 draw by recently relegated Burnley at the weekend, while the Swans returned to winning ways in emphatic fashion by thrashing Blackburn Rovers 4-0 at the Swansea.com Stadium.

Since securing promotion to the Championship in May 2024 and successfully avoiding a return to League One across the last two seasons, John Mousinho has continued to oversee steady progress at Portsmouth, with their recent results suggesting the manager has once again taken his side up another level.

Pompey were held to a goalless draw by Burnley, who were competing in the Premier League just a few months ago, although the result offered a mixed assessment of their performance, highlighting both their defensive strengths and their continued struggles in attack.

After 13 Championship matches, Portsmouth sit in the top half of the table, having recorded five wins, four draws and four defeats to collect 19 points and establish a healthy cushion over the relegation zone.

However, Saturday's stalemate against Burnley, who have now gone 22 matches without a win at Turf Moor, underlined their ability to remain organised at the back while also exposing their wastefulness in the final third, where a lack of cutting edge continues to undermine their efforts.

Their tally of 16 goals is the lowest of any side in the top half and among the poorest returns in the division, making their attacking output an area Mousinho will be eager to improve as he approaches his 200th match in charge of Pompey.

As for Swansea City, they make the trip to Fratton Park enjoying their best start to a Championship season since being relegated from the Premier League more than eight years ago, despite heading into the weekend on the back of consecutive defeats.

The Swans travelled to Loftus Road a week before Halloween and were thrashed 5-0 by Queens Park Rangers, following an earlier defeat to former Premier League side West Ham United, with their place at the top of the table subsequently taken by Middlesbrough.

Despite entering the weekend inside the top two, Vitor Matos and his Swansea side were determined to end their brief losing run at the earliest opportunity, and they did so in emphatic fashion by putting four goals past Blackburn Rovers in South Wales.

First-half strikes from Stephen Eustaquio, Joseph Opoku and Filip Lissah put the Swans firmly in control before Ross Stewart added a fourth shortly before the hour mark, completing a superb response to the heaviest defeat of Matos's reign and matching their biggest victory under the Portuguese manager.

That eighth win of the campaign, alongside two draws and three defeats, leaves Swansea second in the standings, just two points behind the league leaders as they look to maintain their promotion push.

Looking to build on their encouraging start to the campaign, Portsmouth could name an unchanged side for their second away fixture in four days after coming through the weekend's draw without any fresh injury concerns.

However, Mousinho will remain without Connor Ogilvie, Keshi Anderson, John Swift, Luke Brooke-Smith and Colby Bishop, who are all unavailable.

As for Swansea, Matos would ideally like to retain the starting XI that performed so impressively against Blackburn, but he may be forced into at least one change.

Eustaquio, who opened the scoring in Saturday's 4-0 victory, is a doubt after being forced off 17 minutes from time with a groin injury.

Adam Idah replaced the Canadian midfielder during the weekend win, but Matos may favour a more like-for-like alternative when selecting his side for Tuesday's trip to Hampshire.

Cameron Burgess, Ronald and Moussa Kounfolo Yeo remain unavailable for the Welsh visitors.

Schmid; Swanson, Poole, Dia, Meghoma; Pack, Mohamed; Kamara, Segecic, Kavuma-McQueen; Marezi

Vigouroux; Lissah, Cabango, Welsh, Tymon; Widell, Fulton, Just; Opoku, Stewart, Ji-Sung

Although Portsmouth are unbeaten in their last five matches heading into a meeting with second-placed Swansea, we believe the hosts will fall just short of extending that run.

We expect a closely contested encounter at Fratton Park, but the Swans should have enough attacking quality to follow up their emphatic weekend victory with another three points in Hampshire.

#1989. Cole Palmer and Man United unpacked: The truth about Old Trafford links, why he really got a new Chelsea deal, Xabi Alonso's 'emotional control' advice after red card and how he must step up against 'Big Six' rivals

Published: 08:00 EDT, 30 October 2026 | Updated: 05:46 EDT, 31 October 2026

Despite the speculation snowballing in the second half of last season – and it was as if there had been an explosion at a rumour mill – Manchester United never did come in for Cole Palmer.

No conversations were held with Chelsea in the summer. Not about him, anyway. United negotiated for Andrey Santos. It took two days to agree that deal, worth £48million plus £2m in easily achievable bonuses and with Chelsea retaining a 10 per cent sell-on clause.

But according to sources with knowledge of those talks and any others which occurred in that window, Palmer’s name was not mentioned whenever officials from both clubs, such as Chelsea sporting director, Paul Winstanley, and United director of football, Jason Wilcox, spoke.

Which might surprise a few. Because it was said Manchester United wanted Cole Palmer and Cole Palmer wanted Manchester United. Apparently he missed Manchester, could no longer stand London, was tired of waiting for Chelsea to be good again and thought he belonged in the Champions League. He was the boyhood United fan who grew up worshipping Wayne Rooney.

That was what we were seeing while scrolling social media in the build-up to a summer when England manager Thomas Tuchel excluded the 24-year-old from his World Cup squad.

In fairness, the original suggestion that Palmer might be interested in United was not plucked out of thin air. It is said that at least one person close to Palmer's circle was happy to stand up those suggestions.

Cole Palmer returns from suspension for Saturday's match against Manchester United, the club he was linked with in the summer

Palmer's red card against Tottenham last weekend was the first of his career

Daily Mail Sport has also learned one former United legend who dabbles in media work was likewise privately claiming he knew Palmer fancied the move. This came at a time when it was unclear whether Bruno Fernandes would be staying or sold to Saudi Arabia.

Yet nothing happened, and now, tomorrow at Stamford Bridge, Fernandes will return from the naughty step to represent United, and Palmer from his one-game suspension to play for Chelsea.

Chelsea had insisted all along that Palmer was untouchable. They even handed him another improved contract earlier this month, despite his last season not reaching the standards he had set for himself.

He ended an injury-interrupted 2025-26 with 11 goal involvements in the Premier League, after securing 23 in the previous season, and 33 before that.

When asked for the reasoning behind that new deal – whether it followed interest in him from a rival or was to provide parity after the £117million signing of Morgan Rogers from Aston Villa – Chelsea sources described it as a desire to lock down one of their best players.

He was already contracted to 2033. Now he is tied to 2034 on a nicer salary. Nobody in the Premier League has a longer contract, though as Chelsea head into another challenging game against a ‘Big Six’ side, Palmer could do with earning his pay rise.

We have seen this playmaker step up on occasion, usually when there is a trophy for winning.

Palmer signed an improved contract at Chelsea earlier this month despite a below-par campaign last season

In the 2025 Club World Cup final, where he made Paris Saint-Germain’s superstars seem mediocre compared to him. In the Conference League final of that same year, where Palmer had a ‘sod it’ moment as he turned on his creativity, telling us afterwards that he was sick of going backwards and sideways, as per Enzo Maresca’s patience-first philosophy.

Yet these glimpses of his genius have been fleeting in the Premier League’s most high-pressured matches. In 27 games versus Chelsea’s ‘Big Six’ opponents, Palmer has scored only two non-penalty goals.

Both of those arrived against United in his very first season when Mauricio Pochettino got the best out of him.

That is not to disregard the eight penalties he has dispatched which displayed his willingness to embrace extreme psychological pressure from 12 yards.

But statistically, his goals per 90, assists per 90, shots per 90 and chances created per 90 all decrease when playing Arsenal, Liverpool, Manchester City, United or Tottenham Hotspur, compared to his Premier League output overall ever since signing for Chelsea in 2023.

He has had a fun time toying with Spurs on occasion, but not last weekend. Palmer was deservedly shown two yellows in that 2-0 defeat, Chelsea’s first home loss to their rivals since 2018 – one for barging into Mateus Fernandes, and the other for standing on Conor Gallagher’s ankle.

We get it – he was frustrated, feeding on scraps, hardly ever in the game. But this was a flashback to the ill-discipline which plagued Chelsea’s previous campaign under Maresca.

In the 2025 Club World Cup final, Palmer made Paris Saint-Germain’s superstars seem mediocre compared to him

With Joao Pedro sidelined, Chelsea need Palmer to step up now that he is back from his ban

There was nothing cool to that performance from a player who now sells his own ice cubes – it's £3.50 for four pieces shaped like footballs if interested – and Alonso privately reminded him afterwards about the importance of emotional control. Palmer apologised.

It was the first red card of his career, and the first shown to a Chelsea player since Alonso took charge in the summer, with Palmer suspended for their Carabao Cup penalty shootout loss to Liverpool on Wednesday. Another opportunity at a trophy slipped away at Anfield.

With Joao Pedro sidelined – and no specific date set for his return from a knee injury – Chelsea need Palmer to step up now that he is back from his ban.

Against the United team that a fair few thought he could be joining in the summer would be as good a time as any to repay Chelsea’s faith and begin banishing the ‘Big Six’ narrative attached to his name.

Arsenal are one of a number of clubs to allegedly suffer a blow in their efforts to sign Nottingham Forest midfielder Morgan Gibbs-White.

#1986. Scotland on alert as Slovenia rocked by fan mutiny before crunch Nations League clash

Slovenia boss Bostjan Cesar has pleaded with their own fans to behave after a bizarre threat by Maribor supporters to disrupt their huge game with Switzerland in Scotland's Nations League group.

Scotland will be paying close attention to the other game in the group when Sebastien Pocognoli's side host North Macedonia a week on Friday, as they try and overhaul the Slovenians into second place in the section, after that damaging defeat at Hampden.

But the game between Slovenia and Switzerland is at the centre of a huge storm among the hosts.

Slovenia were originally due to play the game in Ljubljana, where they drew 0-0 with Scotland, but were forced to switch the game because of the poor state of the playing surface at the Stozice Stadium.

Read more: 'We must improve': Pocognoli spells out where Scotland have to up their game

They will now play for the first time in five years at the Ljudski vrt stadium in Maribor, but have run into a major obstacle.

NK Maribor's ultras - the Viole - have been engaged in a long-running dispute with the Slovenian FA following heavy disciplinary fines, protests and stadium bans.

And they have threatened to disrupt the game against the Swiss, which would lead to UEFA sanctions unless the Slovenian FA, the NSZ, close their South Stand section where they gather and leave it empty.

They unfurled a banner at the weekend which stated, 'NSZ the choice is yours: Close the stand or open your wallet.'

It provoked outrage in Slovenia and Cesar has urged fans to behave. He said: "I am a coach, so I cannot influence everything. But I believe that there will be no complications. I hope that real fans will come to support the national team, which has not played in Maribor for a long time.

"Let's make a positive story in Maribor and in the end we can all celebrate together.

"We have a great chance of getting second in the group, which was above our expectations at the start of the section."

And the Slovenian FA stated: "We hope and believe our national team will be welcome in Maribor and there will be no trouble."

#1985. What Chelsea must do to sign Alex Scott after Bournemouth owner's transfer update

By Ben Knapton | 02 Nov 2026 16:08

Chelsea must not make a move for Bournemouth midfielder Alex Scott before deciding on the futures of their own engine-room enforcers, a Blues legend has exclusively told Sports Mole.

Chelsea are believed to have identified Scott as their leading January transfer target, after trying and failing to lure the England international away from the Vitality Stadium during the summer transfer window.

Chelsea are supposedly 'completely focused' on signing Scott over the winter, although Liverpool, Manchester City and Manchester United have not yet given up hope of winning the race either.

Bournemouth owner Bill Foley recently delivered an update on Scott's future, insisting that the Cherries have not given up hope of tying him to a new deal beyond 2028, but admitting that young players can sometimes get "stars in their eyes".

Asked by Sports Mole whether Scott could fill Enzo Fernandez's boots at Chelsea, Gus Poyet gave the transfer his seal of approval but implored his former club to sort out which of their midfielders can be moved on first.

"I like the player," Poyet said. "I have seem him a lot and I think he is a very good player. Chelsea need to first decide on the players at the club first, before looking to sign anyone else.

"They have to decide what the future is as they have Caicedo, Lavia, James and others in the centre of midfield, so they must identify who will be the main starters and then move forward on whether Scott is the player they want and then who will then move on."

Scott previously spent one season in the Bournemouth academy between 2016 and 2017, before making a name for himself at Bristol City and earning a return to the Cherries in 2023 for £19.2m.

The midfielder has since scored seven goals and set up seven more for Bournemouth across all tournaments, while winning his first two senior England caps during the September/October international break.

However, it was on Scott's first start for England against Croatia that he aggravated his hamstring injury, and it remains to be seen if he is selected for Thomas Tuchel's November squad.

Chelsea currently have five recognised central midfielders on the books in Moises Caicedo, Valentin Barco, Jordan Henderson, Romeo Lavia and Mahdi Nicoll-Jazuli, while Reece James and Malo Gusto can fill in if required.

The fledgling Nicoll-Jazuli is only 16 years of age, though, and will likely spend another two or three years either developing with the youth team or out on loan regardless of whether Chelsea sign Scott.

Henderson - 20 years Nicoll-Jazuli's senior - is only under contract until 2028, at which point he will be 38 years old, and it is difficult to envisage the Englishman sticking around for longer than 24 months.

Meanwhile, Barco and Caicedo's contracts run to 2033, while the injury-plagued Lavia is tied down to 2030 and has shown signs of a revival alongside Caicedo in recent weeks.

If Scott were to arrive in January, the 23-year-old should immediately battle Lavia to partner Caicedo in Xabi Alonso's engine room, with Barco and Henderson providing youthful and experienced backup options.

Gus Poyet was speaking to Sports Mole on behalf of William Hill sports betting.

Niko Kovac's side will follow this match with back-to-back Bundesliga games against Elversberg and Borussia Monchengladbach, before returning to European action against Arsenal at the Emirates Stadium on November 24.

Dortmund reached the Champions League knockout phase playoffs in 2025-26, losing to Atalanta BC, so there is plenty of room for improvement this term.

Borussia Dortmund form (all competitions):

Serhou Guirassy has been in strong form this season, scoring eight times and registering two assists in 13 appearances, and the 30-year-old will continue in the final third of the field.

Fabio Silva has five goals and two assists in 13 matches this season and will also start, while Jobe Bellingham is in line to feature as an advanced midfielder for the German club.

As for Real Betis, Cucho Hernandez (calf) and Junior Firpo (muscular) are both out of the match, but no fresh issues have been reported.

Three players have scored four times for Real Betis this season - Isco, Marc Bartra and Abde Ezzalzouli - and the trio are set to feature in the first XI.

Troy Parrott has two goals in 11 appearances for the Seville outfit during the 2026-27 campaign and should also feature in the starting side due to Hernandez's absence.

Meanwhile, Antony and Pablo Fornals are expected to be in the XI.

All four goals came in the first half, with Christian Pulisic’s header and Adrien Rabiot’s flick from a corner putting Milan in dreamland less than 10 minutes in. Alessandro Bastoni halved the deficit, before Diego Moreira’s outstanding free-kick restored the two-goal lead.

#1979. Man United news: Erik ten Hag says relegation "is possible" amid Michael Carrick struggles

By Darren Plant | 02 Nov 2026 16:20

Erik ten Hag has claimed that former club Manchester United cannot rely on reputation alone to avoid relegation from the Premier League.

Man United are currently preparing to face Roma in the Champions League on Tuesday night having not won a game in any competition since September 10.

Although Michael Carrick was defiant in a press conference on Monday, the Red Devils only sit outside of the Premier League relegation zone on goal difference.

Given the players that they have at their disposal and the increasing possibility of appointing a more experienced replacement for Carrick, the assumption is that Man United will retain their top-flight status.

Nevertheless, speaking to ESPN NL's 'Goedemorgen Eredivisie', Ten Hag says that no-one associated with Man United can afford any complacency.

The Dutchman claims that Man United are at risk of being involved in a "vicious circle".

He said: "In the Premier League it's certainly possible, because all the teams are simply strong.

"They're all strong squads, all good managers. And if you end up on the wrong side once and you really get into that vicious circle, then it can become very difficult."

Man United have not suffered relegation from the top flight of English football since 1974.

Of 12 managers who have been in the Man United dugout since Sir Alex Ferguson's retirement, only three have lifted silverware.

With a Europa League, League Cup and Community Shield to his name and a win ratio of more than 58% over 144 matches, the stats say that Jose Mourinho is Man United's best manager since Ferguson.

While Ten Hag never had the same affinity with the fans as the Portuguese, he guided the club to a League Cup and FA Cup across a 128-game stint.

Despite his reputation having lowered from his time at Old Trafford, Ten Hag deserves more respect for the job that he did at the Theatre of Dreams.

#1978. Porto vs Napoli - prediction, team news, lineups

By Jonathan O'Shea | 02 Nov 2026 17:13, Last updated: 04 Nov 2026 13:42

One of three teams still without a point, Porto will again try to get off the mark in this season's Champions League when Napoli visit Estadio do Dragao on Wednesday evening.

While the Italian side got up and running last time out, they have lost six and won none of their last seven away games at Europe's top level.

Last month's 1-0 home loss to PSV Eindhoven was Porto's third consecutive Champions League defeat, leaving them in danger of failing to make the knockout rounds later this term.

Following previous setbacks against Manchester City and Real Betis, the Dragons have crucially conceded the first goal each time, always putting them on the back foot.

So, approaching the midpoint of this season's league phase, Porto need at least nine points just to reach the playoffs - and that may not even prove enough.

Still facing tough trips to Feyenoord and Liverpool, Francesco Farioli's men must try to maximise home advantage in midweek, having continued their domestic domination last time out.

After ending a three-year wait for the Portuguese title, they have brought that form into the current campaign: 10 straight wins have put them well clear of both Lisbon clubs atop the Primeira Liga table.

Keeping yet another clean sheet, Porto strolled to a 4-0 win against rock-bottom Estoril at the weekend, and they have only conceded four goals so far.

However, they are now expected to make more of an impact in Europe, as the former Champions League winners look to regain lost glories.

When Farioli hosts his fellow Tuscan Massimiliano Allegri on Wednesday, it will mark the fifth competitive meeting between Porto and Napoli.

In a couple of two-legged ties, each side has gone through once: the Italian side progressed in the 1974-75 UEFA Cup, and Porto won 3-2 on aggregate in the 2013-14 Europa League.

This time, Napoli are three points ahead of their Portuguese counterparts in the Champions League, after edging a chaotic seven-goal contest against Bodo/Glimt on matchday three.

Having lost to Arsenal and Villarreal before welcoming the Norwegian giant-killers to Campania, they finally posted the club's 100th win in UEFA competition, largely thanks to Scott McTominay's brace.

Yet, before setting off for northern Portugal, Napoli are winless in seven Champions League away games, which partly explains why they finished 30th in the 36-team table last term.

A former finalist with Juventus, Allegri has personally lost eight of his last 10 matches at the elite level, and he is also under pressure for some dismal domestic results.

After his current team lost 2-0 to Juve on Sunday evening, they lie eighth in the Serie A standings and - with a 14-point deficit to surprise leaders Lazio - are surely already out of the title race.

Porto are still missing injured pair William Gomes and Vasco Sousa, while it remains to be seen if Polish winger Oskar Pietuszewski will be ready to play in midweek.

The latter skipped Saturday's league fixture with a minor thigh problem, while left-back Zaidu limped off at half time due to a knee issue.

Martim Fernandes missed that game with tonsillitis but could be involved on Wednesday; Chris Smalling, Gabriel Mec and Dominik Prpic will not, having been left off Farioli's Champions League list.

Allegri's options have been trimmed by a number of absences: Alessandro Buongiorno, David Neres, Costantino Favasuli, Alisson Santos, Leonardo Spinazzola and Benoit Badiashile were already unavailable before Stanislav Lobotka injured his left ankle last week.

Vanja-Milinkovic Savic also missed the defeat to Juventus with a knock, and first-choice striker Rasmus Hojlund was sidelined by flu.

Furthermore, full-backs Giovanni Di Lorenzo and Mathias Olivera both sustained muscular injuries in Turin.

Despite a slight ankle sprain, Kevin De Bruyne may make his 86th Champions League appearance from the bench: the Belgian veteran has already created 10 chances from open play in this season's edition.

D. Costa; A. Costa, Bednarek, Kiwior, Zaidu; Froholdt, Rosario, Veiga; Pepe, A. Silva, Sainz

Meret; Beukema, Rrahmani, Marin; Politano, Anguissa, Gilmour, McTominay, Olivera; Vergara; Hojlund

The combination of Porto's stunning domestic form and Napoli's away-day woes strongly suggest a home win on Wednesday night.

Struggling in Serie A, the Italian side are also burdened by a huge injury list, so their hosts can finally put some points on the board.

#1977. GdS: ‘Milanissimo’ – how Amorim outfoxed Chivu in resounding derby win

In last night’s Derby della Madonnina, AC Milan proved that Ruben Amorim has laid the foundations for a long-term project.

Considering how October had been for Milan, most arrived at the game torn about how it would go. If you offered most a draw, they’d take it on the spot. However, the squad didn’t enter the game without belief.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Opening the scoring within five minutes, it was clear they’d come to take the game to the title leaders, and the 3-1 scoreline proved it. A dominant performance, with Amorim once again starring.

Before the game, as this morning’s Gazzetta dello Sport recalled, the Portuguese stated that he was aiming to win the Scudetto, so winning last night’s game would be pivotal. So, that’s why this result feels like more than ‘just’ three points.

They’ve now not lost in eight derbies and won their last four – a first since 1972-73 – so that confidence is backed by historical statistics. A performance like that cannot be limited to numbers, though.

Diego Moreira, Adrien Rabiot, Mike Maignan and Strahinja Pavlovic were all excellent, proving why they are pillars of the team consistently.

The best performance, though, was from Amorim. As Gazzetta states, he was perfect in ‘tactics and psychology’, winning the game with his mind in both ways. He lifted the squad after their midweek defeat and innovated the tools at his disposal again.

Whilst Cristian Chivu considered numerous tactical approaches, the Portuguese was set in his 4-2-3-1. Fluid again, with different movements to counter Inter’s side – such as Sankhoun Diawara pressing to stop Djed Spence.

Chivu had to deal with issues, but he was not alone with that. In other words, a lack of options in his squad cannot be a reason for a performance like that. After all, they had one shot on target in 90 minutes and looked almost resigned despite being on top in moments.

A night of celebrations for the Rossoneri, whilst Inter saw witches, thanks to Amorim and a bit of ‘Milanissimo’.

#1976. RB Leipzig vs Manchester City - prediction, team news, lineups

By Oliver Thomas | 02 Nov 2026 18:00, Last updated: 04 Nov 2026 12:49

Former Manchester City defender Martin Demichelis will lead his RB Leipzig side into Wednesday night’s Champions League clash with the Citizens at the Red Bull Arena.

The two teams butt heads for the first time since November 2023 when City came from two goals down at half time to win 3-2 in a thrilling group-stage contest at the Etihad Stadium.

Just three days after edging past Brighton & Hove Albion on penalties in the EFL Cup fourth round, Man City delivered a surprisingly toothless display against the same opponent last Saturday as they fell to a narrow 1-0 home defeat in the Premier League.

For the third time this season, Enzo Maresca’s side conceded inside the opening 15 minutes, with Yasin Ayari’s goal enough to condemn the Citizens to back-to-back Premier League losses as well as surrender top spot to champions Arsenal.

City will be desperate to return to winning ways in their next top-flight fixture at Nottingham Forest prior to November’s international break, but they must first shift their attention to the Champions League where they have accumulated six points from their opening three League Phase fixtures.

Sitting 10th in the 36-team standings, the Sky Blues suffered a 4-2 home defeat to holders Paris Saint-Germain in between victories against Porto (2-0) and AEK Athens (5-1), beating the latter with a much-changed side a fortnight ago.

Man City have come out on top in only eight of their last 20 Champions League matches (D2 L10), but they head to Germany having won four of their previous six meetings with Leipzig (D1 L1) while they have also prevailed in 21 of their 32 UCL encounters against German opposition (D5 L6).

After a season without European competition, RB Leipzig are back in the Champions League this term and have picked up just three points from their first three matches, leaving them down in 29th place in the 36-team League Phase table.

Die Roten Bullen edged to a slender 1-0 home win over Dutch champions PSV Eindhoven on matchday two, courtesy of a late goal from Brajan Gruda, but this result took place in between heavy 4-1 away defeats to both Como and Real Madrid.

Appointed head coach in June, Martin Demichelis has won eight and lost five of his 13 matches in charge of Leipzig in all competitions; they beat Schalke 04 by a 2-0 scoreline last Saturday to climb up to fourth in the Bundesliga standings, just three points behind unbeaten leaders Bayern Munich.

Demichelis made 15 appearances for Wednesday’s opponents Man City in the Champions League between 2013-14 and 2015-16, with the former Argentine defender scoring once in a 2-1 win away against Borussia Monchengladbach in September 2015.

The 45-year-old is now aiming to steer his Leipzig side to their fourth consecutive victory in all competitions and their first over Man City since they celebrated a 2-1 home triumph in the 2021-22 group stage. However, Die Roten Bullen have lost their last five UEFA games against English opposition.

RB Leipzig duo Assan Ouedraogo (shoulder) and Marc Guiu (muscle) remain sidelined with injuries, while former Burnley defender Maxime Esteve is doubtful with a knock that forced him to miss last weekend’s win over Schalke.

Christopher Nkunku watched on as an unused substitute last time out and it remains to be seen whether he will be fit to start on Wednesday; the Frenchman is one of only five UCL players to score a hat-trick and finish on the losing team, with his memorable treble coming in a 6-3 defeat at Man City in 2021-22.

Antonio Nusa, who has scored a team-high five goals this season, could start on the left side of front three next to Gruda and Romulo Cardoso, while Christoph Baumgartner may be fit to start in centre-midfield at the expense of Rocco Reitz.

As for Man City, their only injury concern is with attacker Antoine Semenyo, who will likely target a return from a knee injury in mid-December.

Rayan Cherki and Phil Foden are two strong contenders to earn a recall, the latter of whom score a hat-trick in City’s convincing win over AEK Athens. At least one of Ayyoub Bouaddi, Enzo Fernandez or Elliot Anderson could therefore make way.

Marc Guehi is pushing to start at centre-back alongside either Abdukodir Khusanov or Ruben Dias, while Josko Gvardiol – who scored for Leipzig against Man City in the first leg of a last-16 tie in the 2022-23 Champions League – could be replaced at left-back by Nico O'Reilly.

Erling Haaland has scored more goals against Leipzig (12 goals, eight games) than against any other opponent in his career, including a UCL record-equalling five strikes in City's 7-0 win in the second leg of the last-16 tie in 2022-23. Few would be surprised to see the prolific Norwegian start again on Wednesday.

Vandevoordt; Baku, Orban, Lukeba, Raum; Banzuzi, El Aynaoui, Baumgartner; Gruda, Romulo, Nusa

Manchester City possible starting lineup:

Donnarumma; Nunes, Dias, Guehi, O'Reilly; Anderson, Fernandez; Foden, Cherki, Doku; Haaland

The previous six meetings between Leipzig and Man City have produced 30 goals – an average of five per game – so an entertaining, end-to-end encounter can be expected on Wednesday.

The Citizens have conceded 12 goals in their last six matches and continue to look vulnerable at the back, providing Leipzig with plenty of optimism. However, we are backing Maresca’s men to rediscover their clinical touch and outscore their German counterparts in a six-goals thriller.

#1975. Rangers star savours maiden Scotland call-up after candid admission over international hopes

James Penrice has described his first Scotland call-up as an “incredibly proud” moment, admitting that representing his country was not an achievement he had envisaged during the early years of his career.

The Rangers defender was left stunned after learning of his inclusion in Sebastien Pocognoli’s latest squad for the upcoming Nations League double-header with North Macedonia and Switzerland only minutes before heading out for training.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

The unexpected confirmation that left him struggling to comprehend the personal significance of the milestone, with the versatile 27-year-old rewarded for a string of consistent performances since arriving at Ibrox on a season-long loan from Greek side AEK Athens.

Returning to Scottish football in the summer, the former Partick Thistle, Livingston and Hearts star has been an integral part of Rangers progress under Derek McInnes, making 14 appearances and scoring on his debut against St Mirren. He also provided a crucial assist in last Saturday’s Premier Sports Cup semi-final victory over Aberdeen.

And Penrice was quick to acknowledge the contribution of his teammates, recognising the dressing room influence in helping him reach a position where international selection became a distinct possibility.

“I found out five minutes before I came out [for training] and just went ‘oh my god unreal’,” Penrice told Rangers TV. “Incredibly proud. I have waited a wee while, but I knew coming back to Scotland, coming to Rangers, it would help my cause. So it's credit to the boys in there as well. They've helped me incredibly and I'm just buzzing.”

Penrice revealed that, earlier in his career, he had not considered representing Scotland a realistic prospect. His selection is an endorsement of the progress made since joining Rangers, where he has established himself as a first-team regular.

He confessed: “It's a weird feeling because I don't ever think going through the early part of my career that I would ever be called up. But it's happened now so I'm just delighted.

“It's an incredibly proud moment for me and my family. They will be buzzing, my phone will probably be going off, it's nuts. I'll have hundreds of missed calls now from my mum asking why I never told her! But I'm just buzzing.”

Penrice will now look ahead to the prospect of making his national team debut when Scotland host League B1 bottom side North Macedonia at Hampden on Friday, 13 November before travelling to St Gallen to face group leaders Switzerland three days later.

By Oliver Thomas | 02 Nov 2026 18:05, Last updated: 02 Nov 2026 18:29

Manchester City manager Enzo Maresca will consider making a few changes to his starting lineup for Wednesday’s Champions League clash with RB Leipzig at the Red Bull Arena.

Nearly everyone is fit for the Citizens, with Antoine Semenyo the lone exception as he recovers from a knee injury that requires several weeks of treatment.

Man City were beaten 1-0 by Brighton in the Premier League last weekend, with playmaker Rayan Cherki a notable omission from the starting lineup.

In defence, Josko Gvardiol may start against his former club but could be replaced at left-back by Nico O'Reilly, while centre-back Marc Guehi will be pushing to replace Abdukodir Khusanov who started alongside captain Ruben Dias last weekend.

#1973. Revealed: Scottish journalist did not include Kylian Mbappe in his Ballon d'Or voting - separately, investigation launched into suspicious bets that returned £149,000 and predicted Harry Kane's glory

Published: 08:24 EDT, 31 October 2026 | Updated: 09:02 EDT, 31 October 2026

Kylian Mbappe was a shock top-10 omission from Scotland's Ballon d'Or vote as scrutiny continues to surround Harry Kane's victory, including the launch of an investigation into suspicious bets.

Kane and Mbappe were locked in a fierce race to be crowned the best player in the world and it was England captain Kane who just edged it at Monday's glitzy ceremony in London.

A full breakdown of how each nation's journalist voted has since come to light and it can be revealed that Scotland's voter did not put Real Madrid and France star Mbappe in his top 10.

The Scottish journalist, who was one of three reporters to leave Mbappe off his top 10, joined by colleagues in Greece and Ukraine, had Kane as his winner, followed by Lamine Yamal and Rodri, both of whom won the World Cup.

Fellow Spaniard Fabian Ruiz ranked fourth, with Erling Haaland, Dayot Upamecano, Khvicha Kvaratskhelia, Marc Cucurella, Ferran Torres and Lionel Messi completing his top 10.

Only two countries left Kane off the top 10 - Mexico and Ivory Coast - while four nations overlooked Yamal - Belarus, Cameroon, Croatia and Greece. Amazingly, the Greek journalist left out Mbappe AND Yamal, including William Pacho (3rd), Joao Neves (5th), Michael Olise (6th), Gabriel (8th), Marquinhos (9th) and Declan Rice (10th) instead.

Suspicious bets made around the Ballon d'Or has triggered an investigation from French police

Former winner Rodri got 10 first place votes - Croatia, Czech Republic, Guatemala, Iceland, Nigeria, Serbia, the United States, South Korea, Thailand and Vietnam - while six countries put Messi on top.

The bigger issue with the voting - as an overall event there were ample problems, as explained by Daily Mail Sport, who was in attendance on the night - was what has been described as suspicious betting.

An investigation by French publication 'Upside', as detailed by the Guardian, has explained that bets that triggered £149,000 in winnings has triggered an inquest by organisers France Football.

Police have been alerted and are looking in to allegations that 12 bets placed on Polymarket - an American cryptocurrency-based platform - were done so with, in the view of organisers, an alarming level of accuracy.

The identified accounts correctly predicted and bet on the eventual top five, leading to internal concerns at France Football that the result had been leaked or compromised.

Upside's findings, which are understood to have since been passed on to police, discovered 12 accounts created in the month of October that made a series of very similar bets. Seven of the accounts only placed bets on the Ballon d'Or market.

France Football go to great lengths to limit the number of people with knowledge of the results prior to announcements on the night. They made sure players and their entourages, including those of Yamal, Mbappe and Kane, were kept in the dark.

But, Upside's investigation has served up some alarming allegations that will now be further examined by French police.

Nevertheless, a start against Inter meant that he was able to control the game from the first minute and set the tempo of the game, rather than trying to find a new one, which he very much did. Thanks to that, Milan claimed all three points.

Speaking at full-time to CBS Golazo, Modric explained how the team recovered after the defeat in midweek, the journey of the team and why he chose to stay, as MilanNews relays.

“An incredible victory, an incredible performance from the first minute. I think this was perhaps our best game of the season. Overall, we deserved the win and we’re really happy after the disappointing result against Bologna midweek.”

How did you recover after the defeat against Bologna?

“We have to stay positive. We can’t complain too much about the last match because we know the next one is coming. It’s an important match and there’s no better opportunity to test ourselves against Inter, and we did just that. Unfortunately, if we want to achieve something important, we can’t afford to lose games like the one in Bologna.”

“We’re growing as a team, and we’ve got new ideas. There will be ups and downs at times, but we have to try to minimise them if we want to win titles.”

What do you think of the atmosphere at San Siro?

“It was incredible. Since I arrived here, the atmosphere has always been fantastic, in every game, but especially in games like the derbies. Tonight, from the warm-up, they were incredible, and that kind of atmosphere helps you win even more.”

After the disappointment of failing to qualify for the Champions League last season, you decided to stay at Milan. Why?

“I’m happy at Milan; I feel loved and appreciated here. I spoke with the club and the new coach and I wanted to stay because I’m happy here; I love this game and I enjoy it. I stayed to help the team and the younger players grow.”

#1968. Scotland lay out Scott McTominay plans as Sebastien Pocognoli awaits first sight of talisman

Scotland manager Sebastien Pocognoli intends to try to make “a good connection” with Scott McTominay after naming the Napoli midfielder in his squad for the first time.

Pocognoli is relieved the midfielder, who underwent a small heart procedure earlier this season, has returned to the fold.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

The Belgian is looking forward to meeting McTominay in the flesh. It’s already tempting to suggest that Pocognoli is pinning his hopes on the player following an underwhelming start to his time as manager.

The Belgian succeeded Steve Clarke in August. Scotland have since won just one of their first four Nations League games and are now sitting third in Group B1, behind Switzerland and Slovenia.

They require a minimum of four points against North Macedonia at Hampden next Friday and then away to Switzerland three days later to have any chance of finishing second and featuring in the play-offs.

The latter game is two days before the first anniversary of Scotland’s titanic 4-2 win over Denmark that secured a place at this summer’s World Cup. McTominay got that famous night underway with an overhead kick after just three minutes.

He has already scored twice for Napoli since returning to the side last month. Pocognoli has only spoken to McTominay online so far and is looking forward to sitting down with him in person as he looks to establish a connection with Scotland’s most valuable player.

He stressed that it is up to him as manager to find a way to ensure the other players give McTominay the chance to excel rather than simply waiting for the Italy-based star to spark the team. It will be interesting to see who he replaces. John McGinn, Lewis Ferguson and Billy Gilmour were the middle three in the last outing against Slovenia, which Scotland lost 2-1. Ryan Christie played just behind Oli McBurnie in attack.

“He (McTominay) will bring experience, quality, an expectation of goals, a presence in the box - and he’ll bring leadership as part of the captain’s group,” said Pocognoli.

“He has a strong voice. He’s a different character to the others, everyone is different. But it’s up to me to make sure the game plan for him and the players allows him to shine. And it’s not just on him to make the team shine, if you know what I mean? That’s the challenge.”

“I just want to know him a little bit more, from the personal aspect,” he added. “We all know his quality. I think he can fit into the way we want to play.

“So I’m just excited to see him on the pitch, to see if he can bring something extra in the way we want to play.

“Also, to see how he fits into the group with my own eyes. I want to make a real contact with him because before it has only been on the phone or by video call. I’m looking forward to meeting him.”

Pocognoli, who has also brought striker Che Adams back into the squad after injury, stressed that McTominay remains committed to the Scotland cause. The 29-year-old was heavily criticised in the summer following a perceived poor showing in the World Cup, although this was before the problem with his heart came to light.

“He was really disappointed to miss the first camp and was already talking about the next camp,” said Pocognoli, recalling his first conversations with the player.

“At that point we weren’t sure because we had to see his rehabilitation. But he was excited to try his best to reach the November camp and he’s still excited now, which is good.”

#1967. Vitor Pereira reveals Nottingham Forest sacking email ‘was not correct’ and sets Premier League title target

By Alexis Pereira | 02 Nov 2026 18:16

Vitor Pereira has revealed that Nottingham Forest sacked him by email at 11.58pm on 30 June, and the Portuguese manager says the way the club went about it ‘was not correct’. Pereira saved Forest from relegation last season, but he has now told The Athletic that he was dismissed with the pre-season already planned.

The 58-year-old was appointed in February, when Forest were three points above the relegation zone, and left them 16th in the Premier League, five points ahead of relegated West Ham United and above Tottenham Hotspur. His contract contained a clause allowing either party to end the agreement before the end of June, and Forest used it with two minutes to spare.

By the time the email arrived, Pereira had reviewed the positives and negatives of the previous season, arranged the pre-season friendlies and even identified possible signings. The players were due to report within weeks, but under a different manager.

‘It was a complete surprise,’ Pereira told The Athletic. ‘I never heard anything that made me feel or think the club no longer counted on me. In the end, they had the right to decide what they wanted for the club, and I accept that.’

He accepted the decision, but not the manner in which owner Evangelos Marinakis’ regime carried it out.

‘The only thing that was not correct was the way they did it - that was the only unfair part. Sending an email... two minutes before midnight, when we had already organised everything for pre-season.’

The late timing had a reason. It came just after Forest learned that Oliver Glasner, who won the Conference League and the 2025 FA Cup with Crystal Palace, was interested in taking over following his exit from Selhurst Park.

‘If they had said to me, “Vitor, although you have organised everything, we have another possibility...”, that would have been fine. That is football,’ Pereira said. ‘In my career, I have spent many years working in different countries, with different cultures. I have plenty of experience, and I know that sometimes football is like that.’

‘But it is fine, I am not the type of person who dwells on the past. I prefer to live in the present, and the present means studying, preparing and getting stronger for the next opportunity. I want to keep the work we did there in my memory. I take with me the affection of the supporters, the people at the club and the players.’

The change has not yet been justified. Forest are second from bottom of the current Premier League table with one win from nine matches, are winless in five and have already been knocked out of the EFL Cup.

Pereira’s job at Forest mirrored his previous Premier League role at Wolverhampton Wanderers, where he took over midway through 2024-25 and secured survival. He stayed on, but was sacked in November last season with Wolves bottom of the table, before they were relegated.

The Portuguese now wants a different path and does not want to take over sides fighting relegation. ‘I am not a firefighter,’ he said.

‘I want to prove my worth by facing and competing with the best managers in the league, and do something special. When you take over a team in the middle of the season, it is because something is not working. That means I have to accept that situation, start with energy and take the right steps to build something solid.’

Pereira says he will look for projects capable of competing for the title and has recently received offers that he might have accepted at another stage of his career.

‘My goal for the future is to compete for titles in the Premier League. If you look at my career before I came to England, you will see that I almost always worked to win titles. I need to take the right steps to reach that level in the Premier League, but that is my goal.’

The last time he took charge of a club among the favourites for domestic honours was Flamengo in 2023, where he failed in the Campeonato Carioca, the Recopa Sudamericana, the Supercopa do Brasil and the Club World Cup, and was sacked within three months.

#1965. Sebastien Pocognoli's Scotland report card has stark message as Euro 2028 qualification warning issued

Just a few days after the last international window concluded with a deeply disappointing 2-1 defeat to Slovenia, Sebastien Pocognoli was back at Hampden.

Nothing too surprising about that, really. After all, he is the Scotland manager. He is, though, based in Belgium and he admitted he needed some time back in his homeland with his family to "refuel" after a challenging and sometimes fraught opening period in charge.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

But he was back in Scotland soon enough to attend a review of his first fixtures in charge, which saw his team take just four Nations League points from a possible 12 against Slovenia (twice), North Macedonia and Switzerland. Although it would have been good to be a fly on the wall on Hampden’s sixth floor as Pocognoli endured this assessment exercise, it’s easy to imagine the gist of the early report card: Must do better.

Pocognoli himself recognises this. “We need to improve,” he said on Monday at the national stadium after naming his second squad. “The first camp was to get to know each other.

“I saw things in training and in the games we produced some very good moments. We created a lot of chances, maybe more than in previous years against those types of opponents. But the next step is to score more goals and clean up the mistakes we made because we conceded goals from nothing. We must try to be consistent in the way we want to play.

“We need to improve but then every country who started with a new coach in September would say the same. Many players in the first camp took it as a new experience with a new style of play and system. That needs a little bit of time but it doesn’t mean we can’t now ask for more and reach the level we want.”

Pocognoli will be handed more time whatever happens in the next two games against North Macedonia and Switzerland. Perhaps the most important date left this year is 6 December, when the draw for Euro 2028 takes place in Belfast. Despite a potentially damaging assumption that Scotland have already qualified as one of the hosts, there’s still work to be done. “We are not qualified,” stressed the Belgian. “We need to qualify. The best way is to qualify from our group.”

He mentioned the need to “stimulate” a winning habit as quickly as possible so that when and if qualification is secured, reaching the knockout stage at a major finals – the final frontier as far as Scotland are concerned – is easier to achieve.

This will go down well with the Hampden top brass. While those first four games will have been robustly scrutinised, it’s only fair Pocognoli’s bosses apply some context to their findings beyond the fact that the heavy defeat against Switzerland was defined by an early red card for Jack Hendry. Pocognoli has barely had time to get his loafers under the desk.

He was also badly served by circumstances. On top of the absent Scott McTominay, recovering following a minor heart procedure, Kieran Tierney and Che Adams were unavailable due to injury. Pocognoli has called up all three for the upcoming games, in the process adding 30 goals to a squad that looked severely short in this department last time out.

Then there was the understandable pomp and ceremony involved in Andy Robertson reaching 100 caps. It meant an early invite back for Steve Clarke, who will have found it excruciating to be perceived as peering over Pocognoli’s shoulder as Scotland were outplayed on their own turf by Slovenia. It was an awkward night, off the pitch as well as on it.

Clarke is actually back in Glasgow next week as a guest of honour at the Street Soccer gala dinner. It will be surprising if he decides to attend Scotland’s home match against North Macedonia two days later. He knows Pocognoli needs space and time to continue trying to put his own mark on the role.

“It was a tough camp,” Pocognoli acknowledged, with reference to those first post-Clarke games. “It was an intense camp. I really liked it. But in terms of intensity…..four games, and I needed to get to know everybody – like 50, 60 new faces. Plus all you (journalists) - 70! It was intense.

“I needed to rest a little bit and refuel after the camp. After one week I was already back here for the review of the camp with the staff and the board and now I am here all this week to prepare for the next camp.”

The Belgian needs to familiarise himself with one more new face: on-loan Rangers player James Penrice, who has been recruited to replace the injured Josh Doig. The squad looks infinitely stronger than last time around thanks chiefly to the inclusion of McTominay and also Adams, still reckoned by many observers – this writer included - to be Scotland’s best striker. The Torino forward's presence takes some of the pressure off Oli McBurnie, who is still struggling to score his first Scotland goal but has struck in his last two appearances for Hull City.

Surprisingly, Aaron Hickey has not started for Brentford since before the last international window. On the upside, Ben Gannon-Doak has seen more action than he is used to in a club context - just as Pocognoli predicted when speaking prior to the last Slovenia game.

The manager was addressing the likely negative impact another period of limited playing time for his club would have on the youngster, who started two of Scotland’s four games in the last window. Pocognoli ventured that, because of Bournemouth’s European commitments, Gannon-Doak will be required to play a more meaningful part as the season progresses, and so it has proved.

The 20-year-old winger was even man of the match in the recent 3-0 Europa League win over AC Milan. Many pointed to this result as underlining football’s new world order. Scotland, meanwhile, have dropped one place to 43 in the international rankings since they last played. They need to start going back up the way without delay.

#1964. Classy hat trick secures victory!

A magnificent second half hat-trick from midfielder Keith Chamberlain meant that a dominant performance was reflected in the scoreline as National Over 60s Football Champions, East Sussex, cruised to a comfortable 6-1 victory against group rivals Kent, in the warm sunshine at Bexhill College last Sunday.

A spectacular, unstoppable volley from the left-hand corner of the penalty box arrowed into the bottom right hand corner earning Chamberlain his first.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

His second, another volley; was calmly placed beyond the reach of the visitor’s keeper from closer range.

Chamberlain finished his hat trick with East Sussex’s sixth and final goal of the game.

This time, his beautifully placed curling effort from 20 yards into the same right-hand corner, left the opposition keeper and defenders watching on motionless.

Although the men in orange and black were dominant by every measure and played attractive football throughout the game, Kent had their moments and only a stunning double save from East Sussex keeper Koosha Movevagh prevented the visitors from scoring in the first half.

Player Manager Alan Osman, had earlier opened the scoring, nodding home a perfectly flighted cross from fellow front man Colin Riggs midway through the first half.

Riggs had an outstanding game. Although he didn’t find himself on the scoresheet; his selfless running and his constant willingness to receive the ball to feet and lay it on for the East Sussex midfielders and wide men were critical in securing the win.

Riggs was inches away from scoring after a superb Osman cross in the first half and he looked certain to score in the second half when a chipped pass from skipper Andy Williams put him through one on one with the Kent keeper, yet what looked like the perfect lob somehow bounced over the vacant goal.

After Osman's opener, Tim Kryezui scored his first competitive goal for the men in orange and black, when he made it 2-0, before half time.

Tim had an excellent first half in his attacking midfield role and the way he calmly rounded the keeper and finished a superb back to front team passing move, characterised his performance on the day.

Nigel Pamplin made his debut replacing Tim in the second half and ‘Pamps’ incisive link up play contributed to many attractive East Sussex attacking moves.

The fifth East Sussex goal came via a neat finish from tricky, pacy winger Kevin Clee, who caused panic and chaos in the visitors’ defence on every occasion he had the ball at his feet.

The East Sussex back four of Dave Pearson. Bob Smith, John O’Meara and Steve Burge were solid in defence and comfortable in possession throughout.

Ed Greenwood and Steve Turner carried real threat from wide midfield positions in the first half, whilst skipper Williams sat in his usual deep midfield anchor role.

Kent scored their consolation with ten minutes to go, shortly after Williams left the field with an injury.

However, Chamberlain’s third moments later ended the scoring and ended any last semblance of fight that the visitors may have had left.

East Sussex’s next game in the competition is a big one, away against main group rivals Farnham and District, on 29th November 2026.

The winners of this fixture are very likely to finish top of the South East qualifying group.

#1963. Viking FK vs Sabah - prediction, team news, lineups

By Matt Law | 02 Nov 2026 18:19, Last updated: 03 Nov 2026 14:17

Viking FK will host Sabah in the Champions League on Wednesday evening, with both sides bidding to put a valuable three points on the board.

Sabah are 25th in the overall Champions League table, picking up three points from three matches, while Viking occupy 33rd, claiming one point from three games.

Viking will enter Wednesday's European fixture off the back of a 3-2 defeat to Bodo/Glimt in the Eliteserien, but they remain top of their domestic table, boasting 59 points from 25 matches.

The Dark Blues are playing in the Champions League for the first time since 1992-93, when they were beaten 1-0 by Barcelona in the first round of the tournament.

The Norwegian outfit, who are jointly-managed by Bjarte Lunde Aarsheim and Morten Jensen, opened their Champions League league stage campaign with a 3-1 defeat to Stuttgart.

Viking then held Bayern Munich to a 3-3 draw, before suffering a 3-1 defeat to Aston Villa in the competition last time out, and one point from three games has left them in 33rd position.

The Dark Blues have scored in each of their last 11 European matches, which is a club record, while each of their last seven home games have produced at least three goals.

Sabah, meanwhile, opened their Champions League league stage campaign with a 4-0 defeat to Manchester United at Old Trafford.

Valdas Dambrauskas' side then recorded a 2-0 victory over Slavia Prague in their second match, before suffering a 2-1 home defeat to Borussia Dortmund last time out, and three points has left them in 25th position in the Champions League table.

The Owls will enter this match off the back of a 3-2 defeat to Turan in the Azerbaijan Premier League, which has left them in second spot in the division behind Neftci Baku.

Sabah had never played in the European Cup before this season, and this is just their fourth European campaign, previously failing to advance past the qualifying rounds of the Conference League or Europa League.

The Azerbaijani outfit will also face Barcelona, Villarreal, Napoli and Arsenal before the end of the Champions League league stage.

Viking will be without the services of Anders Baertelsen (foot), Veton Berisha (thigh), Sondre Bjorshol (knee), Nick D'Agostino (knee) and Martin Ove Roseth (muscular) for Wednesday's European contest.

Peter Christiansen has been in excellent form this season, scoring 15 goals and registering nine assists in 27 appearances, and the 26-year-old will continue in the final third.

There is also set to be a spot in the side for Zlatko Tripic, who has netted seven goals and registered 24 assists in 31 appearances for the hosts in all competitions.

As for Sabah, Veljko Simic (unspecified) needs to be assessed ahead of kickoff, but the visitors are otherwise in strong shape in terms of their squad.

Joy-Lance Mickels has been in impressive form for Sabah this term, netting 11 goals in 20 appearances, and the 32-year-old will continue in the final third of the field.

There should also be a position in the final third of the field for Kaheem Parris, who has come up with three goals in 15 appearances during the current season.

On May 7, 1881, in Edinburgh, Scotland’s Lily St Clare became the first woman in recorded history to score a goal in a game played under football association rules. And what a game it was, with Scotland securing a 3-0 win over England – despite playing in high-heeled boots.

To some, women’s football can seem like a modern phenomenon, but its history dates back almost as far as the men’s game. The fact that we have, in recent years, rediscovered just how popular the sport can be among women and girls is hugely welcome and long overdue.

Now the SNP government has announced its backing for ‘Project 2035’ – a drive to make Scotland a leading nation for women’s football within a decade – providing £250,000 of funding this year. John Swinney spoke of football’s ability to “bring communities together, improve health and wellbeing, and inspire young people to achieve their potential”.

Scotland should be making much greater efforts to become a genuine ‘sporting nation’, but this is, hopefully, a significant step in the right direction. Where pioneers like Lily St Clare led, we must, even belatedly, follow.

#1959. Harry Kane: The 2026 Ballon d’Or winner’s extraordinary England career in numbers

By Oliver Thomas | 02 Nov 2026 18:30, Last updated: 02 Nov 2026 19:12

Harry Kane will go down as one of England’s greatest-ever players, a widespread consensus enhanced by his 2026 Ballon d’Or triumph.

At the age of 33, Kane recently became the first Englishman to lift the prestigious individual prize since Michael Owen in 2001.

Kane has elevated his game to new heights since swapping his legendary spell at Tottenham Hotspur for Bayern Munich, while he continues to play a significant role on international duty with England.

The prolific striker matched Peter Shilton’s record of 125 international caps for the Three Lions during a UEFA Nations League victory against Czechia last month.

This impressive milestone is the latest record in an extraordinary international career spanning 11-and-a-half years, during which Kane has represented his country at eight major tournaments.

With November’s international break just around the corner, Sports Mole provides a statistical breakdown of Kane's international career with England to date.

Kane's journey to drawing level with Shilton at the top of England's all-time appearance charts has been defined by his long-term consistency on the international stage.

Out of his 125 appearances, Kane has been trusted from the first whistle on 111 occasions, amassing nearly 10,000 minutes of international football, and boasting a 66.4% win ratio.

England’s No.9 has represented his country 36 times across major FIFA World Cup and UEFA European Championship tournaments, while he has also made 27 appearances in the UEFA Nations League.

Kane will move above Shilton into outright first position on England’s all-time appearance list when he walks out for his next Three Lions cap (presumable during November’s international break against either Croatia or Spain).

He is also one of only 10 players in history to represent the men’s senior England team at least 100 times.

Men's senior international appearances, all-time

Kane became England’s all-time leading goalscorer in March 2023 when he scored his 54th international goal in a Euro 2024 qualifier against Italy to surpass previous record-holder Wayne Rooney.

Since then, Kane has netted a 37 more goals in 44 appearances for the Three Lions across all competitions, increasing his impressive tally to 91 and closing in on a century of international strikes.

Kane has scored 21 of his goals in major World Cup and Euros tournaments, which includes his six-goal haul at the 2018 World Cup to win the Golden Boot.

Kane has consistently stepped up for England on the biggest stage, ranking third on the all-time list for combined World Cup and European Championship goals (among European players).

The striker has recorded a combined 21 goals in 36 appearances, sitting two behind France star Kylian Mbappe and four adrift of Portugal legend Cristiano Ronaldo at the top of the pile.

While Kane is England’s record goalscorer at World Cups with 14 goals, he is currently tied with fellow Three Lions great Alan Shearer with seven goals at the European Championship.

European players • World Cup & European Championship finals

Kane marked his England debut with a memorable goal scored just 79 seconds after coming on as a substitute in a comfortable 4-0 home victory over Lithuania in Euro 2016 qualifying.

He took just four months to reach 10 goals for England, while he reached half a century of international goals in June 2022 with a late penalty against Germany to rescue a Nations League draw in Munich.

Kane was also on target from the penalty spot to become England’s all-time record goalscorer in March 2023, before scoring his 75th Three Lions goal in a thumping World Cup qualifying win over Latvia just over two years later.

His most recent England goals came in October 2026 when he scored twice in a 3-0 home victory against Czech Republic in the Nations League.

Goal 1: England 4-0 Lithuania | Wembley Stadium | EURO 2016 Qualifying | March 27, 2015

Goal 10: Scotland 2-2 England | Hampden Park | 2018 FIFA World Cup Qualifying | June 10, 2017

Goal 25: England 4-0 Bulgaria | Wembley Stadium | EURO 2020 Qualifying | September 7, 2019

Goal 50: Germany 1-1 England | Allianz Arena | UEFA Nations League | June 7, 2022

Goal 54: Italy 1-2 England | Stadio Diego Armando Maradona | EURO 2024 Qualifying | March 23, 2023

Goal 75: Latvia 0-5 England | Daugava Stadium | 2026 FIFA World Cup Qualifying | October 14, 2025

Goals 90 & 91: England 3-0 Czechia | Wembley Stadium | UEFA Nations League | October 6, 2026

Across his 11-year international career, Kane has scored against 41 different nations, with Albania proving to be his favourite opponent having netted seven times against them in just four games.

Kane has also scored five goals against Croatia, Czechia and San Marino and four times against Germany, Bulgaria, Malta, Montenegro and Panama.

Meanwhile, Kane has registered four assists in just two matches against Bulgaria - more than a fifth of his total assists for England.

While Kane is widely celebrated for his lethal finishing, he has evolved into one of the world’s elite playmakers for club and country, often seen dropping into deeper positions to link up with his teammates.

Since data logs began tracking assists in late 1979, Kane sits joint-second on the all-time playmaking charts for England, level with Liverpool legend Steven Gerrard and only behind Three Lions icon David Beckham at the top.
