#1958. Man United boss Michael Carrick appears to ignore Lisandro Martinez after defender sent off for deliberately elbowing Wesley Fofana

Published: 10:04 EDT, 31 October 2026 | Updated: 10:21 EDT, 31 October 2026

Michael Carrick could not even look at Lisandro Martinez after the Manchester United defender's moment of madness saw him sent off away at Chelsea.

Martinez, not looking at the ball as a corner was whipped in, went in with his elbow on Wesley Fofana's throat, only a minute or so after picking up a yellow card for pulling back Morgan Rogers.

A VAR review was recommended and Martinez, who was in the headlines earlier this month for calling out the United hierarchy for letting Carrick and the players down, was shown a second yellow card and given his marching orders.

It was a ridiculous decision by Martinez to make the challenge he did on Fofana and Carrick elected not to even acknowledge his centre back as he trudged down the tunnel.

Cole Palmer scored the resulting penalty, given away by Martinez, to make it 2-0.

Lisandro Martinez (left) got ignored by boss Michael Carrick (right) after his sending off

Martinez made a ridiculous decision to lead with his elbow, fouling Wesley Fofana in the box

Director of football Jason Wilcox, explicitly called out by Martinez after a 2-0 defeat in the Champions League to Atletico Madrid, watched on alongside CEO Omar Berrada as Martinez's dire decision making took the game away from Carrick's side, who had been the better team in the first half.

'You can't keep changing, changing, changing the manager,' Martínez said in his Madrid rant. 'What about other areas? [looks up] I can't say more.

'It is easy to say the coach, easy to say the players but also we have to see other areas [points up].

'He [Carrick] does his best. Every season is different. You can't stay with what you did last season.

'The teams knows how you play, they know every detail, if you don't change next season is a big problem.

'Last season we did everything, we created the base to create an amazing team.

'It is annoying, disappointing coming here and I am not seeing my team trying to get an amazing result here.'

But he cost his team dearly away at Chelsea, not just with his defending for the opening goal by Rogers, where Martinez and centre back partner Harry Maguire looked incredibly slow, but also for the reckless foul on Fofana that saw Chelsea awarded a result-sealing penalty.

Martinez had a lot to say in Madrid but he was the key person to blame at Stamford Bridge

Martinez was fined for his comments made in Madrid and he sat down for a pow-wow with the hierarchy to thrash out any differences and to get back on the same page.

Yet, at a time when results on the pitch needed to see huge improvement, not least after the Stretford End booed the players off after the 3-0 defeat to Bournemouth last weekend, Martinez let his team-mates down on a day where they looked the better side for 45 minutes.

The expectation is that Martinez will leave at the end of the season and it could even be as early as January with no guarantee that United trigger the additional year option they hold on a contract that expires at the end of the season.

#1956. Little Common’s super six fell Forest and delight Eldridge

After a demanding run of away fixtures, the Commoners made a welcome return to the Rec for only their second Saturday home fixture of the season and marked the occasion with an impressive attacking display.

It was the hosts who came closest to breaking the deadlock in the early exchanges when Lewis Unwin's superb free-kick crashed against the crossbar and bounced to safety.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

However, Common did not have to wait long to make the breakthrough. In the 19th minute, Sam Ellis threaded a perfectly weighted pass through to Ollie MacDonald, who showed great composure to lift the ball over the advancing keeper.

The visitors thought they had drawn level minutes later, but their celebrations were cut short by the an offside flag.

Common doubled their advantage ten minutes before the interval when another dangerous delivery from Unwin caused problems for the Forest Row defence. His free-kick was met by Harvey Mapstone, who made no mistake from close range to give the hosts a commanding 2-0 lead at the break.

The visitors gave themselves a lifeline six minutes into the second half when a well-struck effort was drilled into the bottom corner to halve the deficit.

For a brief spell, the contest looked finely balanced, but Common regained control and produced a devastating attacking display to put the result beyond doubt.

Ellis was next to threaten, bringing a smart save from the goalkeeper, before the Common forward capitalised on a defensive mistake. Showing great anticipation, Ellis beat the goalkeeper to the loose ball before calmly rolling his effort into the unguarded net.

Three became four following some excellent attacking play down the right flank. Sam Atkin saw his initial effort saved by the Forest Row goalkeeper, but Sonny Tyrell was perfectly placed to turn home the rebound and extend Common's advantage.

Ollie Hull added a fifth when he cut inside the area and unleashed an effort which took a deflection before nestling in the back of the net, leaving the visiting goalkeeper helpless.

The scoring was completed in the 80th minute when MacDonald tried his luck from distance. The goalkeeper could only parry his effort, and Fin Jack was quickest to react, tapping home from close range to make it six.

Jack almost added a seventh but his goalbound effort was kept out by the Forest Row goalkeeper.

Little Common manager Russell Eldridge was delighted with his side’s performance and the return to winning ways.

“It was a much-needed three points for us, and I was really pleased with the way the lads went about their business. We’ve had a difficult run of fixtures, particularly away from home, so it was important that we got back to winning ways,” he said.

“I thought we played some really good football, created plenty of chances and, most importantly, were clinical in front of goal. It was disappointing to concede early in the second half, but I was pleased with the response. We didn't let our heads drop, and once we got the third goal, we really took control of the game.

“It was particularly pleasing to have six different goalscorers, and there were some excellent individual performances, but ultimately it was a good team display.

“We know one result doesn't change everything, and we certainly won't be getting carried away. Hopefully, this will give the lads a bit of confidence, and the challenge now is to build on it. We've got another home game against Roffey this weekend, and we need to make sure we approach that with the same attitude and determination.”

#1955. Man United vs. Roma: Michael Carrick addresses fitness fears surrounding "fantastic" Leny Yoro

By Matt Law | 02 Nov 2026 18:43, Last updated: 02 Nov 2026 18:44

Manchester United head coach Michael Carrick has said that Leny Yoro will be available for Tuesday's Champions League clash against Roma.

Yoro sparked fitness concerns when he was seen with strapping on his knee during Man United's training session on Monday.

Carrick has revealed that the France international is suffering with a slight tendon issue, but it will not force him to miss the European game against Roma.

“Leny just had a bit of a tendon really, so it's one of them that kind of comes and goes, but he's been managing it and he's been fine. I think he's been fantastic, to be honest, one of our best players, and he has been since he came back on the first day of pre-season," Carrick told reporters during Monday's press conference.

"He's impressed us all a lot, so I've been delighted with Leny and his performances and he’s got to keep doing the right thing. He's on a really good pathway."

Carrick was also asked for an update on both Marcus Rashford and Luke Shaw.

Rashford has missed Man United's last three matches due to a hip problem, while an unspecified issue has kept Shaw out since October 10.

Carrick has said that Rashford's fitness is being managed "day by day", while Shaw is not expected back in training until at least the start of next week.

"On Marcus and Luke, Luke definitely won't be around this week and fit at that point. Marcus we’ll just have to see, day by day, how he keeps improving," said the head coach.

Patrick Dorgu has returned to training, having recovered from a hamstring injury, but the Denmark international will not be involved against Roma.

Meanwhile, Benjamin Sesko remains unavailable for selection due to a shin injury, with the striker potentially missing until the start of 2027.

Man United have two more matches before the November international break, following the Roma clash with a Premier League fixture against Aston Villa.

Sarcevic's booking count at league level will stand at four when City return to league action.

The Bantams' scheduled League One trip to Leicester City – scheduled for Saturday, November 14 – has been postponed due to international call-ups for the home side.

It means that City's next league game will be against Doncaster Rovers on November 21 – the second instalment of a triple header of Yorkshire derbies at league level at Valley Parade.

After facing Rovers, Michael Duff’s side will welcome his former club Barnsley on Tuesday, November 24.

Duff admits that he and his players are challenged to get back onside with supporters following a painful derby day against Town, but he is also quick to point out that there were 'mitigating circumstances' to factor into the 3-0 reverse.

"I don't want to sound like I'm defending the players," Duff commented.

"We've been beaten 3-0 by our local rivals. So we know that. We know the supporters went home angry.

"But I think there are mitigating circumstances involved. So it's not us accepting it. Hopefully, they watched the same first half as what the staff did.

"It was a good game in the first half. It was a proper local derby. And then it's just circumstances that killed it.

"There are individual errors. But there are certain things that we shouldn't be doing - like taking a short corner in the first place.

"So they're things that we need to learn from as well.

"The killer is against your local rivals. That's the bit that hurts."

As it stands, the Leicester postponement means that City are set for a run of six successive fixtures at BD8, which started with last weekend’s EFL Cup victory over Peterborough United – with the derby with Town following on.

The Bantams host Marine in the cup on Saturday and host York City in an EFL Trophy group game next Tuesday – ahead of the meetings with Rovers and the Reds.

Bradford’s next scheduled away fixture will be at Wycombe Wanderers on November 28.

#1947. Barcelona head coach Hansi Flick discusses Alejandro Balde future amid exit reports

By Matt Law | 02 Nov 2026 19:07, Last updated: 02 Nov 2026 19:08

Barcelona head coach Hansi Flick has suggested that Alejandro Balde still has a future at Camp Nou despite his struggles during the 2026-27 campaign.

Flick said ahead of Barcelona's clash with Alaves on Saturday that Balde currently does not have "the confidence he needs to play".

“Balde doesn’t have the confidence he needs to play, the conviction to attack and press high. The full-backs are very important for us, in our style of play. He needs confidence to reach his best level," Flick told reporters.

Injuries for Xavi Espart, Jules Kounde, Andreas Christensen and Eric Garcia had seemingly opened the door for Balde to start against Alaves.

However, Joao Cancelo started at left-back, with Brian Farinas at right-back, while Frenkie de Jong featured in the middle of the defence.

Balde was instead used off the bench, playing the final 28 minutes of the league fixture.

The Spain international has only played 116 minutes of action for Barcelona this season, and there is currently a host of speculation surrounding his future.

Manchester United are in the market for a left-back and could reignite their interest in the 23-year-old when the winter window opens for business.

Balde could potentially start Barcelona's Champions League fixture against Aston Villa on Tuesday, but it is more likely that he will again feature on the bench.

Flick has suggested that Balde is still in his plans moving forward, with the German determined to "help" the defender "regain his confidence".

“What’s happening to him is normal; when you don’t play often, you lack confidence. I see him training well, but we have to decide what’s best for the team, and Joao Cancelo is in great form,” Flick told reporters during his press conference.

“When I say he lacks confidence, I know it can affect him, and I spoke to him after the last press conference. I respect him a lot; he’s young, but he’s a great person and a very hard worker. I’ll help him regain his confidence.”

Balde has made 172 appearances for Barcelona in all competitions since breaking into their first team, scoring three goals and registering 21 assists.

#1946. Wrexham v Middlesbrough FC: Kim Hellberg on Will Lankshear England talk and Riley McGree praise

That was back on August 7 in the EFL's curtain raiser to the season, when the Red Dragons visited the Riverside Stadium for a first-round Carabao Cup fixture.

Just after the hour mark, Lankshear settled the issue on his debut with a technically exquisite hooked volley. A televised audience and not just those present on Teesside watched on in admiration.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

'Middlesbrough get their first glimpse of a striker who could be a hero in waiting' were the prescient words by the Sky Sports commentator.

Just under three months on, the 21-year-old remains the talk of the Championship in many respects ahead of Boro's first league meeting with Wrexham in 2026-27.

Lankshear has scored 15 times in 16 appearances for Boro in league and cup. The former Tottenham Hotspur frontman, who had a spell earlier in his career at Sheffield United, has scored in his last five successive fixtures since the last international break - netting on seven occasions.

His 13 Championship goals have arrived in 13 league appearances, the best record for any Boro player at the start of a season since the legendary George Camsell in 1926.

Speak to the forward, who arrived for an initial £10m in the summer—and he will be quick to remind people that his tally so far this term is 16 and not 15. Lankshear also scored for England under-21s in their September fixture against Kazakhstan.

His feats have even led to some talk about a possible maiden senior call-up. That is surely one for the future as opposed to the present, but the fact that it is being talked about is significant.

Sensibly, Boro chief Kim Hellberg is circumspect regarding such conjecture and rightly so.

Last season, there was plenty of gushing talk about the prowess of the player wearing the number seven shirt currently worn by Lankshear in Hayden Hackney. His season would ultimately end in tears of frustration.

Asked about the prospect of a full call-up, Hellberg, very much wearing his manager’s hat - his high-fliers are seeking to extend their unbeaten league sequence to 12 games this evening - said: "No, it would be better if he was playing with us and training with us, to be very frank. I'm going to be honest…

"So, that's my answer. Then, of course, for him, everyone wants to play for the country and everyone is happy with that.

"We take a lot of pride in our football club if they are involved in the under-21s or the senior team or whatever it is for their country, and we know that's a big thing for the players and they work very hard every day to be there.

"I think that's also one thing that's been seen, that we have more call-ups this year than last year, because we are in a good position and we have a lot of good players. We will see and that's the same thing with all the players."

One player who is likely to be on international duty next month is key Australian midfielder Riley McGree.

It had been expected that the creative force would also be on Socceroos business at the Asian Cup, which was scheduled to take place in Saudi Arabia in January and early February. But it has been postponed because of a series of terrorist attacks on the host country and has been rescheduled for December 2027.

Amid a key period, McGree's availability would be welcome from a Boro perspective. The 28-year-old has already started over half of the league games that he managed in 2025-26.

On McGree, who has started 10 of Boro's 13 league games thus far, Hellberg commented: "I think Riley is an absolutely perfect player for us in how he plays.

"He has so much quality in finding spaces to connect with other players and he's involved in a lot of good things. Often when you watch the game after, you see so many good movements that are off the ball, where he opens up space for people and understands the game in a brilliant way.

"I'm very happy with the amount of game time he has been having on a high level. You still need to manage and balance things, but that goes for everyone.

"But I think he's taken big steps to play even more and it's a case of of just keep going, improving and working hard with that. Everyone wants him on the pitch as much as possible."

McGree and Boro are in a good place. That extends to off the pitch with head of football Kieran Scott and recruitment supremo Chris Jones signing new long-term deals this week. Paul Watson has arrived from Brentford as chief technical officer.

Hellberg added: "They have done a brilliant job. We talked about signing players and getting them here. The recruitment, how we work with players and all those things is a key thing."

#1945. Chelsea 2-0 Manchester United PLAYER RATINGS: Who was 'sloppy' in possession? Which £70m star 'came up short'? And who is 'coming of age'?

By KIERAN GILL, MAIL SPORT REPORTER and CHRIS WHEELER, NORTHERN SPORTS WRITER

Published: 10:56 EDT, 31 October 2026 | Updated: 10:57 EDT, 31 October 2026

Things continue to go from bad to worse for Michael Carrick as his prospects of holding on to his position as Manchester United manager took another dent following this 2-0 defeat at Chelsea.

United were the better team for 45 minutes but wasted their opportunities and were made to pay for it in the second half when Morgan Rogers fired Chelsea ahead.

From there, United capitulated, not helped by the ridiculous decision-making of Lisandro Martinez, who launched an elbow at Wesley Fofana on a corner, conceding a penalty and picking up a red card.

Cole Palmer scored that penalty and United never looked capable of getting back into the game as fans turned on the Argentine defender.

For Chelsea, this was the win they craved following a week in which they lost to Tottenham Hotspur in the Premier League and Liverpool on penalties in the Carabao Cup.

Daily Mail Sport's KIERAN GILL and CHRIS WHEELER were in position at Stamford Bridge to run the rule over both sides...

Morgan Rogers (left) and Cole Palmer (right) both scored to pile misery on Manchester United

Michael Carrick had his head in his hands as his side unravelled before going down to 10 men

Earned his first Premier League clean sheet as a starter. Denied Amad twice, including after one of Wesley Fofana's errors. Saved by the offside flag when Matheus Cunha scored at a corner, and tipped Bryan Mbeumo's rocket on to the crossbar.

Much-needed sliding challenge to stop Cunha from tapping in and a block to deny Bruno Fernandes amid other tidying up. The Cobham graduate was Chelsea's best defender here. He's coming of age.

Chelsea won, but we cannot pretend Fofana did not endure a shocker of a first half. Manchester United should have scored from at least one of his mistakes. But Fofana at least won his team a penalty when Martinez clattered into him at a corner.

Needed to attack crosses as United grew into the game in the build-up to half-time. A much easier – or enjoyable even – afternoon when the visitors dropped down to 10 men.

Had to fly forward down the left wing so that Morgan Rogers could drift inside. Got some mistakes out of his system in what was his first competitive start. A much more comfortable second half.

Marco Palestra struggled early on but managed to get mistakes out of his game as he settled

Replaced the unwell Jordan Henderson. Created Chelsea's opening goal as he brilliantly won the ball in midfield and gave it to Morgan Rogers. Regularly read passes before they happened. My star performer here overall. Back-to-back full 90s for him now.

Rarely is Caicedo upstaged by another midfielder, but even he knew his partner here was performing at an even higher level than him. A second-half showing full of control from Chelsea.

Chelsea fans demanded him. Xabi Alonso delivered him. Had two goals disallowed for offside on his first Premier League start of the season. Even hugged Alonso after he thought he had made it 3-0. Only for VAR to decide his shoulder had strayed offside. Such a positive performance.

Had hardly been in the game in an attacking sense when Chelsea were awarded a penalty, which he scored for 2-0. Would have tapped in another were it not for good defending from Harry Maguire.

Could not believe his luck as United's defence parted like the Red Sea to allow him through. He kept running and running and then chipped Lammens for 1-0. A lovely goal.

Rogers was a real livewire and couldn't believe United's defending as he went clear to score

Shot parried by Senne Lammens led to Estevao's offside tap-in. Had a good chance before half-time after winning the ball from Maguire but the angle was too tight for him to find the finish. Tried his best as a false nine.

The first half was poor, but he stood by his selection at the break, and Chelsea wound up winning comfortably. Good on him for finally using Estevao.

Eased back from injury by coming on with Chelsea leading 2-0.

Had no chance with Rogers' opener and Palmer's penalty. Got lucky when Caicedo hit the post in the first half, but did his best to keep United in the game and made a superb late save from Estevao.

Did well against Rogers in the first half but less so in the second as Chelsea's front line began to run United ragged. He wasn't alone in that respect.

Leny Yoro (right) started well and looked a bright spot but he faded as the game got away

Gave Rogers the freedom of Stamford Bridge to score the first goal. He had been solid up until then, apart from a slip that almost let in Neto, and got forward well at set-pieces.

Let his team down with a stupid challenge on Fofana at a corner shortly after being booked. Red card and penalty killed United's chances. A player of his experience should know better.

Continues to fill in at left-back and it's no easy task, especially when you are up against a winger like Estevao. Another player who did well up to half-time and suffered after that.

Crucially lost out in the 50-50 that led to Chelsea's opener. United paid £70m for Baleba to make a difference in those moments and he came up short. Substituted shortly afterwards.

United's other new defensive midfielder showed why he was never a first-choice at Chelsea. Powerless to stop the game turning in his old team's favour when they came on strong after the interval.

Andrey Santos (left) was powerless to stop Chelsea taking control of Saturday's early kick-off

How different might this game and result been if Amad had taken his chances? Could have had a hat-trick in the first half alone. By far United's liveliest player but finishing let him down.

The captain was back in the team after being dropped, and back in the No 10 role. Sadly, still not back to his best though. Too sloppy in possession and missed a great chance in the first half.

Another player recalled by Carrick. A handful on the left and when he alternated with Fernandes at No 10. Wanted to get on the ball and had a goal ruled out for a marginal offside, but faded after half-time.

Inches away from giving United a lifeline when he hit the underside of the bar in added time. Had more impact in the first half when he produced arguably the pass of the match to set up Fernandes.

These were the marginal games Carrick was winning last season. It was an improved performance from United but missed chances cost Carrick the game and may soon cost him his job.

#1944. Sheffield Wednesday manager Dave Challinor clear what his style challenge entails

When it came to his new players, the Chester-born manager's first priority was clarity – a word that regularly cropped up in his first press conference. When it comes to the supporters, it is about delivering attractive football – and he is clear what that means to him.

As Henrik Pedersen discovered to his cost, winning alone is not enough at League One Wednesday.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

The Dane only needed two defeats on the back of a nine-match unbeaten run to be shown the door at Hillsborough. But it was about more than that – his football just was not doing it for the supporters.

So Challinor knows he has to play with panache. Fortunately, he does not think he will have to change much to produce it with the squad he has been furnished with.

The problem is, one man's entertainment is another man's boring football. Some love pure passing, others are bored by tippy-tappy – "Gerri’ forward" is not an unusual thing to hear on a Yorkshire terrace.

"If you look at the last few years I would suggest some of the teams that have played the most attractive football have got promoted in Birmingham and Cardiff," argues a manager who led Stockport County before resigning when the Hatters lost the League One play-off final to Bolton Wanderers in May.

"Attractive football is different for everybody.

"How Brighton go about it in the Premier League is very different to how Arsenal go about it.

"The Arsenal fans will tell you that the football they play is really attractive because they won the Premier League last year.

"What this football club needs and wants is different from 20 miles away maybe."

It begged the question: what is his definition of attractive football?

"I want us to be possession-based but purposeful in that," he says. "I want us to play forward and be aggressive with and without the ball and play with good ball speed.

"I want to make the team we play against defend from their box."

It feels like everyone is starting from a position of clarity.

Challinor worked with sporting director Simon Wilson for five years at Stockport, and although he was careful to take a while choosing Pedersen's replacement, and to remove himself from certain discussions so there we no accusations of bias, it was clear he wanted what the 51-year-old provides.

And Challinor knows what he is walking into.

"Carlton Palmer was the manager at Stockport when I went there," he says. "I grew up as a Liverpool fan and go back to the early 90s when Sheffield Wednesday as a football club were in the Premier League and FA Cup finals. The history is there.

"You don't need to be told if you're involved in football around what Sheffield Wednesday is. I shared a car with Brian Barry Murphy for six years at Bury.

"I know Steve Haslam really well. I played with Steve at Bury and he played for me at Fylde.

"But I think everyone involved in football understands the magnitude and size of this football club."

He took time to reflect whilst out of work.

"My wife works from home and didn't like me in the house very often," he smiles. "When you come out, there's probably only so much you can do.

"You go on a few holidays, you go to other clubs. I've made some brilliant trips over the summer to go and see some brilliant people.

"I went up to Celtic and spoke to Martin O'Neill, who was amazing. I watched them training and Martin said I wouldn't learn anything from that.

"But just to watch him and how he works as he's someone I've got a massive amount of respect for was great.

"H's don a not too dissimilar journey to him in terms of starting in non-league so you take an awful lot from those things."

He comes promising evolution, not revolution.

"I just spoke to the players at the first meeting," says Challinor. "The big thing for me will be clarity around what our structure will be, roles and responsibilities, standards, behaviours that we need to live every day.

"They'll get honesty, I expect them to be honest with us.

"I won't ask them to do something that I can't do, except maybe run around on a football pitch now.

"It'll be a steady process, but I think you'll see some things that are different.

"Structurally, there'll be some little bits, clarity and simplicity around what we want to do in certain areas of the pitch.

"We need to get some excitement into especially this place. That comes from being positive, playing forward, being purposeful with our possession, making the other team defend for long periods, and getting the supporters off their seats."

#1943. Barcelona, Lille and Brighton and Hove Albion scout Estoril teenager Jordan Arnolin

By Alexis Pereira | 02 Nov 2026 19:19, Last updated: 02 Nov 2026 19:19

Barcelona are reportedly taking a close interest in Jordan Arnolin, but the Estoril centre-back is also attracting attention in France and the Premier League.

Barcelona are not only looking to sign established players to strengthen their defence. The Catalan club, leader in LaLiga, are also scouting young European talents, and according to Portuguese newspaper Record, they sent a representative to the Estadio do Dragao on Saturday to watch 18-year-old Arnolin.

The interest comes as Barcelona have spent several months trying to strengthen their back line. The sporting department is working on several profiles, with the aim of finding a centre-back who can give Hansi Flick more guarantees.

The name of Inter Milan stalwart Alessandro Bastoni has been mentioned insistently in recent months, most recently by Sky Sports. The Italy international would be an especially expensive operation, however, and Inter have no reason to make his departure easy. Against that backdrop, a young player with high potential is another route for the Barcelona hierarchy, and Arnolin fits that logic.

Barcelona will have to contend with two other suitors. According to Record, Lille and Brighton and Hove Albion also sent representatives to the Dragao to monitor the young Portuguese.

For Lille, the move would fit a well-established recruitment policy of backing high-potential players who can take a step up and increase in value. The northern French club have regularly used that model to bring in players who are not yet well known to the wider public. Brighton are a far stronger financial rival, with greater resources than Lille and their own reputation for finding talent. Their ability to attract young players and offer them exposure in the Premier League is another argument in their favour.

Lille face a stiff challenge. Barcelona have a sporting and media pull that is unmatched, and even though Arnolin would probably not walk straight into Flick’s starting line-up, joining the Catalan club would be hard for an 18-year-old to turn down.

Lille do have one strong argument in playing time. With heavy competition in the Barcelona squad, particularly at centre-back, the young Portuguese could have to wait for first-team chances, while a gradual path to the Lille first team looks easier to envisage.

The financial side remains a factor, too. Brighton have more room for manoeuvre, and Barcelona keep considerable economic strength and international appeal, despite their well-known budget constraints. Lille will probably have to rely on their sporting project and their ability to support the defender’s progress.

Another element could complicate negotiations. Arnolin has just signed his first professional contract with Estoril, running until June 2029, so the club are under no pressure to sell. Lille have a card to play, but they will need to be convincing to beat two very serious competitors.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The Rossoneri entered last night’s game with a run of seven unbeaten and they finished the night with eight unbeaten and a fourth consecutive win. It’s a first in itself for more than 50 years, which is telling.

It’s a result which brought Gerry Cardinale to tears and it’s clear that something has really clicked at San Siro, as the player ratings showed.

Speaking at a press conference after the game, as relayed by MilanNews, the Inter coach spoke about several things, including his unfavourable record in the Derby della Madonnina.

“Compared to last year, there’s something to note about our approach to matches: the superficiality and casualness with which we handle certain situations, where we lack a bit of grit, a bit of determination, a bit of danger perception. But we need to rediscover them.

“We need to be aware that right now, despite a few more points than last year, we’ve lost something that absolutely needs to be rediscovered.”

“I couldn’t, because the forwards have had some problems in the last few days. Bonny only made himself available on the last day after two days with a fever of 39°C and severe nausea and vomiting, so we were forced to find a solution, to make a virtue of necessity, changing the system a bit.

“We knew that, in this type of match, it would be the right thing to have pace on the wings with Spence and Carlos and attack the line a bit more, as well as looking for depth in space with Diouf operating under the striker, looking for both him and Sucic between the lines.

“Unfortunately, sometimes things don’t work out, but, I repeat, we were forced to change.”

“It’s too easy to talk now that Lautaro is injured and the other two forwards aren’t feeling well. These things happen, fortunately not often. We’ll make some assessments, but we’re still happy with our four forwards, in addition to what Lavelli gives us, what Mosconi gives us, and whoever we bring in from the Under 23s.

“But, I repeat, it’s too easy to bring these things up at a time when two forwards aren’t at their best and the third is injured.”

Is there something mental that comes into play in the derby?

“There’s always something mental, I think, and history teaches us this, when you get to play another season after winning.

“So, let’s try not to throw everything away and try to rediscover some determination, some humility in doing certain things, starting with myself, because I’m primarily responsible for everything we do.

“We shouldn’t throw everything away because we’ve reached the tenth matchday and this is the first game we’ve lost. We’ve got 25 points, and last year we’d got fewer, but we’ve always been able to react, we’ve always kept our feet on the ground and our heads down to build a strong season.

“That’s what we’d like to do again this year, because we have this desire and this ambition to have another strong season; we just need to find the way to build it again.”

“My natural progression would have been to try and get a Championship opportunity,” he admitted.

“That made the number of clubs I am appealing to was probably pretty small. The next opportunity either needed to give me that chance, or be one I could grow with.

“I certainly couldn't have picked a bigger one in terms of this club and the amount of growth it's got in it.

“I won't say this isn't a League One club – on the football pitch it is – and it's our job to try and push it forward but everyone around football is saying off the field this is a Championship club.

“It's to do with history, fanbase, the size of the stadium and all those things. We have to make it a huge advantage for us.

“But on the pitch, that's where we are. We have to understand that and put things in place that allow us to move forward and be that club in the long term.”

Challinor's predecessor Henrik Pedrsen was sacked in no small part because his football did not excite supporters, and Challinor says tapping into them is essential.

“It's the one factor where we can definitely say we have an advantage,” he said. “There's more supporters been coming in here than any other ground in League One and most of the Championship.”

Challinor's former Tranmere Rovers team-mate Clint Hill joins alongside Antony Sweeney as assistants, with further coaching appointments and redefined roles for existing coaches promised.

#1940. Alan Shearer makes Arsenal claim after win over Liverpool

Alan Shearer hailed Arsenal’s defence as the ‘best in world football’ after a hard-fought win over Liverpool.

The reigning champions moved to the top of the Premier League with a 1-0 victory at Anfield on Sunday afternoon.

Kai Havertz gave Arsenal the lead on 16 minutes and that proved to be enough to bag all three points despite some intense Liverpool pressure.

While Liverpool mounted attack after attack, they mustered just one shot on target against an Arsenal side who have conceded just 10 goals in 15 games this season.

Sign up to our daily football newsletter, pick your team and get the latest news sent directly to your inbox every morning.

‘That is how you work as a team,’ Shearer told Premier League Productions after Arsenal’s first win at Anfield in 14 years. ‘That is how you defend as a team.

‘Every single one of them to a man were outstanding. When they were under the cosh in the second half, you could see how much they wanted to defend and what it means to them to keep a clean sheet.

‘I don’t think there is a better team in world football that defend quite like Arsenal defend. Every player does their bit, it isn’t just the back four.

‘It was brilliant sitting behind the Arsenal bench today and seeing what it means to them. The team ethic and team work and belief Arteta has in them.

‘He didn’t get flustered at all even when Arsenal had to suffer. He trusts his players.’

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

Former Arsenal winger Theo Walcott also heaped praise on the Gunners’ defence, insisting that solidity will make Mikel Arteta’s side ‘difficult to stop this year’.

‘Arsenal frustrated them,’ Walcott said. ‘To limit Liverpool to no shots on target shows the level of this team. They just love defending, don’t they?

‘I felt like they don’t mind that pressure. These are champions who can do a bit of everything. They are going to be difficult to stop this year.

‘I look at Arsenal’s forward players and at no point do they get frustrated working for the team. That is different to many years ago.

‘I remember the Arsenal teams I played in and we always wanted to attack. Now they are happy to work for the team.

While Arsenal underlined their status as Premier League title favourites at Anfield, Liverpool suffered a humbling defeat after a promising run under Andoni Iraola.

Liverpool hero Steve McManaman said: ‘They were the better team today, but they’ve walked off losing with just one shot on target.

#1939. Ezri Konsa, the best Arsenal signing of last window, gives Mikel Arteta a welcome selection headache

By Alexis Pereira | 02 Nov 2026 19:29

Arsenal’s outstanding defensive display in the 1-0 win over Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday ended a 14-year wait for a Premier League victory at their rival’s ground. The result was built on superb organisation and discipline in front of David Raya’s goal, and one of the standout names was Ezri Konsa.

The England defender produced a top-level performance to secure the clean sheet. According to Opta, he won eight of nine duels, made eight clearances, five tackles, five recoveries and two blocks, and won two fouls.

For the first time in the Premier League era, Liverpool did not register a single shot on target in a game at Anfield, a mark that highlights the outstanding collective defending and the performance of the centre-back pairing. Konsa’s understanding with Gabriel Magalhaes makes it look as though the two have played together for many seasons.

So far, Konsa has maintained the high level he showed at his former club, Aston Villa. He has made only 13 appearances for the Gunners this season, yet he already merits the label of a successful signing. His assured displays have almost made supporters forget who held the position before his arrival.

The 29-year-old joined Arsenal in August for £51m to replace William Saliba, who suffered a serious back injury that forced him off in the World Cup semi-final between France and Spain.

Saliba, who is not expected to return until the end of this month, had been one of Arsenal’s defensive foundations in recent seasons, and the club decided to bring in an outside name, even though Christian Mosquera, Piero Hincapie, Riccardo Calafiori and Jurrien Timber could all have played there.

From here, boss Mikel Arteta will have the kind of selection headache every manager dreams of. Konsa and Saliba will compete at a high level to play alongside Gabriel Magalhaes, and Arsenal can only benefit.

The season is long and the Gunners will compete for every trophy. Having elite players both on the pitch and on the bench is essential to withstand the physical strain over the months ahead.

In recent seasons, Arsenal have made good signings, especially in defence, such as Timber, Calafiori and Hincapie. Konsa shares a key characteristic with those names. His versatility, as he can also play at right-back, gives Arteta a range of options very few European clubs can match, and over a long season that could prove decisive.

#1937. Dwight Yorke names the manager Manchester United must appoint to replace Michael Carrick

Manchester United hero Dwight Yorke has told the Red Devils to pay whatever is necessary to bring in Unai Emery as manager.

Michael Carrick remains in charge at Old Trafford, but after nine games without a win his grip on the job looks very flimsy.

United have two games before the next international break, hosting Roma in the Champions League on Tuesday and then Emery’s Aston Villa in the Premier League on Sunday.

If they win neither of those contests then it seems extremely difficult to imagine Carrick will still be in charge when the players return from international duty.

Sign up to our daily football newsletter, pick your team and get the latest news sent directly to your inbox every morning.

Yorke, who played for Villa from 1989-98 before moving to Manchester United, says Emery is the only man for the job and the Red Devils should have done whatever they could to get him before they hired Ruben Amorim in 2024 and should do the same now.

‘I have said this all along, and it baffles me when people are now jumping on the bandwagon,’ Yorke said on talkSPORT.

‘I said this two-and-a-half years ago. Unai Emery was the man to go and get way before Amorim has come into the equation.

‘And just like how, you go and spend £70million on players, I think Unai Emery, you can go and spend that money, I am not saying £70m, but pay whatever Villa has asked and get him. Give him the authority to come in.

‘I have said that way before Amorim has come in. I got a backlash from the Villa fans, and to this day, I still believe that he is the best manager in the business, certainly to get Man Utd to some type of credibility and sustainability at the same time as well.’

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

Yorke recognises that the Manchester United players are massively under-performing, but feels that Carrick has to take some of the blame for that as he appears unable to turn the tide.

‘When things are good, which it was really good under Carrick when he first took over, football is easy,’ said the former striker.

‘The difference in management is when things are not so good. As a player when things are not so good, have you got the character to bounce back?

‘This is where we have seen Carrick is being let down. You need a reaction from your players. Whether the players are on board with you, are they going to fight for you? I’ve not seen that.

‘We’ve seen Carrick in his element when things are really good. When things have not gone so well the manager’s job is trying to motivate the players, get them back to playing, showing some character, play with conviction, play with passion.

‘Even if you lose a football match, that’s fine. But if you lose football matches the way United have been losing football matches, I’m afraid that it does not look good.

‘You look at Tottenham, for instance, they were at the bottom and the manager somehow finds a way. You’ve got to find a way from your players and I’m not seeing that with Carrick.

‘This is the time as a manager when you’ve got to earn your coin and he’s not really doing that at the moment.’

#1936. Huddersfield Town 1 Luton Town 1: Lack of clinical edge at both ends costly for Terriers

But a few seconds of defensive doziness as errors piled on top of one another was all it took to end their four-match winning streak.

It was harsh on the Terriers, but they were not the only team on the pitch who are hard to beat at the moment.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

It may not be the elite level Hatters manager Jack Wilshere used to play at, but even in England's third tier you need to be clinical at both ends, and Town's failure to do that stopped an otherwise good performance being a winning one as they had to settle for a 1-1 draw.

Huddersfield had the better of the first half but one moment of awful defending meant they finished it behind.

The Terriers were playing with the confidence both sides ought to have gone into the game with after four straight wins, as shown by Cameron Humphreys twice trying to score from corners. His first effort dropped onto the roof of the net in the 13th minute, his second had to be tipped over by James Shea seven minutes later.

But the Terriers needed to get in front before they could showboat, and despite their best efforts, could not do so.

Marcus Harness had a shot touched behind after a nice turn and shot wide. Taylor had at the goalkeeper and Archie Collins volleyed very wide when a long throw-in dropped to him.

But their best chance came on the half-hour.

When former Hull City midfielder Kasey Palmer brought a Fernandes dribble to an abrupt end, the winger's free-kick took a deflection on its way to the far post. Even the ricochet nearly bounced in off a Luton defender.

So it looked for all the world as though Town would be the first scorers, but they were caught out in the 41st minute when left-back San Roughan overcommitted at a long ball, letting Jamie Donley. He let them off the hook by failing to find an orange shirt with his ball in, but the hosts failed to clear it, former Barnsley player Jordan Clark eventually putting an end to the nonsense with the goal.

Taylor's goal early in the second half should have fired the starting gun on a comeback but instead, Huddersfield ran into a succession of nearly moments.

Twice in a minute Town got to the right byline and put the ball over.

Having got above his man, Taylor headed Collins' centre wide. But when Fernandes did something similar a minute later, he thrashed in a volley.

Mumba twice did well down the left but Harness hit his shot into a defender and when the wide man wriggled through a few minutes later, his cross only found Taylor's hand.

Picked out by a nice Humphreys pass, Taylor's touch let him down, and when Fernandes beat his man easily in the 73rd minute, he could not find a blue-and-white striped shirt.

It could have been worse, an alert Radinio Balker snuffing out a couple of threatening Luton counter-attacks, but Huddersfield are now the genuine League One title challengers they expected to be last season, they demand more of themselves.

Huddersfield Town: Young; Bronkhorst, Balker, Bowat, Roughan; Fernandes, Collins, Humphreys, Mumba; Harness (Fletcher 75); Taylor (Tovide 90+2).

Unused substitutes: Low, Gooch, Kasumu, Ashia, Alnwick.

Luton Town: Shea; Jones, Andersen, Johnston, Naismith (Ashby 17); Walsh; Mendel (Richards 60), Clark, Donley (Gore 85), Palmer (Lawrence 85); Wells (Marshall 85).

#1935. Liverpool legend Steven Gerrard says three teams can rival Arsenal for the Premier League title

Steven Gerrard believes Arsenal will retain the Premier League trophy but says three other teams will also ‘pull away’ at the top of the table.

The reigning champions reclaimed their position at the top of the Premier League with a hard-fought 1-0 win over Liverpool on Sunday.

Previous leaders Manchester City suffered another surprising defeat, losing 1-0 at home to Brighton, and Arsenal took full advantage with a narrow win at Anfield thanks to Kai Havertz’s first-half goal.

It was another performance from Arsenal that convinced Gerrard that the Premier League trophy will be heading back to the Emirates Stadium after Mikel Arteta ended the club’s 22-year wait last season.

Sign up to our daily football newsletter, pick your team and get the latest news sent directly to your inbox every morning.

But Gerrard believes three other clubs – Man City, Liverpool and Chelsea – will also ‘pull away’ from their Premier League rivals and could all challenge Arsenal for the title.

‘Credit to Arsenal because that’s how you win leagues, going to places like Liverpool, being strong, sticking together, and putting in a different type of performance,’ Gerrard told The Overlap Daily, sponsored by Sky Bet.

‘It was full of grit and fight and togetherness, and they got over the line. And they will know that come the end of the season, if they win the league, which I think they will, I haven’t changed my mind from the beginning of the season, they will look back at that more than your four or five-nils where they look fantastic, because I’m sure they will at times.

‘They’ll look at that and think, we went to Anfield, tough crowd to play against, tough Liverpool performance, Andoni Iraola’s got this Liverpool team playing an awful lot better, Liverpool played well and we managed to get out of there with three points.

‘So it could be huge for Arsenal. At this moment in time, nine points behind for Liverpool. So, Liverpool have got work to do if they want to challenge.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘But this Arsenal team just look as if they can beat teams in different ways. I think that could be the difference.’

Brighton are third in the Premier League after a memorable win at Manchester City and Gerrard believes Fabian Hurzeler’s side can challenge for a top-four place if not the title.

‘I’m going to put my neck on the line and say that I think they will fall away from that, but that’s not a criticism, because I think they’re a top team with a top manager,’ Gerrard added.

‘I just think to go the distance over the course, I think the stronger teams in the league will pull away a bit, but I certainly think they’re top four contenders and the most dangerous team in the league at the moment to play, because they’re playing without fear.

‘Everyone knows their job in the team, in and out of possession. They’ve improved a lot, I would say, from a defensive point of view. And they’ve got so many dangerous players, people that are comfortable on the ball.

‘They’re fantastic to watch. I think Brighton are more of a threat for the top-four chasers because I think they’re going to push for Champions League places.

‘Over the course, you’re faced with so many different challenges in the Premier League. And I just think where Arsenal’s squad is, and City’s, the Liverpool squad, I just think over the course of the 38 games, the three teams, and Chelsea, when you look at Chelsea in the second half there, I think them teams will pull away a bit over the course.

‘But I think they’re going to push and I think they’re going to go for it and I’m really interested to see how hard they can push. They’re not a title contender, in my opinion.’

#1934. Barcelona's Gavi stance 'revealed' amid transfer speculation surrounding 22-year-old

By Matt Law | 02 Nov 2026 19:49

Barcelona are reportedly unwilling to discuss an exit for Gavi, with the club viewing the midfielder as a vital player despite his struggles for action this term.

The 22-year-old has been restricted to just 191 minutes of football across seven appearances for Barcelona at the start of the 2026-27 campaign.

The Spaniard has only started twice in La Liga this term, while his three appearances in the Champions League have come off the bench.

There is currently a host of speculation surrounding Gavi's future, with some reports claiming that the midfielder could be allowed to leave Camp Nou for the right price.

However, according to transfer expert Fabrizio Romano, Barcelona have no desire to allow Gavi to leave, viewing the Spaniard as an important part of their plans moving forward.

Barcelona head coach Hansi Flick was asked about Gavi during his press conference on Monday, with the team preparing to face Aston Villa in the Champions League on Tuesday.

“We all know his quality and Gavi is always an option, but once the match starts that option might disappear and you can’t always stick to your initial plan. I’ve spoken to him and the important thing is that he has confidence," Flick told reporters.

Gavi has been with Barcelona since the age of 11, progressing to the first team in 2021, and he has represented the Catalan outfit on 173 occasions, scoring 10 goals and registering 18 assists for the club in all competitions.

Worryingly, Gavi has already had two severe knee injuries in the early stages of his career, first being absent between November 2023 and September 2024.

Gavi was also missing between August 2025 and March 2026, and fitness problems have made it difficult for him to find consistency in recent seasons.

It is understood that a number of major clubs are keeping a close eye on the situation in the event that Barcelona signal a willingness to let him depart.

Barcelona will follow Tuesday's clash against Villa with a La Liga fixture away to Atletico Madrid ahead of the November international break.

#1933. Paul Merson slams Manchester United over Andrey Santos transfer and makes relegation claim

Paul Merson has criticised Manchester United’s decision to sign Andrey Santos and says the Red Devils will be in the relegation zone come December.

Brazilian midfielder Santos has made an inauspicious start to his United career following a £50m move from Chelsea over the summer.

The 22-year-old has started less than half of Manchester United’s games so far this season and struggled to make an impact when he has featured.

Santos is certainly not the only player at Old Trafford under-performing, with Michael Carrick’s side only out of the relegation zone on goal difference following their worst start to the season since the 1980s.

Sign up to our daily football newsletter, pick your team and get the latest news sent directly to your inbox every morning.

United’s next five league games are against Aston Villa, Liverpool, Brentford, Newcastle United and Coventry City, and Merson believes they will be sitting in the drop zone by the time they face Frank Lampard’s side in early December.

‘Manchester United play Coventry on the 5th of December and I’d be shocked if they’re not in the bottom three by then,’ Merson told Sky Sports.

‘That’ll be about a third of the season gone then. They might go and get a big result next weekend, Aston Villa looked beatable the other day.

‘I don’t see them getting relegated, absolutely not. But this is not Manchester United and there’s no quick fix, they got it all wrong upstairs.

‘The first window, they went for the forward line but it wasn’t good enough. Matheus Cunha, Bryan Mbeumo, Benjamin Sesko, they’re nice players but they’re not 20-25 goal-a-season players.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘You’ve got to be a seven, seven and a half out of 10 every week at Manchester United. But they’re a four one week, a nine the next. You can play for Wolves or Brentford and do that, no disrespect.

‘The day you’re a nine you win the match and everyone’s pleased. When you’re a four, people say that’s just the way it is.’

Merson believes a weak and unbalanced midfield is one of Manchester United’s biggest issues, questioning the decision to sign Santos from Chelsea.

‘Youri Tielemans, he’s a good player but there’s no legs around him in the team. He had legs around him when he was playing at Villa.

‘And now they say they’ll work on the defence in the next window. It’s madness – you can’t build a house on a puddle. You just can’t. Why not start with the defence first and then go from there?

‘They say they’re going to go and outscore teams but they haven’t bought players who score enough goals.

#1931. Preston North End 2 Sheffield United 3: Hat-trick hero Sydie Peck steals show for Blades

The silky midfielder’s previous goal this season had arrived not far away from Preston at Ewood Park.

He must have a liking for these parts after plundering a first-half hat-trick in less than 20 minutes, becoming the first Blades player to achieve that feat since the legendary Billy Sharp in February 2019.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

A thoroughly bizarre first period saw United stink the place out in the opening 20 minutes and deservedly trail rock-bottom hosts, who led after just two minutes, courtesy of Leo Leroy’s first goal for North End.

Fortunately, United eventually got with it, thanks to the elegant Peck.

A 76th-minute goal from Preston substitute Callum Lang would set up an edgy finale at 2-3. It has rarely been easy and straightforward where United have been concerned over the past couple of seasons.

But that night was theirs and Peck’s as Wilder’s side recorded back-to-back league wins for the first time since April.

It’s the time of year when the nights draw in, the overcoats come out and league tables start to mean that bit more.

Five games into a seven-match block of Championship games ahead of the November international break, Wilder’s side were in reasonably good shape - certainly in comparison to this time last season - with 10 points accrued from a possible 15.

Being consistently inconsistent remains something that the Blades had been wrestling with and against a Preston side on the ropes all season and propping up the rest virtually since day one, it was an evening for getting the job done.

North End definitely weren’t in good shape. The arrival of Graham Alexander from Bradford City had failed to arrest their fortunes, quite the opposite in fact. They had taken a derisory one point from his opening five games.

Preston came into the game with a horrific statistic against their name, with the only side in Championship history to muster few points after the first 13 games of a campaign - without points deductions - being Sheffield Wednesday back in 2023-24.

That campaign, the Owls won in game 14 and managed to stay up. The odds of Preston doing that appear long, indeed.

Kalvin Phillips, Joe Rothwell and Patrick Bamford all missed out through injury, with Jairo Riedewald handed his first league start since September 5. Mark McGuinness came in for the suspended Liam Kitching, while ex-North End loanee Tom Cannon was back up front for United.

The game started off in the worst possible fashion for United, wearing their luminous yellow away strip.

Tahith Chong was painfully weak in the challenge and home captain Andrew Hughes powered forward and found Andrija Vuckevic down the left in acres of space on the overlap.

Andrew Moran failed to connect with a fresh-air shot following Vuckevic’s low centre, but Leroy - left untracked after powering into the box - was unerring, blasting home a first-timer into the top corner.

It was a dreadful start for United, who were safe, passive and meek in the opening 20 minutes. It certainly did not look like a Wilder team with the hosts outworking and outenthusing those in visiting colours and winning virtually all of the duels.

The midfielder delivered a precious nugget of much-needed quality on 27 minutes from the left, where United were far more convincing than on the opposite flank.

Peck’s sweetly struck cross-shot evaded everyone before nestling in the far corner.

It was the prelude to Preston starting to display the brittle defensive confidence that you would associate with a side marooned at the foot of the table.

Daniel Iversen’s decision to race out of goal was ill-advised in the extreme following Ben Brereton Diaz’s astute pass and he found himself in total no-man’s land.

Still, Peck had so much to do after rounding the home keeper on the left-hand side.

With North End defenders on the cover and team-mates in support, Peck had a decision to make. Play it safe and pass or go for it?

He chose the latter and his marvellous curled shot was perfection and flew into the top corner. It was a thing of beauty not in keeping with United's first 20 minutes.

Their fans had been getting understandably edgy against seemingly pumped-up hosts. The half would end with considerable home tension and even chants of ‘You’re not fit to wear the shirt’ ahead of boos at the interval.

Peck’s hat-trick goal was the reason with Romelle Donovan’s low centre dissecting a dozing North End defence, with Peck obligingly tapping home from close in.

Early in the second half, Peck - clearly getting a taste for it and enjoying himself immensely - almost added another, testing Iversen low down at his near post.

The Peck show continued. A free-kick was blocked and an angled shot almost crept in at the far corner

The next goal was a Preston one as North End secured a lifeline after Lang coolly converted following an assist from fellow replacement Alfie Devine with the visitors opened up in central defence.

It made it a needlessly tense finale. But the night was Peck’s.

Preston North End: Iversen; Offiah, Storey (Lindsay HT), Hughes; Mills (Potts 90), Leroy, Thompson, Vukcevic (Wiley HT) Moran; Erabi (Devine 64), Kenny (Lang 13). Substitutes unused: Nicholls, Small, Nolan, Burgzorg.

Sheffield United: Cooper; Choudhury (Ayew 71), Tanganga, McGuinness, Burrows; Chong (Seriki 58), Peck, Riedewald (Arblaster 58), Donovan (McCallum 84); Cannon, Brereton-Diaz. Substitutes unused: Doherty, Campbell, Norrington-Davies, Betts, Baptiste.

#1928. Jamie Carragher issues apology for telling Aston Villa fans to 'shut the f*** up' - after club's owners threatened former Liverpool defender with legal action

Published: 08:57 EDT, 31 October 2026 | Updated: 11:21 EDT, 31 October 2026

Jamie Carragher has fronted up and apologised to Aston Villa and its supporters after his 'clumsy & wrong' language saw the club's owners threaten legal action.

The story took a dramatic turn on Friday night when Villa released a club statement revealing the bombshell claim that they intend to take legal action against Carragher.

In a statement on club channels carrying the name of co-owner Nassef Sawiris, Villa wrote: 'Aston Villa will initiate legal action against Jamie Carragher for his unacceptable insults about the Club and its fans.

'Aston Villa will not allow anyone to stop our ascension in English and European football. Nassef Sawiris, Chairman.'

The row, which centres on comments made by Carragher on the Overlap this week in which he pushed the idea of Unai Emery becoming the next Manchester United manager, only escalated further when Carragher doubled down, telling Villa fans to 'shut the f**k up'.

But the Liverpool legend changed his tune on Saturday afternoon in a bid to defuse an increasingly volatile situation.

I’d like to apologise to Aston Villa, the owners & their fans. My language this week was clumsy & wrong.I can assure Villa fans it was tongue in cheek but I can understand it’s not come across that way, so apologies. Good luck today UTV!

Jamie Carragher has apologised for comments he made about Aston Villa and Unai Emery

'I'd like to apologise to Aston Villa, the owners & their fans,' Carragher wrote on social media.

'My language this week was clumsy & wrong. I can assure Villa fans it was tongue in cheek but I can understand it's not come across that way, so apologies. Good luck today UTV!'

Fans were left stunned at the response by Villa to Carragher's comments, seemingly innocuous linking Emery, who is admired at Old Trafford, to the Manchester United job, which may soon be available with immense pressure on Michael Carrick.

‘I think Unai Emery is unbelievable with what he does year after year. That amount of change, players needing time to settle and he does it year after year,' Carragher had said.

'But the reason I’m going to go back at Villa fans is I can’t believe that a manager who is so successful in the Europa League, take a player, if you’d won the Europa League three or four times (Emery has won it five times) surely you’ll then want to go for the Champions League.

‘Aston Villa will never be Manchester United. I just think he didn’t do well at PSG or Arsenal, and maybe that’s because of egos in the dressing room and that sort of thing.

'But surely he would want that opportunity to manage a giant again. There is a chain in football, whether you like it or not.’

A sloppy moment defensively cancelled out by Joe Taylor's stunning volley but not added to meant Town had to settle for a 1-1 draw in a game when they had lots of the ball in their attacking third, but did not make enough of it.

Coach Drury felt their mindset was slightly to blame.

"A challenging game, a difficult game against a team with really good individuals. I thought they started the game slightly better than us, started a little bit quicker. We'd been scoring goals early on in the game, so it was disappointing to start as slow as we did.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

"That being said, I thought we started to understand the game better, understand what they were doing better and how we could attack them. I thought we then started to take control.

"I thought we were absolutely dominant in the first half, got to their box numerous times, hit the post, hit the bar.

"We probably just lacked that little bit of decision-making in key moments for us. I felt we were trying to almost find the perfect angle to shoot tonight and not use their defenders to help us, whether it be through the legs or shape one round in.

"We were looking for a little bit more perfection and clear-cut chances, but Luton defended well.

"We get to half-time, it threw up a new challenge for us. We've not been behind at half-time this season in the league. That was a new challenge for us, which I'd welcome because I want to know what we're made of in those moments when it's not all our own way.

"In the second half, I thought we started really well. We were strong, we were dominant, scored a fantastic goal. From there on, I thought we were in the ascendancy and I thought we'd go on to win.

"But you're playing against good players and a good group. The game then started to settle down again.

"I thought we had some really nice attacking moments. Luton had one or two maybe half-chances, but we got into their box so many times, we just lacked that killer instinct in the final third.

"But, again, take nothing away from them, they defended the box really well."

Luton led against the run of play through former Barnsley player Jordan Clark after San Roughan overcommitted at a long ball and Huddersfield missed a couple of chances to clear their lines.

"I'm really disappointed with the goal," said Drury. "The goal is a very, very poor goal to concede.

"We have to do better in that moment because no disrespect, but that is not a well-worked goal. That is a goal that we've not defended well enough.

"We've gambled on the ball in behind and then we've not headed it clear. We're in the middle of the box and then we've come to block the shot and it's one player against two and they get shot and then scored. So, that's not a goal that we would normally concede.

"What I did like is the reaction after it.

"Both as individual players and the group as a whole, I thought there was a real strong mentality there to kick on from there. And, as I say, second half, I thought we showed that a lot. But disappointing, just not to kick on and get any more goals."

Peck then came to the party with a cross-shot drawing the Blades level on 27 minutes. Ten minutes later, he scored a brilliant curler before tapping home just before the interval.

Substitute Callum Lang pulled one back in the final quarter but United held out for their fourth win in their past six matches. Wilder's side are up to ninth in the Championship table.

On his match-winner, Wilder said: "His all-round performance was excellent. I'm talking about playing him higher and getting in the box and making forward runs.

"He's done it right the way through his young career, scored goals and he needs to score more. I'm just thinking about it and I spoke to him about Leicester last season when he got a couple. We had a good afternoon at the King Power and he's got that in his locker.

"I think he's a touch disappointed because he's had a couple more opportunities in the second half and we did. We got into some great positions. (Tahith) Chong should score, Sydie possibly should score (again).

"I'm not going to be greedy and say every opportunity that we have we should score from, but we created enough to take the game away from the opposition.

"But Sydie will get all the headlines and deservedly so. He'll one day hopefully captain this football club.

"It was too early, in my opinion, when he was doing it before I came back, I needed to take that responsibility off of him and make sure he got his head down and was a good footballer. He was a good footballer tonight.

"Off the pitch, (you see) his leadership skills in training, he wants to win and you can see that. It was there in abundance and I'm all over that.

"First and foremost, you've got to win the game of football, but the emotion side of it, he plays his football emotionally as well as intelligently and it's a good night for him, a great night for him."

On his side’s overall display, Wilder, whose side visit Charlton this weekend, continued: "Apart from the first two minutes and maybe the last five minutes, I thought my team was outstanding. We gave them an obvious lift and a leg up with the start.

#1921. Man Utd boost as £33m left-back decides he’s ‘open’ to January transfer

Barcelona misfit Alejandro Balde is reportedly ‘open’ to leaving the club in January amid strong interest from Manchester United.

Balde joined Barca at the age of just eight after impressing in Espanyol’s youth ranks and would go on to break into the Catalan giants’ first-team in 2021.

The 23-year-old left-back has since made a total of 172 appearances in all competitions for Barca while helping the club win seven pieces of silverware, including three La Liga titles.

However, Balde has badly struggled for regular playing time under head coach Hansi Flick, with all four of his appearances this season coming from the substitutes bench.

Sign up to our daily football newsletter, pick your team and get the latest news sent directly to your inbox every morning.

Balde currently finds himself behind both Joao Cancelo and Xavi Espart in the pecking order at the Camp Nou and the Spain international’s career appears to be at a crossroads.

According to Spanish publication Mundo Deportivo, Barca’s coaching staff are of the belief that Balde is prone to ‘losing focus’ and is unable to read the game well when it comes to pressing.

‘Balde doesn’t have the confidence he needs in his game right now, nor the conviction,’ Flick told reporters ahead of Barca’s 6-1 victory over Alaves last weekend.

It’s claimed the situation has left Balde ‘open’ to the prospect of moving on from Barca, with the out-of-favour full-back ‘beginning to accept’ that this is likely his only route back to playing consistently.

Balde is said to have grown ‘upset’ as he expected Flick to have been direct and honest with him over his limited minutes, as the German supposedly had been with the likes of Marc Casado and Hector Fort.

He has ‘learned lessons’ from his close friend Ansu Fati, who spent a number of years waiting for opportunities at Barca without managing to nail down regular game-time.

It is believed a bid in the region of €40million (£33m) could be enough to secure a deal for Balde when the January transfer window opens for business.

There are 18 months remaining on Balde’s current contract with the reigning Spanish champions.

Diogo Dalot has therefore been forced to fill in as a makeshift left-back during United’s miserable winless streak under an increasingly under-pressure Michael Carrick.

#1920. Rotherham United boss Alex Bruce on job talk plus clarification on player absence

Rotherham's elimination from the EFL Trophy was confirmed following a 1-0 home reverse to Newcastle United under-21s in front of a crowd of just 805.

The only goal of the game arrived on 34 minutes through Magpies player Kyran Thompson, with the north-easterners progressing to the next stage alongside Northern Group C winners Bradford City. The Millers did not muster an effort on target in the second period.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Bruce's side have not win a competitive game since September 19. They visit Bromley in the FA Cup this weekend and are 22nd in League Two.

Asked whether his job is in jeopardy, Bruce said: "It's not about me. If there's a fight to be had, I'll have it, but I know the buck stops with me."

On his side's winless streak extending, he continued: "In large parts of it, there wasn't really that much in the game.

"They counter-attacked us in the first half and scored. We didn't do enough to win the game. I think we huffed and puffed.

"As I've just said to the players in the dressing room, to win football matches, you have to show a little bit more than that. If we are going to get out of the trouble that we're in, we need to start showing a bit more than we did."

Despite being available for the competition, Jili Buyabu - dismissed for elbowing a Swindon Town player in last Saturday's League Two fixture - was not involved, with Bruce revealing he had been ordered to stay away from the training ground following his senseless dismissal.

Bruce continued: "I've not seen him since the Swindon game.

"He's stayed away for a couple of days. I told him to stay away. He's back in on Thursday, so we'll look at things then.

"It doesn't take a rocket scientist to realise why he's not been involved.

"I accept people make mistakes, I don't accept certain other things. When he comes back into the group, he needs to show an appetite to wear the shirt in the right way. On Saturday, he didn't do that."

#1918. William Saliba back in Arsenal training after 'absolutely smashing' injury recovery

By Ben Knapton | 02 Nov 2026 20:02

Arsenal defender William Saliba has reportedly returned to full training after 'absolutely smashing' his milestones in his recuperation from a back injury.

The France international is yet to make an appearance for the Premier League champions this season, having exacerbated a long-standing back issue during the World Cup semi-finals.

Arsenal and Saliba opted against surgery in favour of a conservative approach to treatment, although there were fears that the 25-year-old would not feature again in 2026.

However, Saliba returned to individual training in October, and Arteta refused to rule out a return for the centre-back following the November international break.

A comeback this month could very well be on the cards, as according to HandofArsenal, Saliba is now back in first-team training, thus clearing a major milestone in his recovery process and taking a huge step towards being available again.

The X account adds that Saliba has 'absolutely smashed' his recovery targets over the past few months, although Arsenal will understandably be extremely cautious when it comes to his re-integration.

Saliba is not expected to be involved in Wednesday's Champions League league-phase match against Slavia Prague, although he may be seen taking part in the team session during Arsenal's open training on Tuesday morning.

Mikel Arteta will inevitably be quizzed for an update on Saliba in his pre-game press conference if he does appear, but the Spaniard is likely to keep his cards close to his chest.

However, the 25-year-old may be in with a slim chance of making the squad against Hull City this weekend, or Arsenal's first game back following the international break away to Newcastle United on November 21.

Saliba made 50 appearances for Arsenal across all competitions in the 2025-26 season, including 30 Premier League starts and 12 in the Champions League, while playing 4,254 minutes in total.

The former Saint-Etienne starlet also started six games for France at the 2026 World Cup, but he was taken off in the 30th minute of Les Bleus' semi-final loss to Spain as a result of his back problem.

Saliba's imminent return to first-team football will give Arteta the best selection dilemma imaginable, thanks to Ezri Konsa's seamless integration into the Arsenal backline.

The England international has already played his part in five clean sheets in the 2026-27 Premier League season and produced another defensive masterclass in Arsenal's 1-0 win over Liverpool, as his relationship with Gabriel Magalhaes blossoms further.

Konsa should expect to maintain his undisputed starter status for the next few weeks at least, while Saliba builds his match fitness back up, and the 29-year-old can be viewed as a genuine competitor to the Frenchman, not just his backup.

However, if Saliba can return to the level he was performing at in each of the past four years, expect the 25-year-old to eventually regain his rightful spot in the Arsenal back four, even if Konsa has been one of the signings of the season so far.
