#1915. Lisandro Martinez's self-destruction sums up a broken Man United as Michael Carrick's future hangs by a thread - and there are still questions to ask of Xabi Alonso's Chelsea, writes IAN HERBERT

Published: 10:52 EDT, 31 October 2026 | Updated: 12:01 EDT, 31 October 2026

The sun was high and fierce and Michael Carrick shielded his eyes from it on the few occasions he got to his feet and tried to direct the Manchester United players, who did not seem to hear him. The United contingent hurled personal abuse at Sir Jim Ratcliffe and Jason Wilcox. The scrutiny was remorseless and unyielding.

For a time, there seemed to be hope - and no one can say that this latest hammer blow for Carrick removes the doubts about Xabi Alonso’s methods – but it was crushed by the same fecklessness and mindlessness that is burying United alive.

Carrick did not cast so much as a glance at Lisandro Martinez - who had just finished off the team’s hopes by leaping with Wesley Fofana and extending an elbow into his face to concede a penalty - when he walked past on the way to the tunnel.

Bruno Fernandes and some others made a half-hearted protest about the dismissal but Carrick didn’t. He knew. This looked for all the world like a footballer looking to leave the field early – making no attempt to play the ball as he was up with Fofana, having been booked for a reckless challenge on Morgan Rogers, just three minutes earlier.

The Argentinian, whose words publicly challenging the club a few weeks back will always belong to the story of these Carrick-era death throes, will perhaps want to trash talk the club again when he has been shown the door. But it was also his own gross inadequacy which had allowed Morgan Rogers to dance through the defence to put Chelsea ahead. Martinez should never darken the door of a United squad again.

Michael Carrick’s future at Manchester United looks increasingly untenable after his side imploded in the second half to lose 2-0 against Chelsea at Stamford Bridge

Lisandro Martinez, publicly outspoken earlier this month, was booked twice inside two minutes

There are few grounds for optimism from here but Fernandes is one. When he forfeited the chance to write a new script for himself – blasting into the stand after Bryan Mbeumo’s cross had gifted him a golden opportunity – the prospect of him righting the wrongs of the past week seemed forlorn.

By then, he had already been dumped on his backside by Romeo Lavia and Moises Caicedo and ceded possession. But he brushed off the mockery of the Chelsea faithful to put in a performance which demonstrated that he has a part to play at United.

In front of the small United away section before the game, he went through a free-kick taking routine, arcing one into the top-left corner and striking another against the bar.

He was the one who saw the picture late in the first half, sliding in a pass which sent Amad in. When United went 2-0 down, he conferred with Carrick. He lingered before United’s fans at the end and they accepted him. The turmoil remains but he will be needed.

Fernandes was the one who saw the picture late in the first half, sliding in a pass which sent Amad in and United went 2-0 down, he conferred with Carrick

There can be no overstating the gravity of the week just passed for Xabi Alonso: a lamentable performance in defeat to Tottenham, the Carabao Cup defeat to Liverpool and the Spaniard’s suggestion that trophy didn’t matter, which has gone down badly with the fans.

His brief programme notes made it clear how much he wanted something better here but the yawning gaps between Chelsea’s midfield and defensive lines and the ease with which United exploited them in the first half were disturbing. Wesley Fofana was lamentable.

United’s Amad could have plundered them twice – first burgling Fofana on the half-way line but lacking the pace to accelerate on and score, then easing into space and failing to despatch when one-on-one with Mike Penders. Cole Palmer’s error allowed Matheus Cunha to send Fernandes off but Mbeumo couldn’t connect with his cross. United’s failure to capitalise was fateful.

Wesley Fofana was lamentable and United’s Amad Diallo could have plundered them twice

As both sides squandered chances and laboured under basic defensive challenges, it was hard to countenance the notion that two gladiators of European football used to compete in this fixture and actually contested a Champions League final.

The occasion cried out for a moment of class and it was Morgan Rogers who provided it, taking a ball Romeo Lavia had won, dancing his way through half of the Manchester United team and slipping the ball home.

The defending shamed the traditions of the visiting team. Carlos Baleba, Andrey Santos, Martinez and Harry Maguire just watched Morgan go. But it was Rogers, taking his Chelsea tally to six goals and four assists in all competitions, who turned the game around.

Morgan Rogers had scored a brilliant solo goal for Chelsea's second-half opener to show up United’s awful finishing

It was always clear that the test of United’s mettle would come if they fell behind. The general view of the fans marching through Euston Station at 11am was that if United scored first they would come away with the points. If they conceded, their heads would drop and the psychological failure at the heart of this team would come to the fore. And so it came to pass.

In a straw poll of 15 or so at Euston, only two thought Carrick was the man to restore ‘Standards’, to quote the mantra captured on an Old Trafford banner last week. The way Chelsea turned the screw just bore that pessimism. Cole Palmer converted the penalty Martinez had conceded to finish things off.

It was to the jubilant cheers of the Chelsea faithful that Estevao left the field towards the end and this was an afternoon which will live long in the memory for him. Twice he had the ball in United’s net – pouncing on Senne Lammens' failure to hold a cross in the first half and taking Palmer’s pass to crash home in the second – but twice he was denied by VAR.

By the end, he had the control of Chelsea’s right as he interlinked with Palmer and came close a third time. Some will say this calls into question Alonso’s decision to limit his game time so far, though it was only as United fell away to nothing that he ran the show.

Some will say Estevao's display calls into question Alonso’s decision to limit his game time so far, though it was only as United fell away to nothing that he ran the show

As the minutes ticked down on another desperate result for United, the away section sang Carrick’s name once more and, significantly, he walked over towards them alone once more, just as he had after the defeat at home to Bournemouth. But it was a less emphatic assertion of empathy and support for him this time, and he did not linger so long.

The talk of Eddie Howe’s availability grows. It emerged on Saturday that under the terms of his departure agreement with Newcastle United that he will cost United only £3million. The United fans are really not convinced by him and it looks like the club will work through many more managers before a corner is turned. The constant will be that support base, who began and ended the match singing Sir Matt Busby’s name. They will always have their history.

#1913. Barella admits Inter have changed derby approach in recent years: “We’re too inconsistent”

After the game, Nicolo Barella attempted to lessen the damage of last night’s loss to AC Milan in his post-game press conference.

For Milan, last night was another instance in what is becoming a new norm. After Inter’s streak of derby wins, it’s now the Rossoneri who are enjoying themselves. They’ve won each of their last four meetings and haven’t lost in eight games.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

In short, despite all of the managerial changes that have taken place, the Diavolo remain on top when it comes to playing the Nerazzurri.

Of course, last night’s win was also monumental considering what it meant for the Serie A table. Rather than falling 10 points behind, they only sit four points behind Inter and Lazio, who share first.

Speaking at a post-match conference, Barella admitted that Inter are going through a bad cycle in the derbies, but was keen to remember the streak from a few years ago, as MilanNews relayed.

“Certainly, if we talk about this, we’ve been lacking the ideal approach to matches since the start of the year. Right now, it’s a clear criticality for us.

“It’s true that we’ve shown our strength on many occasions, perhaps coming out on top in the second half or whenever we manage to break the deadlock, but it’s clear that not every match goes that way.

“We can’t expect to always repeat the same pattern, especially when we face a packed schedule with matches every three days. Fatigue, both physical and mental, is starting to take its toll, and we need to learn to manage matches better without being forced to keep them in the balance until the ninetieth minute.”

Is there a feeling that, whatever you do, Milan will prevail in derbies?

“Let’s say I’ve also experienced it the other way around. I’ve had a lot of derby wins in a row, so I don’t know if it’s a cyclical thing, but it’s definitely a game we haven’t approached in the best way in recent years, recently.

“There have been derbies where we’ve played well and lost, where we’ve played poorly and maybe drawn, but we’re too inconsistent in derbies, and right now, even in important matches. Even though we won, we still needed to do better.”

Do you still have the fierce desire to prove that you are the strongest?

“Being the strongest is sometimes not enough, because we’ve also been the strongest team, or the one everyone thought was the strongest, but then we didn’t win. So right now, I think we need to focus on something else rather than our strength.

“It’s true that if we look back at the last few games, many goals come from individual errors, and we need to improve on those, each of us, because unfortunately, individual errors work against the team. But as a team, we need to improve a bit in terms of solidity, which is what has always set us apart, what got us to the Champions League final, what helped us win the Scudetto, and perhaps right now we’re not the best version of ourselves. So we need to work on that. We still have the desire to win, for sure, because that’s what keeps us going to the pitch every day and motivates us, but we need to improve.”

#1912. PSV Eindhoven vs. Club Brugge - prediction, team news, lineups

By Seye Omidiora | 02 Nov 2026 22:00, Last updated: 03 Nov 2026 14:16

PSV Eindhoven seek consecutive Champions League wins for the first time since January last year as they host Club Brugge at Philips Stadion in Wednesday's fourth matchday.

Peter Bosz's men secured a 1-0 win at Porto last time out, their first clean sheet in the competition since November 2024, and now look to surpass their 11th-placed Belgian opponents by recording a victory.

PSV's form dipped in recent weeks leading up to the Eindhoven side's win at Porto on matchday three, ending the Peasants' run of two consecutive losses and three defeats in four matches.

Bosz's team had gone seven matches in all competitions without defeat until their 3-2 loss at FC Twente prior to the international break, which led to a dip in performances and results.

Immediately apparent was the Dutch giants' drop-off in the attacking third, with the four-peat-chasing Eredivisie side atypically failing to score more than one goal in four of their six matches preceding the weekend's 7-0 thrashing of Willem II.

Nevertheless, given that Willem II are the bottom-placed side in the Dutch top flight, much cannot be read into the beatdown of the struggling side.

Yet fans must have been gratified to see the 1987-88 European Cup winners find some much-needed fluency ahead of facing Club Brugge, as the Peasants chase a first victory over Belgian opponents in this competition after two losses to Anderlecht in 2000-01 and a defeat against Union Saint-Gilloise last season.

Snapping that losing streak will be far from easy against the 20-time Belgian champions, who have responded to their 3-2 defeat by Aston Villa on matchday one with consecutive wins.

The pick of that run was a stunning 4-3 triumph away at three-time European Cup winners Inter Milan at San Siro before following that up with a 3-0 success over Lens in Bruges.

Those wins have been part of Blauw-Zwart's eight-match winning streak both domestically and in Europe, with the latter catapulting Ivan Leko's team to 11th in the league phase table, seven spots ahead of their Eindhoven hosts.

The Bruges outfit have been free-scoring during that run, finding ways to outscore Inter in Europe and St. Truidense as well as Zulte Waregem; however, they have also found ways to win narrowly and even comfortably, highlighted by successes against Lokeren (1-0), Genk (3-0) and Lens (3-0).

A third consecutive victory could take FC Bruges into the coveted top eight spots, but they must win away at Dutch opposition for the first time in three attempts after drawing at Twente in the 1989-90 UEFA Cup and in the 2003-04 Champions League loss at Ajax.

PSV have a few injury worries ahead of matchday four, with Paul Wanner and Sam Lammers requiring late checks to assess their readiness, while Sami Ouaissa, Alassane Plea and Jerdy Schouten are sidelined.

Suspended for De Kraker against Feyenoord, Sven Mijnans scored and assisted in the 7-0 beatdown of Willem II at the weekend to extend his streak of either scoring or assisting to three consecutive matches.

Guus Til has scored or assisted in four consecutive matches, including his match-winning strike in the 1-0 success at Porto last month, and the attacker aims to extend his streak on Wednesday.

The undeniable standout star for the Belgian outfit is Nicolo Tresoldi, who has netted four of his side's nine Champions League strikes, accounting for 44% of their European efforts; no other player has scored more than one goal, further underlining the young forward's prolific continental record.

While Club Brugge have a healthy squad, Leko is without the services of Joel Ordonez, who has not played in any capacity since Ecuador's loss to Mexico at the 2026 World Cup.

Kovar; Dest, Geertruida, Obispo, Kostic; Sano, Junior; Perisic, Til, Van Bommel; Mijnans

Sommer; Sabbe, Spileers, Mechele, Seys; Potts, Vanaken; Forbs, Vetlesen, Virgili; Tresoldi

Putting seven past the Eredivisie’s bottom side does not necessarily signal the end of PSV’s inconsistencies, especially against opponents who have already demonstrated their credentials at San Siro.

With Tresoldi spearheading a confident attack and Leko’s men showing several ways to win during their eight-match streak, the visitors have our backing to extend their impressive sequence.

#1911. Rasmus Kristensen reveals he was 'completely broken' after season at Leeds United

Rasmus Kristensen has revealed he was “completely broken” after his maiden campaign on Leeds United’s books.

The 29-year-old arrived at Elland Road in the summer of 2022, making a move from Red Bull Salzburg for a fee in the region of £10m.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

He was recruited to be Luke Ayling’s successor at right-back but the Denmark international struggled for consistency in West Yorkshire.

Leeds were relegated at the end his debut campaign and he spent the following two seasons out on loan before departing permanently.

In an interview with Ajax Life, the defender has opened up on the difficulties he endured at Elland Road.

He said: “I suffered from stress and depression. After that season, I was completely broken. I always saw myself only as a footballer.

“When I walked through the city or sat in a restaurant, I worried about training or the next match. If you do that, you become mentally exhausted.”

Kristensen spent the 2023/24 season on loan at Roma before linking up with Eintracht Frankfurt for the 2024/25 campaign.

The latter signed him on a permanent basis in 2025 but he is now back in his native Denmark with FC Midtjylland.

Reflecting on his first temporary stint away from Leeds, Kristensen said: “Rome was beautiful, but as a footballer, I found no joy there. Wherever I played, I felt pressure. Football is a religion in Italy - even more so than in Leeds and Amsterdam.”

Kristensen now appears to be in a better place, enjoying his football in his homeland. He will face his former club Ajax tomorrow (November 5), when Midtjylland host the Dutch giants in the Europa Conference League.

He said: “Before, after a bad training session, I would think ‘f**k football’. Now, I can put things into perspective more easily when I get home. As a father, I enjoy the game more.

“My wife and I enjoyed having our family and friends close by again.”

#1910. Coventry fan, 14, arrested following ‘cruel’ Bradley Lowery taunt in Sunderland match

A 14-year-old male has been arrested on suspicion of a public order offence and subsequently bailed after a video emerged appearing to show a Coventry fan taunting Sunderland supporters with a photograph of the late Bradley Lowery.

Bradley was a lifelong supporter of Sunderland and his battle with neuroblastoma, a rare form of childhood cancer, touched the hearts of supporters across the footballing world – and beyond – before his tragic death at the age of six in July 2017.

His legacy lives on through the Bradley Lowery Foundation which was established in August later that year and has helped support countless families in raising funds for treatment and equipment which is not readily available through the NHS.

Footage of the alleged incident came to light after Coventry’s 3-1 victory at home to Sunderland in the Premier League on Saturday afternoon.

Sign up to our daily football newsletter, pick your team and get the latest news sent directly to your inbox every morning.

The five-second clip in question appears to show a young spectator in the home end at the Coventry Building Society Arena grinning while pointing to a picture of Bradley on a mobile phone.

It is not the first time that Bradley’s story has seemingly been hijacked in such sickening circumstances, with Sheffield Wednesday fan Dale Houghton sacked from his job and handed a 12-month suspended prison sentence following a similar incident in 2023.

‘Coventry City FC is aware of footage circulating on social media in connection with an incident during our Premier League fixture against Sunderland,’ a statement from the Sky Blues read on Sunday.

Coventry City FC is aware of footage circulating on social media in connection with an incident during our Premier League fixture against Sunderland.The club does not tolerate offensive behaviour and will liaise with the relevant authorities to determine the appropriate course… pic.twitter.com/RxXnhtW3DF

‘The club does not tolerate offensive behaviour and will liaise with the relevant authorities to determine the appropriate course of action.’

It’s understood the teenage boy in question voluntarily handed himself into West Midlands Police, who, in turn, confirmed that an investigation was underway.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

The shocking video footage went viral on social media shortly after Coventry’s defeat of Sunderland and was widely condemned by both Black Cats fans and supporters of rival clubs.

A host of Coventry fans have also shown their support for Lowery’s family in the intervening days, with many leaving heartfelt messages alongside donations on JustGiving’s The Bradley Lowery Foundation fundraising page.

Lowery’s mother, Gemma, meanwhile, has called for her ‘beautiful boy’ to be ‘remembered with love, not hate’ in a heartbreaking statement on Instagram.

‘My beautiful boy deserves to be remembered with love, not hate. Yesterday, a Coventry fan used a photograph of Bradley to taunt Sunderland supporters,’ she wrote.

‘As Bradley’s mam, this is heartbreaking, especially as it’s one of my favourite photographs of him. Just look at that smile.

‘I remember that day like it was yesterday. He was so happy, having so much fun. Those moments were precious because they were few and far between. So much of Bradley’s short life was spent battling cancer and enduring treatments no child should ever face.

‘To see such a beautiful memory used in such a cruel way really does make my heart hurt.

‘We are a football-loving family who follow Sunderland home and away. I’m all for football banter, but surely mocking a child who died from cancer is not banter?

‘I hope the club takes appropriate action and the young lad’s family help him understand how hurtful his actions were. I don’t want hatred directed towards him, so please please don’t. I just for him to learn from this.

‘Behind that photograph is a little boy who was loved beyond measure and a family who miss him every day.’

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Gemma took the opportunity to thank those who had stepped up to defend Bradley since the video first began to circulate on social media.

‘Thank you to everyone who has defended Bradley and shown us so much love. It means more than you know,’ she added.

‘What some people don’t realise is that Bradley’s story didn’t end when his life did.

‘Because of Bradley, children’s lives are being saved, hundreds of families have received vital support, and children facing unimaginable battles are being given hope.

‘Through Super Brad’s Pad, families can escape hospital life, spend precious time together and make memories that last forever.‘That is Bradley’s legacy. The difference my little boy continues to make in this world. No amount of cruelty will ever take that away.‘So rather than let this photograph be remembered for hatred, I want it remembered for what it truly represents.

‘My beautiful little boy, enjoying one of the happiest days of his life, with the biggest smile on his face. That is how I want the world to remember him. #CancerHasNoColours Forever 6. Forever loved.’

Gemma finished by sharing a link to the Bradley Lowery Foundation’s website: www.bradleyloweryfoundation.com

#1909. Goalkeeper Jesus Owono in ‘profound distress and anguish’ after death of Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel

Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono ‘is experiencing profound distress and anguish’ after the death of Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel.

De Miguel suffered head and chest injuries following a collision with Owono, who was sent off for his challenge near the halfway line, during the closing stages of the Spanish second-division match on Monday.

Owono had sprinted from his goal to clear a long ball when his knee collided with De Miguel’s chest.

De Miguel rolled on the floor immediately after impact but was then motionless on his back as several players urgently signalled for medical help.

Sign up to our daily football newsletter, pick your team and get the latest news sent directly to your inbox every morning.

The 30-year-old’s condition was first described as ‘stable, given the seriousness of the condition’ on Monday night but Tenerife issued a second update in the early hours of Tuesday morning which said that his ‘medical condition has deteriorated neurologically.’

Later on Tuesday morning, Tenerife announced that De Miguel had died in hospital.

Owono initially went to leave the pitch after his red card but then turned back after the severity of De Miguel’s situation became clear.

The 25-year-old, who was playing for La Liga side Alaves last year and has made 47 appearances for Equatorial Guinea’s national team, deleted his Instagram account after receiving abuse.

According to Spanish radio station COPE, some supporters at the Heliodoro Rodriguez Lopez stadium shouted ‘murderer’ at Owono, while the goalkeeper is said to have been crying and praying in the dressing room after the match was abandoned.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

Meanwhile, Venancio Tomas Ndong Micha, the president of the Equatorial Guinean Football Federation, has issued his ‘full solidarity and support’ to Owono.

‘It is with deep shock and immense sorrow that I have received the news of the tragic passing of your player, Jesus de Miguel. On behalf of the Equatorial Guinean Football Federation, and on my own behalf, I wish to express our most sincere and heartfelt condolences for this irreparable loss,’ Ndong Micha said in a statement.

‘Football is a family that, in moments like this, unites in grief. We wish to extend our deepest solidarity to his family, his teammates, the coaching staff, and all the blanquiazul (blue-and-white) fans, who are currently enduring a time of indescribable sadness.

‘Furthermore, I feel it is necessary to convey our full solidarity and support at this time to our player, Jesus Lazaro Owono.

‘We know that, as an involuntary participant in this fatal incident during the match, he is experiencing this situation with profound distress and anguish.

‘The Equatorial Guinean Football Federation offers him our full personal and professional support, fully aware of the severity of this event—something no one in our sport ever wishes to witness.

‘We share in your mourning and remain entirely at your disposal. Please accept our deepest respect and support during these most difficult times.’

On Tuesday, police in Spain opened an investigation for possible involuntary manslaughter following De Miguel’s death.

Judicial authorities in the Canary Islands said it is a routine procedure as any death deemed non-natural under Spanish law automatically triggers a judicial inquiry.

However, the chief prosecutor of Santa Cruz de Tenerife, Jose Luis Sanchez-Jauregui, has said it would be ‘very difficult’ for a criminal process to be opened as De Miguel’s collision with Owono occurred during the match.

Speaking to Spanish news agency EFE, Sanchez-Jauregui explained that long-standing Spanish Supreme Court precedent distinguishes injuries sustained during a match from deliberate assaults which are committed when play is halted.

Sanchez-Jauregui added that the referee’s report and the decision of the Sports Disciplinary Committee, which will determine whether Owono intended to cause harm with his challenge on De Miguel, will be considered before any legal action.

On Tuesday afternoon, the Royal Spanish Football Federation (RFEF) announced that all of its football competitions have been suspended until November 6.

#1908. Middlesbrough FC and Sheffield United's rivals West Ham United confirm Scott Parker appointment

Sheffield United and Middlesbrough’s Championship rivals West Ham United have appointed Scott Parker as their new head coach.

Nuno Espirito Santo was relieved of his duties yesterday (November 3) with the Hammers sat eighth in the Championship table.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

West Ham have wasted little time replacing him, turning to former Hammers and England midfielder Parker.

The 46-year-old was most recently employed by Burnley and has also managed Fulham, AFC Bournemouth and Club Brugge. He is something of a Championship promotion specialist having led all of his English employers into the Premier League.

After taking the reins at the London Stadium, Parker said: “It is a very proud moment for me to step into this role and return to a club that means so much to me and my family. A lot of very fond memories of my time here - four years of probably the best football I played in my career.

“There was a warmth, a love, a feeling that I probably didn’t have anywhere else. There was something which stood out constantly and that was the relationship that I built up with the fanbase here. That rapport and respect, that I felt instantly.

“More than anything, this is an opportunity that I am very excited about. I feel privileged and honoured to be the guy that wants to lead us back to the Premier League and be the head coach of this football club at this moment in time.

“My energy levels, my enthusiasm, my desire, my passion - it’s absolutely running through and that's the feeling I had as soon as there was a conversation that this was possible. That's exactly why I'm here and why I want to be here.

“From my first calls with Karim [Virani] and Daniel [Křetínský], it was clear they have a shared vision and desire to return the club to the Premier League as quickly as possible. I share that ambition and I’m very confident we can achieve it.

“I’ve been in this division three times and I've got out of this division three times. This is a tough division, there is absolutely no denying it. And I will use every ounce of my experience, every ounce of my knowledge, to have an understanding of what we're going to need to bring consistency.

“And that's going to be the key word for all of us really. The consistency of what we do and the commitment levels that we go to will give us the best opportunity to get out of this division and be the team that we can be.”

West Ham sit level on points with ninth-placed Sheffield United and six points adrift of table-toppers Middlesbrough.

#1907. Monaco vs Nordsjaelland - prediction, team news, lineups

By Joel Lefevre | 02 Nov 2026 22:28, Last updated: 03 Nov 2026 14:51

Monaco will put their 100% record in the Conference League on the line Thursday as they return to the Principality to face Nordsjaelland at Stade Louis II.

After two matchdays, Les Monegasques are tied for first on points, having defeated Freiburg 3-0 the last time out, while Nordsjaelland sit 19th after a 2-2 draw with CSKA Sofia.

While their form has dropped a little domestically, Monaco have yet to falter in Europe, winning all four of their games in this competition so far.

However, Filipe Luis has seen his side go winless in their last three Ligue 1 affairs, netting just one goal over that stretch.

On the other hand, they sit third in the Conference League regarding average goals conceded per match (0.5), with only Brighton & Hove Albion and St. Truiden doing better (0).

At home, this team have been especially sharp defensively this season, conceding a goal or fewer in five of their six matches played at Stade Louis II across all competitions.

Monaco have netted three or more times in both of their home games in this competition so far and can stretch their unbeaten run in the League Phase of a European tournament to seven matchdays on Thursday.

This will mark the first time they face a side from Denmark in Europe, with Les Monegasques winning their only European match this decade against a Scandinavian opponent, blanking Bodo/Glimt 1-0 in Norway in last season’s Champions League.

They continue to seek that elusive first triumph in this edition of the Conference League, but Nordsjaelland have shown plenty of resilience in the League Phase this time around.

Jens Fonsskov Olsen’s men have come back from 1-0 down in both of their group matches to earn a point, putting them just a point above the knockout line heading into matchday three.

Thursday will be their first-ever meeting versus a Ligue 1 side in Europe, as they seek a first victory in the League Phase of this tournament since hammering Fenerbahce 6-1 in Denmark in 2023.

Their last away victory in this competition came in Slovakia that same year against Spartak Trnava (2-0), while they are currently on a four-game unbeaten run as the visitors across all competitions.

The Danes have never lost a Conference League affair in this portion of the competition when netting first, dropping points only once in that scenario.

On Thursday, they could suffer consecutive competitive defeats for the first time all season after losing 3-2 domestically versus Midtjylland on Sunday.

Hamstring injuries will likely keep Stanis Idumbo and Ansu Fati out of the Monaco fold on matchday three, while Eric Dier should be available after recently recovering from a thigh strain.

Paris Brunner has two goals for Les Monegasques in this phase of the tournament, with the German netting the winner against Freiburg on matchday two, while Lamine Camara and Ansu Fati also scored on that occasion.

An ankle issue may keep Noah Markmann on the Nordsjaelland sidelines for this one, Victor Nelsson has a sore shoulder, Tobias Salquist is dealing with fitness problems, while Jakob Busk and Souleymane Alio have knocks and Justin Janssen is suspended.

Ibrahim Adel netted a brace against Sofia, as he now leads the team in this competition thanks to those two strikes.

Hradecky; Vanderson, Teze, Dier, Mawissa; Zakaria, Camara; Minamino, Golovin, Detourbet; Brunner

Hansen; Acquah, Tuka, Norheim; Heyde, Brink, Rojkjaer, Lahteenmaki; Berthelsen, Lind, Adel

We expect the Danes to play conservatively and hang back, trying to hold off the Principality club throughout the match.

Monaco, however, are usually at their best offensively at home, and we believe they can dominate this game and eventually break down Nordsjaelland, who have not faced a side with as much attacking depth as Les Monegasques.

#1906. Michael Carrick insists he will NOT be sacked as Man United manager - despite side slipping closer to relegation zone after Chelsea defeat

By CHRIS WHEELER, NORTHERN SPORTS WRITER and KIERAN GILL, MAIL SPORT REPORTER

Published: 12:33 EDT, 31 October 2026 | Updated: 12:50 EDT, 31 October 2026

Michael Carrick believes he will cling onto his job as Manchester United head coach despite watching helplessly as his team slid closer towards the relegation zone at Chelsea.

Goals from Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer – who converted a penalty after Lisandro Martinez was sent off for picking up two yellow cards in the space of 82 seconds – consigned United to a 2-0 defeat at Stamford Bridge as they sank to 17th(check) place in the Premier League.

Earlier this week, Carrick was given more time by Old Trafford bosses to turn the club’s disastrous season around, but he is now without a win in nine games.

Asked if he will be in charge for Tuesday’s Champions League clash with Roma, he replied: ‘Yes. I'm just looking forward to getting the boys ready for the midweek now.’

The 20-time champions of England are faced with the humiliation of dropping into the bottom three and it was put to Carrick, a player and coach at United stretching back two decades, that seeing the club in such a position must be hurting him.

‘Yeah, pretty much exactly that,’ he said. ‘There is a lot of emotion. We're a great football club and we want to win football matches. Things have gone against us in a big way and unravelled quickly.

Man United are now without a win in nine games in all competitions, their longest such run since October-November 1988

‘There is no hiding from the fact that we haven't won enough games. There's no words that I'm going to explain to you now that makes it any different, it's not going to change it.

‘You can look at how far you can move up the league quite quickly if you win football matches. So that's the way it's got to be approached, for sure.’

Carrick insisted that he didn’t feel let down by Martinez, but did not even look at the Argentine as he left the pitch.

‘It has a major importance on the game. A huge moment. I think that is pretty obvious really,’ added Carrick. ‘The second goal and losing the man at that stage had a big influence on it, for sure.’

The United fans continued to give Carrick their support while once again turning on the club’s owners, the Glazer family and Sir Jim Ratcliffe, and director of football Jason Wilcox.

Meanwhile, Xabi Alonso admitted Estevao’s positive performance will give him a selection headache after the wonderkid showed Chelsea what they have been missing.

Morgan Rogers' brilliant solo goal set Chelsea on their way to victory

The 19-year-old Brazilian was handed his first Premier League start of the season and scored two disallowed goals for offside as well as creating several other opportunities.

‘He’s given me reasons (to pick him),’ said Alonso. ‘This is football and sometimes you don’t get what you want, but the best way to show it is not by being angry, it’s by being competitive and Este has done it really well.’

Alonso also hailed Romeo Lavia after the 22-year-old Belgian filled in for the unwell Jordan Henderson in midfield on short notice, and was arguably this game’s best performer.

‘From a midfielder point of view, for me it has been a top, top performance,’ Alonso said. ‘He's done so many things right. He’s been always connecting the defence with the attacker players, he's been able to switch the game, he's taken many right decisions, he's been very dynamic, competitive. I'm very happy for him and he deserves a huge recognition for his performance.’

#1904. Scunthorpe United next manager: Ex-Sheffield United and Barnsley FC men emerge as favourites

The favourites for the Scunthorpe United job - including ex-Sheffield United and Barnsley men

Former Sheffield United and Barnsley figures sit top of the list of favourites for the Scunthorpe United job.

Andy Butler, a former Doncaster Rovers stalwart, took charge of the Iron in 2024 and led the club to promotion from the National League North.

However, with the club hovering dangerously close to the bottom of the National League table, he was recently relieved of his duties.

A club spokesperson said: “Following a meeting of the borad of directors this morning, Scunthorpe United can confirm first-team manager Andy Butler has been relieved of his duties.

“Taking charge in May 2024, Butler steered the Iron to promotion from National League North in his first full campaign via the play-offs, before building on that momentum with a fifth-placed finish in the National League last season, narrowly missing out on back-to-back promotions after being edged out at the semi-final stage.

“As a defender, coming through the club’s academy system, Butler would go on to make 174 appearances in all competitions across three spells, scoring 15 goals with his final spell seeing him also return as first team coach, before transitioning into the manager’s role the following season.

“He took charge of 127 games for the club during his tenure, winning 62, emerging with a win rate of just under 50 per cent, and departs with our gratitude for his fantastic commitment, work rate and dedication during his whole time at Scunthorpe United, of which we undoubtedly know he gave his all.

“We wholeheartedly wish Andy the very best for the future, and look forward to watching him continue to grow and flourish in the game wherever it takes him next. The club will be making no further comment at this time, with further details will be provided in due course.”

#1903. Wayne Rooney slams Bruno Fernandes during Manchester United’s comeback win over Roma

Wayne Rooney criticised Bruno Fernandes for not running back during Manchester United’s remarkable comeback win over Roma in the Champions League.

United, enduring their worst start to a season since the 1980s, looked on course for their fifth defeat in six games as they trailed Roma 2-0 at Old Trafford.

Michael Carrick once again called on his players to produce an improved performance following a shocking run but the Red Devils fell behind inside 12 minutes.

The Serie A side took advantage of the acres of space left on the left-hand side by the out-of-position Diogo Dalot to take the lead through Matias Soule.

Sign up to our daily football newsletter, pick your team and get the latest news sent directly to your inbox every morning.

A similar gap in the Manchester United defence led to Roma’s second as Ayden Heaven was penalised for a handball blocking a shot and Donyell Malen converted from the penalty spot.

Dalot attracted much criticism for his part in Roma’s goals but Rooney was disappointed by Fernandes’ lack of effort in getting back, especially given his status as club captain.

It looked as though Fernandes’ woes would deepen when he missed a second-half penalty but he was offered a reprieve due to encroachment and tucked his second effort away.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

The goal, scored just before the hour mark, lifted Old Trafford but Manchester United still trailed with 10 minutes remaining.

In an extraordinary comeback that may have saved Carrick his job, Matheus Cunha then scored two goals in the space of three minutes to completely turn the game on its head.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

Cunha was shown a yellow card for jumping into the stands during his goal celebrations and received another shortly after, but United were still able to hold on with ten men to clinch a remarkable and unlikely victory.

Speaking on Amazon Prime at half-time, Rooney said the team were ‘shot to bits’ and was shocked by a lacklustre first-half display.

Asked whether the opening 45 minutes felt like a ‘new low’ for his former club, Rooney said: ‘Yeah, there’s been a lot of those lately but yeah, it did.

‘You’re in the Champions League and with all the talk and criticism the team have got, you were expecting some sort of reaction. There was nothing, absolutely nothing.

THAT DIDN'T TAKE LONG 😬United fall behind after just 11 minutes as Roma score through Matías Soulé 🇦🇷 pic.twitter.com/DtIOFJYZ6D

‘Roma took the ball and were more aggressive, no one on the United team put a tackle in. They were really struggling down the left-hand side.

‘You just want to see something, some sort of fight and passion and desire to win the football game but there was nothing.

‘For the first goal, if you’re playing in a system, when Dalot goes higher, Bruno should go into that position. He has to run back, you’re the captain of the football club, run back and take responsibility.

‘You’re a team and you need to play as a team. If a teammate is out of position, even if you don’t want to be there or run back, you have to run back.

‘I feel so sorry for the fans because they don’t know what to do. They’ve not been in this position for years, they don’t know whether to get behind the team or to get on their backs. I feel so sorry for them.

‘The team have just run out of ideas. There’s no confidence or belief, the team is shot to bits.’

Reacting to Manchester United’s comeback win after full-time, Rooney added: ‘The second-half was amazing, they were front-footed and they deserved to win the game in the end.

‘The first half was terrible but we saw the passion and fight we wanted in the second half. The crowd got right behind the team and you felt like they could go on to win the game.’

Fellow England legend Alan Shearer, meanwhile, said: ‘Great credit to Michael Carrick because they were down and out at half-time.

‘They were all over the place in that first-half, and he had to change and tweak things.

‘I said what can he do, I didn’t know where he would start, and he must have started in the dressing room, and pointing at a few people telling them to be brave and courageous and move the ball quicker.

‘They did all those things in the second half and got their reward by getting their win.’

Manchester United, sitting just 17th in the Premier League, face Unai Emery’s Aston Villa at Old Trafford this weekend.

#1902. Cardiff City vs West Ham United - prediction, team news, lineups

By Ben Sully | 02 Nov 2026 22:36, Last updated: 03 Nov 2026 14:59

West Ham United will be looking to bounce back from consecutive defeats when they head to South Wales for Wednesday's Championship clash against Cardiff City.

The managerless Hammers head into the midweek round of fixtures in eighth position, while Cardiff are currently sitting in 17th spot in the Championship table.

Cardiff, who won promotion from League One last term, are sitting five points above the drop zone after winning three, drawing five and losing five of their 13 league games this season.

The Bluebirds recently enjoyed a three-game unbeaten run that saw them record home wins against Watford and Birmingham City, on either side of an away draw against Middlesbrough.

However, their encouraging run of form was brought to a disappointing end by Saturday's 3-0 loss against Wolverhampton Wanderers at Molineux, extending their wait for their first away win of the season.

Having mustered just two points from seven road trips, Brian Barry-Murphy's side will be looking forward to returning to the Cardiff City Stadium, especially as they are one of four teams yet to lose a Championship home game this term (W3, D3).

In fact, they have won each of their last three home games, scoring nine goals and conceding on just two occasions in that winning run.

They will be hoping to produce another strong performance in front of their supporters in their first meeting with West Ham since picking up a 2-0 victory in March 2019 - a result that ended a seven-game losing run in head-to-head encounters.

West Ham may be sitting inside the top eight, but after the Hammers won just two of their last six matches (D2, L2), Nuno Espirito Santo was given the boot on Tuesday morning.

The Hammers are in need of a confidence boost after losing back-to-back league matches for the first time since being relegated from the Premier League, and managerial favourite Scott Parker could soon provide that amid suggestions that he will soon replace Nuno.

West Ham shipped three goals in the first half of the 3-2 loss against the Saints, before they fell to a 3-1 defeat to West Bromwich Albion at the weekend, leaving them four points adrift of automatic promotion.

The visitors can at least take comfort from the fact that they will head on their travels with the only unbeaten away record in the Championship after recording three wins and three draws from their six road trips.

In fact, they are looking to claim a third consecutive away win without conceding after beating Lincoln City 6-0 and Swansea City 1-0 in their last two away assignments.

The visitors certainly possess the firepower to take three points from Wednesday's away, having racked up 33 goals in 13 league games this term - at least three more than any other side ahead of the midweek round of fixtures.

Cardiff are experiencing a defensive injury crisis, with Barry-Murphy unable to call upon the suspended Gabriel Osho and the injured trio of Dylan Lawlor, Callum Chambers and Krystian Bielik.

Will Fish is a doubt after sustaining a hamstring problem against Wolves, while Perry Ng may have to battle through his own fitness issues to help his side in Wednesday's fixture.

Midfielder Alex Robertson is also an injury concern after being taken off in Saturday's defeat with an Achilles problem.

As for the visitors, Konstantinos Mavropanos will miss a second straight game with a knee injury he sustained in the defeat to Southampton.

Interim coaches Mark Noble, Steve Potts and Gerard Prenderville are also without Venezuela international Keiber Lamadrid, who has not featured in any of the last eight matchday squads due to a knee problem.

The West Ham coaching team could make several changes to their starting lineup, with Joel Veltman, Tomas Soucek, Manor Solomon and Taty Castellanos among those in contention to feature at the Cardiff City Stadium.

Trott; Kpakio, Ng, Bagan, Scanlon; Colwill, Turnbull; Tanner, Moylan, Ashford; Salech

West Ham United possible starting lineup:

Hermansen; Walker-Peters, Veltman, Kilman, Morato; Bowen, Soucek, Engels, Solomon; Kante; Taty

West Ham may be reeling from back-to-back defeats, but they head into the midweek matchday as the league's highest scorers, and we think their attacking strength will be decisive, especially as Cardiff are experiencing a defensive injury crisis.

#1901. Carlos Baleba injury update after Manchester United’s win over Roma

Michael Carrick has provided an update on Carlos Baleba after the midfielder was forced off during Manchester United’s Champions League win over Roma.

The Cameroon international made a promising run into the Roma box shortly after half-time but then pulled up just as it looked like he would get a shot away.

Baleba immediately grabbed his hamstring and it soon became clear that the medical team would not be able to prolong his evening.

The 22-year-old was in tears as he made his way off the pitch and Carrick said the injury ‘doesn’t look great’ in his post-match press conference after an extraordinary 3-2 comeback victory.

Sign up to our daily football newsletter, pick your team and get the latest news sent directly to your inbox every morning.

‘I haven’t got any more news on Carlos at this stage but obviously it’s his hamstring and we’ll have to assess it more in the next few days,’ Carrick said.

‘Initially it doesn’t look great but I haven’t got much more to give you than that in terms of a timeframe or anything.’

Following Carrick’s comments, former Manchester United midfielder Nicky Butt said on Amazon Prime: ‘It looks like Baleba will be out for a while now and that won’t help United because they don’t seem to be able to get a settled team out on the pitch.’

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Baleba has made an unconvincing start to his Old Trafford career following a £70m summer move from Brighton and now looks set for a significant spell on the sidelines.

Manchester United have endured their worst start to a season in 40 years and looked on course for a fourth successive defeat as Roma stormed into a 2-0 lead at Old Trafford.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

Matias Soule put the Italians ahead on 11 minutes and Donyell Malen doubled Roma’s lead five minutes later from the penalty spot after Ayden Heaven blocked a shot with his arm.

LOOK AT THOSE SCENES 🤩From two goals down, Matheus Cunha completes Man Utd's comeback as they defeat Roma 3-2! 👏 pic.twitter.com/EwhKx1rNkY

The Red Devils were once again booed off at half-time but improved drastically after the break, finding a lifeline just before the hour mark through Bruno Fernandes’ retaken penalty.

Carrick’s side still trailed with ten minutes remaining but Matheus Cunha then scored two goals in six minutes to turn the game around and potentially save his manager’s job.

‘It was a good night,’ Carrick said. ‘I have to give a lot of credit to the players for starters, showing that character and quality when we needed it.

‘This place does incredible things, magical things and we spoke about it at half-time. I thought we grew into it a little bit first half after giving away the goals too easily.

‘We spoke at half-time about how this place can change, it only takes one moment. The boys made every little bit of every little opportunity really and were fantastic in the end.’

Asked what the remarkable comeback win means for Manchester United, Carrick added: ‘It’s a win for us as a football club.

‘To see the supporters go home happy is what we live for, to give them performances and nights like this so they can get back again energised.

‘As a team, we’ve shown a lot of character to weather what we’ve had to. You find out a lot about each other.

‘The players will find out things about me, I certainly do about them and their character, what it means to them and what they’re prepared to put in.

‘Tonight was right at that moment. It depends what happens next, we’ve got to make the most of it, we’ve got to move forward but I’m feeling a lot better about things tonight.’

Manchester United, now 17th in both the Premier League and Champions League, face Aston Villa at Old Trafford on Sunday.

Ramazani’s loan deal contains a mandatory buy obligation, therefore the Belgian does not have a future at Elland Road.

In September, ex-Whites winger Jermaine Pennant said: “He can [prove Leeds wrong]. I think he was very important in the Championship run when he was there. He’s a decent player, a good player, and he just needed game time.

“It’s very difficult when you haven’t got bags and bags of game time to really get into a rhythm. We all need that. It doesn’t matter how good you are - if you’re playing little dribs and drabs of games here and there, you’re not going to be at your peak. You need continuity of games.

“With a new lease of life and a fresh start, playing week in, week out, I’m sure he can prove the doubters wrong at Leeds and go, ‘Look, this is what you maybe could have had’. But Leeds have got top players as well now, and they’ve invested well.”

United’s worst start to a season since the 1980s looked set to take another blow as Roma stormed into a 2-0 lead at Old Trafford.

Matias Soule took advantage of an alarming amount of room near the United box to put the Italians ahead inside 12 minutes.

United were still heading for another defeat and Michael Carrick for the sack until Matheus Cunha scored twice late on to complete a memorable European comeback.

Manchester United legend Schmeichel says he felt ‘so sad’ at half-time but believes the game changed upon the introduction of summer signing Tielemans.

The Belgian midfielder replaced the injured Carlos Baleba shortly after half-time and proceeded to ‘change the game’, according to Schmeichel.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘At half-time I was so sad about what I had seen in that first 45 minutes because it was bad, it was bad. And then Carlos Baleba goes off injured early in the second half and you’re thinking, this can’t get any worse.

‘But Youri Tielemans came on and he changed the game. That’s the best I’ve seen him play for Man United and I’m so pleased for him.

‘But they did in the second half. The tone was set with Carlos Baleba. It was so unfortunate he got an injury for it but that was a spark.

‘Anytime there’s a difficult situation or pre-match team talk, it’s going to be look what you do when you apply yourselves in that manner then you are impossible to live with.’

#1898. England captain Harry Kane reveals whether he would swap Ballon d'Or for Champions League trophy

By Ben Sully | 02 Nov 2026 23:34, Last updated: 03 Nov 2026 04:09

Bayern Munich forward Harry Kane has admitted he would trade his Ballon d'Or for Champions League glory.

Last week, Kane became the first Englishman to win the prestigious Ballon d'Or award after fending off competition from Real Madrid's Kylian Mbappe and Barcelona's Lamine Yamal.

Kane was recognised after scoring 61 goals in 51 competitive matches for Bayern last term, as well as netting six goals in England's World Cup campaign.

The 33-year-old has won multiple individual honours throughout his career and has claimed five trophies during his time in Germany, including two Bundesliga titles.

However, like Mbappe and Yamal, he is still waiting to get his prize on the biggest club trophy in European football, the Champions League.

Kane, who is set to lead the Bayern line against Atletico Madrid on Tuesday, provided an honest answer when asked which trophy he would choose between the Ballon d'Or and the Champions League.

"Team trophies are why we play football, the team aspect of our sport is really, really important," Kane told reporters on Monday.

"The Ballon d'Or last week was one of the best feelings I've had in my life and my career.

"But to have moments with the team, celebrations with the club, to be able to lift the Champions League with Bayern would be an incredible feeling.

"I would choose the Champions League, but I have the opportunity to do both - let's see what happens.

"The Ballon d'Or is a highlight, it puts me on an even bigger level, but you want to have these big finals, the Champions League, having that feeling of emotion with your teammates as well."

Tuesday's Champions League fixture between Bayern and Atletico will take place at the ground where Kane came closest to winning the European Cup.

The striker played the full duration of Tottenham Hotspur's 2-0 defeat to Liverpool in the 2018-19 Champions League final at the Metropolitano.

Kane has made two semi-final appearances since joining Bayern, including a narrow 6-5 aggregate defeat against Paris Saint-Germain in last season's Champions League.

Vincent Kompany's side certainly has the talent to make another deep run in the competition and is seen as one of the teams that could seriously challenge for the trophy.

However, their chances of winning may depend on the form and fitness of key players, like Kane, Luis Diaz, Michael Olise, and Joshua Kimmich.

Kane will most likely need to produce a similar European campaign to last season's return of 14 goals in 13 matches, including six goals in five knockout-round appearances.

Diego Moreira wrote himself into AC Milan history with three contributions on his derby debut last night and it’s clear that this may be the start.

Before the game, Moreira spoke with confidence about the derby, even though he’d never played in the game before. Indeed, even before a ball was kicked, he gave a reason for the Milan fans to appreciate him more: “We’re fired up, I’d die for my team and to play these games, we’re fired up.”

With two assists and a free-kick, then, it’s clear that he wasn’t mincing his words when he said that and he’s offered another comment that fans will get behind.

Speaking to Milan TV after the game, via MilanNews, the Belgian made a statement of intent for last night and the future. After his performance, he’s certainly able to make these comments and it shows he already understands what it means to the Rossoneri.

“I’m very happy with these three points. Today was very special for me and for the team because it’s a derby, and derbies aren’t played, they’re won. We must stay focused and stay united, because we know that every match is important.

He’s already – rightly – becoming a fan favourite.

#1894. 'It was a little bit of a gamble' - Lukas Nmecha opens up on decision to join Leeds United in 2025

Lukas Nmecha has described his decision to join Leeds United in the summer of 2025 as “a little bit of a gamble”.

The 27-year-old forward was the first signing of Leeds’ post-promotion recruitment drive, arriving on a free transfer from Wolfsburg to bolster Daniel Farke’s attack.

He has since scored seven goals across 47 appearances, spending the bulk of his time at Elland Road as a back-up option behind Dominic Calvert-Lewin.

In an appearance on The Official Leeds United Podcast, Nmecha has lifted the lid on his return to British shores with Leeds.

He said: “Doors open and doors close - and it just kind of pointed towards Leeds. I spoke to Daniel, he was very convincing, obviously. [He said] just that it’s a massive club, a great opportunity for Premier League football. He’s obviously watched my journey and sees that I can help the team.

“It was a little bit of a gamble, I would say, to go to a newly-promoted side. But with it being Leeds, the history of the club and everything that Leeds was, it kind of made it a little bit easier for me to make that choice. I needed a change, because I’d had a such a tough time with injuries previously. It kind of just opened itself up.

“When you’re a free agent, it’s a lot easier, let’s say. I could have stayed in Germany, I could have stayed at my club there.”

Nmecha is a product of Manchester City’s youth system and was exposed to senior EFL football during loan spells at Preston North End and Middlesbrough.

He settled back in Germany, the country of his birth, when he joined Wolfsburg from Manchester City in 2021. The frontman started strongly and broke into the Germany squad, only to find himself hampered by injury in the latter stages of his Volkswagen Arena stay.

Nmecha said: “As soon as I entered training, I thought this level is quite similar to where I’d come from. But as soon as we entered the game, it was a completely different thing.

“I think Germany and England are very different. Even the players in terms of character, they’re a lot more, I’ll say just vicious. I like it. We’ve got good players for that as well.

“We’ve got Ethan [Ampadu], where he’s the nicest guy ever, and then on a matchday it’s like ‘what’s going on here?’.”

#1892. Fenerbahce vs Liverpool - prediction, team news, lineups

By Anthony Nolan | 02 Nov 2026 23:58, Last updated: 04 Nov 2026 12:48

Fighting to maintain their 100% start in the Champions League's league-phase, Liverpool will travel to face Fenerbahce at Sukru Saracoglu Stadium on Wednesday.

The Yellow Canaries are in dire form ahead of this high-profile clash, and the Reds will be hoping to bounce back from defeat last time out.

Fenerbahce are currently under the leadership of interim manager Dirk Kuyt, a familiar face to Liverpool fans, following Ismail Kartal's resignation last month.

The Dutchman spent six years at Anfield, scoring 71 goals across 285 appearances, but will be vying to end his former club's continental winning streak.

Kuyt took the reins on October 28 after the Yellow Canaries were downed 2-1 by bitter rivals Galatasaray, but fell to a 2-1 defeat of his own against Goztepe on Saturday.

While the boss is waiting for an inaugural positive result, Fenerbahce are also searching for their first win in this season's Champions League, having drawn 1-1 with Roma and 2-2 with Slavia Prague either side of a 6-0 demolition by Aston Villa.

While the hosts come into Wednesday's showdown as the underdogs, fans will cling to the fact that the Istanbul club have only tasted defeat in one of their last five home matches as a reason for optimism.

Meanwhile, Liverpool seem to have found their feet under Andoni Iraola, though they will need to show character to recover after a disappointing defeat at the weekend.

In the aftermath of their 3-0 loss to Manchester City on October 11, the Reds racked up five consecutive wins across all competitions, including a 2-0 victory over high-flying Brighton & Hove Albion and a penalty shootout triumph against Chelsea in the EFL Cup.

Iraola's side also collected six points from six in the Champions League during that run, thanks to a 6-3 win over LASK and a dramatic 4-3 comeback against Villarreal on October 20.

However, Arsenal claimed their first league success at Anfield for 14 years on Sunday, beating the Merseysiders 1-0 in controversial fashion, a result that perhaps laid Liverpool's limitations against deep blocks bare.

That being said, Wednesday's visitors are undefeated away from home throughout 2026-27, winning four times and drawing once, scoring 13 goals in the process.

Already in a strong position - third in the Champions League table with nine points - another victory would solidify the Premier League giants' spot in the top eight as the rankings begin to take shape.

Fenerbahce will be lighter in defence than ideal without centre-backs Jayden Oosterwolde and Kojo Peprah Oppong, the former with a hamstring injury and the latter having been forced off against Goztepe.

Ex-Man City star Nathan Ake is also a doubt due to a muscle problem, so Archie Brown and Milan Skriniar could start at the heart of the hosts' defence, flanked by Mert Muldur and Munir Levent Mercan.

Elsewhere, attacking midfielder Marco Asensio was revealed to require knee surgery last month, though Mason Greenwood, Irfan Can Kahveci and Oguz Aydin should be ready to operate behind striker Romelu Lukaku.

As for Liverpool, the Reds were dealt a fresh blow on Tuesday with the news that Ryan Gravenberch will miss the game due to a heel injury.

Centre-back Giovanni Leoni remains sidelined as he closes in on a return from an anterior cruciate ligament injury, while right-back options Conor Bradley and Jeremie Frimpong are out due to respective knee and hamstring injuries.

In their absence, Ronald Araujo could continue on the right of the back four, alongside Jeremy Jacquet, Virgil van Dijk and Kostas Tsimikas.

At the opposite end of the pitch, Lewis Koumas may come into the XI for striker Alexander Isak, with Hugo Ekitike working through his rehabilitation following the Achilles injury he suffered in April.

Ederson; Muldur, Brown, Skriniar, Mercan; Kante, Guendouzi; Greenwood, Kahveci, Aydin; Lukaku

Alisson; Araujo, Jacquet, Van Dijk, Tsimikas; Szoboszlai, Mac Allister; Ngumoha, Wirtz, Barcola; Koumas

Fenerbahce have been in poor form lately, but they will be determined to deliver a competitive performance in front of an intense home crowd.

Liverpool should have enough to come out on top despite the pressure applied by their opponents, though they are unlikely to keep a clean sheet in Istanbul.

#1891. Full throttle Brighton have the depth, quality and guile to hang in there with Arsenal and Man City, writes JACK GAUGHAN, as individual mistakes haunt Enzo Maresca's men in latest defeat

Published: 13:16 EDT, 31 October 2026 | Updated: 14:38 EDT, 31 October 2026

A game condensed into 15 seconds. Jeremy Doku loses possession on the touchline but won't have that, thundering into a tackle to recollect and then sets off beating two men. He seems in the mood for destruction.

An expectant Etihad is up, the Premier League's trickiest winger cutting loose and Manchester City are in. One calm final ball and an equaliser is on.

Doku tries to find a lurking Erling Haaland, or at least it appears so, because the pass is so bad that Brighton are already storming upfield themselves.

Around 15 minutes after that, Fabian Hurzeler is roaring at his bench. He is chest bumping substitutes and backroom staff with defiant pride, vindication of the words spoken about seeking revenge in the immediately aftermath of losing on penalties here in the cup a matter of days ago.

Brighton stayed in Manchester after Wednesday night and Hurzeler spent that time plotting, organising the battle plan to topple league leaders who have been fallible defensively under Enzo Maresca this season but are producing scintillating attacking moments.

Hurzeler leaves the north west following a little getaway at the Lowry Hotel having drawn and won against City over the course of two 90 minutes. His stock is soaring, his side a fascination and the faint chorus of 'we're gonna win the league' from the away end might just grow a little louder over the coming weeks if they can keep this up.

Manchester City were turned over by Brighton to make it back-to-back league defeats

Yasin Ayari's first half goal was all that was required for Brighton to leave as the victors

Brighton's manager peeled away from the group as they enjoyed being serenaded by the away end, instead sharing a moment with match winner Yasin Ayari, whose third goal of the campaign owed much to the quick thinking of Lewis Dunk to restart play from a dead ball with haste and the individual mistake of Matheus Nunes, failing to clear Diego Gomez's cross. Ayari and Dunk were those to miss from the spot in the Carabao Cup.

'Wednesday was brutal,' Hurzeler said. 'We promised ourselves that we won't have the same feeling.

'We created energy, positivity. How the players stuck together and built the connection through the four days is really impressive.'

Hurzeler discussed the virtue of luck here in midweek and City's was out on the day, now only two points between the teams after consecutive league defeats.

The joyous, and somewhat knowing, celebrations between staff members shone a light on the preparation that went into this result and how it quite clearly serves as a warning shot.

Brighton showed across four days that they have the depth, quality and wherewithal to be at least be considered strong enough to stay close with City and Arsenal. More specifically, they showed on Saturday that they can mix the way in which they play, adept to altering circumstances.

Their full throttle movement in midfield before half time confused their City counterparts, the home midfield discombobulated – arms pointing frantically, basic organisational shouts becoming more hurried – and that filtered through to other areas of the pitch.

Maresca was seem directing Elliot Anderson on who to follow and there were occasionally some befuddled looks.

Gianluigi Donnarumma was full stretch but could do nothing about Ayari's pinpoint strike

Enzo Maresca was in disbelief as his side spurned numerous opportunities to score a goal

Out of possession, home wingers were often full backs and full backs were often stationed as wingers as they followed their men, with Brighton happily piercing through any gaps. For a while, City were taken for a ride on the waltzers.

And then later on, when City pushed and pushed, Brighton went to a back six and contained.

They still gave up a number of very presentable chances, City failing to convert five of those – most notably two for Iliman Ndiaye and Nico O'Reilly's late header – but the rearguard action is proof that they own the minerals to enjoy more days like these before May is done.

Brighton managed to create four big chances from just nine touches inside the City box, indicating that once Maresca's midfield is breached then they are too easy to play through.

The Italian – who dropped Marc Guehi - is concerned by the volume of individual mistakes at both ends of the pitch after the Nunes error.

'We're probably conceding [too many] silly goals,' Maresca said, with the defeat at Aston Villa also pockmarked by them.

'We created enough but unfortunately didn't score. For sure we are not happy. Nobody is happy when we lose. But we were aware that we weren't going to win all the games.'

Maresca said he had not reviewed two penalty appeals for handball and the decision to award a free kick in the build up to Brighton's 11th-minute goal.

Brighton showed enough quality this week to suggest they can hang with Arsenal and Man City

Man City (4-2-3-1): Donnarumma 6; Nunes 5, Khusanov 6, Dias 6, Gvardiol 5 (Foden 79); Anderson 7, Bouaddi 6 (Cherki 55, 7); Ndiaye 6 (Allan 79), Fernandez 5 (O’Reilly 65), Doku 5; Haaland 5.

Brighton (4-2-3-1): Verbruggen 7; Costinha 7, Vuskovic 7, Dunk 8, Boscagli 6 (Hadjam 64, 6); Gross 6, Chema 6 (Wieffer 64, 6); Gomez 7 (Rutter 84), Ayari 7, De Cuyper 7 (Yalcouye 72); Kostoulas 6 (Hinshelwood 72, 6).

Left back Josko Gvardiol was largely tucking in to become a third centre half and Nunes told to occupy the sort of attacking positions that the Croatian usually devours.

And interestingly, were City to win their appeal against the guilty verdicts – the sanctions for which would likely spell relegation – then left back is an area they would be expected to look at.

Sources have indicated that Bournemouth's Adrien Truffert is one potential target who was scouted extensively last season before City decided against bolstering their ranks in that area in the summer.

Rayan Ait-Nouri is looking to leave, while any signings in that position would present intrigue as to how Gvardiol and O'Reilly are used in future.

#1885. Jesus Owono’s team-mate defends goalkeeper after death of Jesus de Miguel

Andorra star Lautaro Spatz has offered his ‘sincere condolences’ to Jesus de Miguel’s loved ones following the footballer’s tragic death, while also sharing a message of support for his team-mate Jesus Owono.

Tenerife centre-forward De Miguel sustained severe head and chest injuries following a heavy collision with Andorra goalkeeper Owono, who was subsequently shown a red card for the challenge.

Owono had raced out of his his goal in an attempt to clear the ball when the deadly coming together occurred in the closing stages of Monday’s Spanish second-division contest.

It quickly became apparent that De Miguel required urgent medical attention and while the striker’s condition was described as ‘stable but serious’ after he was carried from the field and taken to hospital, his condition quickly deteriorated.

Sign up to our daily football newsletter, pick your team and get the latest news sent directly to your inbox every morning.

A heartbreaking statement on Tenerife’s social media pages on Tuesday morning confirmed that De Miguel has succumbed to his injuries, devastating news that has rocked the footballing world to its core.

Players and organisations have united in support of De Miguel’s friends and family in the hours that have followed, with heartfelt tributes shared and moments of silence observed across the globe.

Meanwhile, the Spanish FA postponed all Copa del Rey and Copa de la Reina matches that were scheduled to take place on Tuesday to allow for time to ‘grieve over this sad loss’.

It has also been announced that Tenerife’s Segunda Division clash with Granada – which had been due to kick off on Saturday – will be moved to a later date.

‘Following the tragic news of the death of Jesus de Miguel, a player for CD Tenerife, the LaLiga Hypermotion match between Granada CF and Tenerife, scheduled for Saturday, November 7th at the Nuevo Los Carmenes stadium, has been postponed,’ read a statement on Granada’s official website.

‘The new date for the match is pending confirmation. The club reiterates its deepest condolences to the loved ones of Jesus de Miguel, as well as to the entire CD Tenerife family, sending them all strength and encouragement in these difficult times.’

Con el corazón encogido. Impresiona esto. Cientos de aficionados están despidiendo en estos momentos a Jesús de Miguel junto a la puerta 9 del Heliodoro. #jesusdemiguel pic.twitter.com/9aoHdlAh87

Reuters reported on Tuesday that police in Spain had launched an investigation for possible involuntary manslaughter in the wake of De Miguel’s death.

Under Spanish law, any death deemed to be non-natural automatically triggers a judicial inquiry.

However, criminal proceedings against Andorra shot-stopper Owono are ‘very unlikely’, according to Santa Cruz de Tenerife chief prosecutor Jose Luis Sanchez-Jauregui.

🖤 A moment of silence in memory of @CDTOficial forward Jesús de Miguel Alameda and the victims of last week’s train accident in Spain. pic.twitter.com/o1e4bQRX3E

Owono is yet to make a public statement in relation to the incident and Venancio Tomas Ndong Micha, the president of the Equatorial Guinean Football Federation, has said the 25-year-old was ‘experiencing profound distress and anguish’ following the news of De Miguel’s death.

Spanish radio station COPE reported that a section of supporters inside the Heliodoro Rodriguez Lopez stadium had yelled ‘murderer’ at Owono, appearing to blame the goalkeeper for the tragic circumstances that played out.

But Andorra defender Spatz, who helped carry De Miguel off the pitch on a stretcher, took to Instagram to defend Owono on Tuesday night, insisting his team-mate would ‘never intentionally hurt anyone’.

‘There are moments when football stops making sense. Moments that stay with you forever and make you realise just how fragile life can be. What we have experienced is something none of us will ever forget. A tragedy that has left us completely heartbroken, speechless and with a sadness that is difficult to put into words,’ Spatz wrote.

‘First of all, I would like to express my most sincere condolences and send all my love to the family, friends and loved ones of Jesus, as well as to the entire Chicharrera fanbase and the football community.

‘Since yesterday, the entire FC Andorra squad has been shocked, devastated and deeply affected by what has happened. It is a tragedy that we could never have imagined experiencing on a football pitch.

‘I would also like to say a few words about my team-mate, goalkeeper and friend, who has been deeply affected by what happened. Those of us who know him know what kind of person he is, how much he is suffering at this moment, and that he would never intentionally hurt anyone.

‘In football, accidents happen, but nobody could ever imagine that one of them could lead to such tragic consequences.’

The Andorra centre-back added: ‘Today, football doesn’t matter. All that matters is standing together in grief, showing the utmost respect and sending all our strength to the family and everyone suffering from this terrible loss.

‘Rest in peace, Demi. [broken heart emoji].’

A separate message on Andorra’s official website read: ‘We are deeply moved by the death of Jesus de Miguel. The first thing we want to do is extend our most sincere condolences to his family, CD Tenerife, and all those close to him.

‘We know that no words can ease such pain, but we want them to know that we stand by their side and deeply share their sadness.

‘We also want to extend all our support to CD Tenerife, its players, its technical staff, its workers, and its fans. We are deeply affected by what has happened and share the pain the club is experiencing. From the very first moment, we have been in contact with them and are at their disposal for anything they may need.

‘Likewise, we are in contact with LaLiga, the Government of Andorra, and the relevant organizations to offer all our collaboration and the necessary support during these very difficult times. We have also requested the postponement of the next match against RCD Mallorca, as we believe these are moments of profound grief in which respect and support for all those affected must prevail.

‘What has happened has had a great emotional impact on our players, the technical staff, and everyone who is part of FC Andorra. These are especially tough times for everyone, and we want to ensure that no one has to face them alone. For this reason, the club is providing psychological support to all those who need it.

‘We are a team, on and off the field. Now more than ever, we must stand together, support each other, and take care of one another.

‘All of football and all of sports are in mourning. These are moments of profound sadness in which we must remain united, support those who need it most, and show the utmost respect.

‘Our most sincere condolences to Jesús’s family and to everyone at CD Tenerife. Rest in peace, Jesus.’
