#1884. Unbeaten run, a rare free-kick and more: All the key stats from AC Milan 3-1 Inter

As is often the case with the derby win, there were a lot of fun facts and stats to delve into after the full-time whistle, including a free-kick rarity from Diego Moreira.

Many headed into the Derby della Madonnina with a lot of worry considering Inter’s strong start to the season, as well as Milan’s mid-week defeat to Bologna. However, it turned out to be a great evening for the Rossoneri, who clinched all three points in a 3-1 win.

Diego Moreira played a key role in the success, bagging one goal and two assists, while Ruben Amorim got his tactics right as well. In short, it was just what they needed and as is often the case after a huge win, a lot of fun stats emerged afterwards.

Starting with the general stats, it’s clear that Milan made the most of their chances with a 0.66 xG and three goals scored. Moreira’s free-kick obviously didn’t yield a high xG, nor did Adrien Rabiot’s tidy effort, and Christian Pulisic’s header wasn’t super easy to pull off.

Inter had some good chances from close range, parried by Mike Maignan, so that is probably why their xG is higher. Alessandro Bastoni’s header was also an easy one, unlike Pulisic’s, but it was nice to see Milan be the efficient team for once.

The possession is linked to the above, really, as Milan sat back a lot after scoring their goals. Tactically, they played it to perfection and Inter didn’t really create much with all that possession in the end.

This deserves a section of its own because Milan’s recent record in the derby is truly amazing. After losing six games on the trot, the Rossoneri have certainly turned things around with six wins in the last eight encounters and no defeats!

Now the Inter fans can feel some of the pain that we experienced a while back… It’s not just that the Nerazzurri as a club have been really poor against Milan, it’s also that Cristian Chivu has failed completely.

Winning trophies is the most important thing, he’s absolutely right, but there is no question that the derby record is bothering him. As reported by Opta, he’s only the third manager to lose his first three derbies after Leonardo (2009-2011) and Massimo Giacomini (1979-1980).

Like we said at the start, a lot of fun facts emerged from the win last night and giving each of them a section would be a little silly. From a rare free-kick goal in the derby to a midfielder in red-hot form, we have listed them below.

Moreira’s free-kick: Since Opta started collecting the stats in 2004-05, Milan have only scored three direct free-kick goals against Inter in all competitions, with Moreira’s being the latest one. Pirlo (2007) and Theo Hernandez (2025) were the first two.

Pulisic’s speedy start: Pulisic’s goal is the fastest Milan have scored in a league derby against Inter since the 2010-11 season, when Alexandre Pato found the back of the net after a mere 43 seconds. Talk about getting off the right foot.

Rabiot’s goal contributions: Rabiot has become the third Milan midfielder to have at least one goal contribution in five consecutive league games since 2004-05, following in the footsteps of Hakan Calhanoglu (in 2020) and Ricky Kaka (2004 and 2008).

#1883. Michael Carrick spotted ordering Man Utd star to leave the pitch after Roma win

Michael Carrick was spotted telling Matheus Cunha to leave the pitch immediately after the final whistle in Manchester United’s comeback victory over AS Roma.

The Brazil international scored twice as United fought back from two goals behind to win 3-2 at Old Trafford on Tuesday night. After Bruno Fernandes’ penalty, Cunha pounced on a defensive error to level the contest before firing home a winner on 86 minutes.

The former Wolves star removed his shirt and leapt into the crowd in celebration, earning himself a booking. A second yellow followed in injury time for an overzealous challenge as United held on.

Cunha slowly trudged around the perimeter of the pitch as he made his way to the tunnel, desperate to see the final minutes of the match play out.

Sign up to our daily football newsletter, pick your team and get the latest news sent directly to your inbox every morning.

He briefly disappeared down the tunnel before reemerging to join the post-match celebrations after the final whistle had blown.

But TV cameras picked up Carrick appearing to tell his player to go straight to the dressing room with Cunha seen pleading with his boss on the pitch. The unhappy Brazilian eventually made his way back down the tunnel, flanked by a club official.

IFAB rules, which also govern Champions League matches, state that a player who has been sent off ‘must leave the vicinity of the field of play and the technical area’ and cannot return, even after the full-time whistle has been blown.

Cunha is set to miss United’s next Champions League match away to Sporting CP on 25 November.

Victory handed Carrick a lifeline with United’s focus now shifting to Aston Villa on Sunday.

#1881. Buoyant Bairns are a different beast this year after summer rebuild... and that spells bad news for Celtic

Published: 15:07 EDT, 31 October 2026 | Updated: 15:14 EDT, 31 October 2026

Was there ever any doubt that Falkirk would eventually get over their sticky start to the season and begin making their way up the Premiership table?

Well yes, actually. Quite a lot of it, in fact.

A mass exodus over the summer saw 17 depart, including a host of key players who helped the side upset the odds last season by making the top six.

Barney Stewart and Calvin Miller left for West Bromwich Albion and Hearts respectively – both bringing in a tidy profit for the club in the process – with Dylan Tait making the move to Premiership rivals Dundee United and Ben Broggio going back to Aston Villa after an impressive loan spell north of the border.

The excellent defensive pair of Filip Lissah and Kyrell Wilson also returned to parent club Swansea, with the former now an automatic starter for the promotion-chasers while the latter is plying his trade in the Belgian top flight with Gent.

Replacing that lot was rightly viewed by most as a near-impossible task. Top six? Forget it.

And results over the first couple of months suggested that survival might have to be the main priority for this year.

Falkirk striker Jacob Murrell has scored four goals in his last five Premiership games

But as we enter November, it appears as though those fears were unfounded. We should have known better than to doubt Falkirk at all.

It’s taken a while – certainly longer than manager John McGlynn would have liked – but his new-look squad are finally starting to find their feet.

Winning three on the bounce in the Premiership is no small feat. Indeed, for all the plaudits Falkirk rightly earned on their march to the top half last season, that was something they failed to achieve.

And the most encouraging aspect of this mini-run is that they’ve managed to do it in a very un-Falkirk way.

Motherwell aside, Falkirk were the most entertaining side to watch in the top flight last term, just as they were as they swept away the opposition in League One and the Championship on their incredible journey up the divisions.

It’s not necessarily for a lack of trying, but the free-flowing style which has been the blueprint for so much of their success in recent times has been all but abandoned over the past fortnight.

Aside from two moments of real quality from striker Jacob Murrell at Easter Road, the three points were largely earned thanks to a gritty, dig-your-heels-in kind of performance.

Murrell and fellow American CJ Fodrey have been taken into the hearts of Bairns fans

The 3-0 victory against Kilmarnock the following week was fairly comfortable in terms of the scoreline. But the hoolie provided by Storm Boelo rendered that affair a war of attrition rather than a game of football.

And then up at Pittodrie midweek, McGlynn himself admitted that the display was one to be endured rather than enjoyed.

That his side have collected nine points from nine in their last three outings despite being miles off their top level bodes well going forward. Not chucking in late goals has certainly helped spark this upturn in fortunes too.

Dundee United, St Johnstone and Dundee have all taken points off the Bairns this season with virtually the last kick of the ball. They could be five points better off at this stage had they managed to hold out. All ifs and buts, of course.

Yet, at the moment, they don’t even look like conceding. From back to front, the team is gelling together nicely.

Winning with a swagger is all good and well, and that will always be the aim for as long as McGlynn is at the helm. But we’re now seeing a side demonstrating they are every bit as capable of doing it the ugly way if required.

In some ways, the manager might take greater satisfaction in that, at least in the short term.

McGlynn, of course, deserves the bulk of the credit for turning things around. He has completely rebuilt this squad without complaint. The nature of the job and all that.

John McGlynn has once again proven himself a master in the art of squad rebuilding

And, in that regard, he has put several others with significantly bigger budgets to shame. Not that he has ever needed a particularly big budget to succeed anyway.

His eye for a player remains razor sharp. Nineteen-year-old Owen Eames isn’t realistically going to produce anything like the numbers supplied by his predecessor Miller – few could. But the Derby County loanee has taken no time at all to settle into this team. He’s getting better with each passing week.

The same can be said of the chap playing in front of him. Murrell has come a long way from missing two absolute sitters against Rangers on his home debut back in September, scoring five in his seven appearances since.

The American was never remotely prolific throughout his time with DC United in the MLS. In truth, there was little on his CV that would suggest he would be able to cut it. But fair play to him – and the Falkirk scouting team for that matter – for proving the rest of us wrong.

Murrell will no doubt be rubbing his hands at the prospect of going up against a Celtic defence which has been a doddle to get at all season long.

He is playing with the confidence of a guy who only needs one chance to find the back of the net. Against this opposition – top of the table or not – he may well get a few opportunities.

Falkirk have lost their last ten against Sunday’s visitors. However, considering the way they’re playing, this should be viewed as a genuine opportunity to halt that horrid sequence.

Liverpool will travel to take on Turkish giants Fenerbahce on Wednesday, battling to keep their perfect start to the Champions League's league-phase intact.

Andoni Iraola's Reds were beaten 1-0 by Arsenal on Sunday afternoon, though the boss will be pleased with his team's performance overall - as well as the fact there were no new injuries from the intense showdown at Anfield.

In the attacking third, Rio Ngumoha should start on the right wing, with Bradley Barcola on the left, the latter looking for his first goals since netting a hat-trick during the 6-3 win over LASK on matchday two.

Alexander Isak could begin the night on the bench, presenting an opportunity for Lewis Koumas to lead the line, supported by Florian Wirtz from the number 10 role while striker Hugo Ekitike continues his rehabilitation following the Achilles rupture he suffered in April.

#1872. Arsenal transfer news: Gunners 'set sights' on Junior Kroupi swoop - but face competition from two Champions League clubs

By Ben Sully | 03 Nov 2026 01:05, Last updated: 03 Nov 2026 02:50

Arsenal have reportedly earmarked Bournemouth star Junior Kroupi as a transfer target ahead of the January window.

The Gunners currently enjoy a three-point lead at the top of the Premier League table after winning eight of their nine matches this season.

Arsenal's league position is largely based on a strong backline that has recorded six clean sheets, the latest of which came in Sunday's hard-fought 1-0 win over Liverpool.

While their backline is their major strength, Arsenal can still improve at the opposite end of the pitch, which is an area Mikel Arteta is keen to address in the winter transfer window.

According to The Mirror, the Arsenal boss has made signing a 'top-class' striker his main priority for the winter market.

Arteta can currently call upon Kai Havertz and Viktor Gyokeres as his main centre-forward options, but the latter has netted just once in 12 appearances this term and has been linked with a potential move away.

The report claims the Gunners have their sights on Bournemouth's Kroupi, although they will need to overcome some major obstacles to pull off the transfer in the new year.

Champions League winners Paris Saint-Germain and German giants Bayern Munich are among those obstacles, with the European heavyweights believed to be among Kroupi's suitors.

Even if they can get ahead of their competition, Arsenal would still face the difficult task of convincing Bournemouth to part ways with an important player in the middle of the season.

Kroupi finished the 2025-26 Premier League season as Bournemouth's top scorer after netting 13 goals in 33 appearances.

The Frenchman's progress has been hampered by a foot injury which required surgery and forced him to miss the first two months of the season.

Kroupi has recently returned to the fray with three substitute appearances, although Bournemouth boss Marco Rose is keen to exercise caution with the minutes he gives the 20-year-old as he continues to build up fitness.

With Kroupi being eased back into action, Bournemouth will be reluctant to sanction his departure in January, especially as they will want to keep their key players to give them the best chance of enjoying success this term.

The Cherries harbour ambitions of going a long way in the Europa League, while they are also looking to match or go close to equalling last season's sixth-place finish in the Premier League.

#1871. Neuer dreaming of Champions League final after ‘exceptional’ win at Atletico

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Manuel Neuer believes the Metropolitano would be the perfect place to win the Champions League in the wake of Bayern Munich's victory over Atletico Madrid on Tuesday.

The Champions League final will be held at the venue on June 6, and Bayern boosted their hopes of reaching the next round with a 2-0 win over Diego Simeone's side.

Bayern needed to wait until the 54th minute to take the lead when Lennart Karl took advantage of Robin Le Normand's hesitation on the ball inside his own penalty area.

Konrad Laimer sealed the win 20 minutes later after rifling into the roof of the net having been picked out by Harry Kane, with the result ensuring Bayern got back to winning ways after back-to-back draws with Viking and Arsenal.

After also beating Real Madrid 2-1 away in last season's quarter-final, Bayern have now won consecutive away games in Spain in European competition for the first time ever.

Bayern (51) are also the second top five European league side to hit 50 goals in all competitions this season after Barcelona (60).

The Bundesliga giants have not won the Champions League since beating Paris Saint-Germain in the 2019-20 final, though Neuer is confident that Bayern can end their wait for a seventh title in the competition this season.

"Yes, absolutely. And perhaps winning here now is also a good omen," Neuer told Amazon Prime of Bayern's chances of winning the Champions League.

"Of course, it's a tough, challenging road for all of us, for all the teams who are usually favourites and contenders to make it to the final here.

"We believe we can do it. We have what it takes, and we'll give everything to make it happen."

𝘊𝘭𝘦𝘢𝘯 𝘴𝘩𝘦𝘦𝘵 𝘴𝘦𝘤𝘶𝘳𝘦𝘥 on his 164th UCL appearance https://t.co/OdVtIvRmE1

— FC Bayern (@FCBayernEN) November 3, 2026

Neuer made his 164th appearance in the Champions League, moving one ahead of Lionel Messi and Thomas Muller (163), with only Cristiano Ronaldo (183) and Iker Casillas (177) appearing more often, while also keeping a clean sheet in the process.

But it was Atletico who made the better start, with Julian Alvarez bending a shot just past the right post and Pablo Barrios seeing a goal-bound effort deflect over the crossbar.

From there, Bayern assumed control of the contest and finished with an expected goals (xG) total of 1.91 from their 19 shots to Atletico's 1.02 from their nine attempts.

"I'd say it was total dominance from the first minute to the 93rd. Whatever Atletico threw at us, we always had an answer," Neuer said of Bayern's display.

"And we're incredibly happy, especially considering the circumstances and the fact that we've had to make some adjustments due to injuries and everything that's happened at FC Bayern in recent days.

"But I think we stuck together, gave everything we had, and made sure we could enjoy a team performance like this. It was exceptional."

Bayern will also be hoping for a return to winning ways in the Bundesliga after last weekend's 2-2 draw in Der Klassiker with Borussia Dortmund, with Mainz up next on Saturday.

#1869. Barcelona vs. Aston Villa: ‘We have no fear at all’, Pau Torres identifies Barca weakness

By Axel Clody | 03 Nov 2026 06:55, Last updated: 03 Nov 2026 07:08

Barcelona have been through a run of tricky games, losing their 100% record in the Champions League and La Liga to Paris Saint-Germain and Real Madrid, and now, after recovering with two wins, they face another big challenge. On Tuesday, Barcelona host Aston Villa at the Camp Nou.

The English side have won every game in the European competition and are unbeaten in five Premier League matches. That is why Pau Torres, an undisputed starter for Aston Villa, is not afraid at all of the game against Barcelona.

‘We have no fear at all, but we do have respect. We know how difficult it will be, but nothing is impossible. We will try to compete with our own weapons’ - he said in an interview with Catalan newspaper Sport.

The 29-year-old defender also pointed out what to exploit in the contest.

Barcelona, under the management of Hansi Flick, are characterised by heavy pressing in the attacking half, which forces a high defensive line to keep up with the rest of the team. That space is something for Aston Villa to exploit, as Pau Torres explained, based on the profile of their trio of very quick attackers, including a Brazilian.

‘This year we have very vertical players, such as Ibrahim Mbaye, Alysson and Nicolas Jackson himself. They work very well when opponents leave space behind the defence.’

Of course, there is a way to attack, but for more than 60% of the time Barcelona’s opponents will be defending. Focus is a must if they are to avoid conceding against Barcelona, who have scored 57 times in 14 matches this season. ‘If we want to get a positive result, we will have to be alert defensively.’

Pau Torres also has a special mission. As a left-sided centre-back, he could come up against right winger Lamine Yamal several times because of the cover he will have to provide for left-back Ian Maatsen, who is known for being very attacking.

‘When you play this type of match, you always want to face the best to find out what level you are at. It will be a pleasure to play against Lamine and have to mark him on some occasions.

He always surprises, he is unpredictable and, often, just one player to mark him is not enough. We will have to be very alert to the cover from team-mates.’

The clash, which promises to be an interesting one, kicks off at 8pm UK time on Tuesday. Aston Villa share top spot in the Champions League league phase with Paris Saint-Germain, who are ahead on goals scored, Liverpool, Real Madrid and Real Betis. Barcelona are looking to recover after losing 4-2 to leaders Paris Saint-Germain in the last round.

#1868. James Trafford's old ghost returns to haunt him as Marco Rose's Bournemouth side claim another heavyweight scalp to make it six wins on the spin

Published: 13:23 EDT, 31 October 2026 | Updated: 16:56 EDT, 31 October 2026

How fitting it was, amid this season of werewolves and vampires, that it was one of James Trafford’s old ghosts that came back to haunt him.

No witches or zombies will give the Leeds goalkeeper a sleepless night quite like this familiar howler that cost his side the game.

The visitors dominated Bournemouth for most of the first half with confident, flowing football and thought they had a deserved lead when Dominic Calvert-Lewin bundled the ball into the net early on after a stunning passing move only for the goal to be ruled out for a handball.

Leeds were firmly on top…and then they had a goal-kick. Trafford didn’t take it but received it short and tried to pass it out to Ao Tanaka only to play it straight to the lurking Justin Kluivert, who squared it to Evanlison for a tap-in.

It was almost identical to the goal Trafford conceded at the Etihad Stadium against Tottenham at the start of last season, on his second league start for Manchester City, when he - again - received a short goal-kick and tried to pass it to a team-mate who was already surrounded. City signed Gianluigi Donnarumma 10 days later and Trafford’s City career was all-but over.

The England keeper has been able to resurrect it at Leeds, and came into the game with the best save percentage of any stopper in the Premier League, and marshaller of the second-best defence in the division behind only champions Arsenal.

Trafford made a fine save from a Marcus Tavernier free-kick, and another effort late on from Junior Kroupi but the damage had been done. He could do little about Amine Adli’s finish that doubled Bournemouth’s lead in second-half stoppage time. The Bournemouth supporters, who jeered him every time he touched the ball, made sure he didn’t forget it.

‘James is a terrific young goalkeeper,’ said Leeds boss Daniel Farke. ‘I’m pretty sure he will save us way more points than he perhaps has cost us today. We win together, we lose together. We’re all happy to have him. He’s still top class and has all my trust and all my love. My recommendation is that he shouldn’t watch the scene back!’

It was almost identical to the goal Trafford conceded against Tottenham at the start of last season when he - again - received a short goal-kick and passed it straight to the opposition

The English goalkeeper could do little about Amine Adli’s finish that doubled Bournemouth’s lead in second-half stoppage time

Bournemouth have made such a habit of punching above their weight in recent years, that victories over traditional Premier League big boys no longer seem as remarkable as they once did. Running your club brilliantly, signing excellent players and developing them with superb coaches season after season will tend to normalise such success for a club of this size.

The Cherries are no longer content to constrain their heroics to slaying mere domestic giants. In the space of 10 days, they have dispatched former European Cup winners AC Milan, Manchester United and Aston Villa — all 3-0 — and now former runners-up Leeds.

Yes, they needed a bit of luck and a glaring mistake to get them ahead but, once they got in front, they rarely looked like letting it slip. Brazilian sensation Rayan went close before substitute Adli wrapped it up late on after a stunning through ball from Kroupi.

Bournemouth needed a bit of luck and a glaring mistake to get them ahead but, once they got in front, they rarely looked like letting it slip

Bournemouth (4-2-3-1): Petrovic 7; Smith 7 (Diakite 88), Hill 8, Silva 7, Truffert 6; Adams 7, Christie 7 (Cook 6); Rayan 6 (Adli 88), Kluivert 7 (Kroupi 68, 8), Tavernier 7; EVANILSON 8 (Rodriguez 76).

Leeds (3-4-2-1): Trafford 5; Justin 6 (Bahoya 84), Elvedi 6, Muharemovic 7; Bogle 6, Ampadu 6, Tanaka 5 (Stach 65, 6); Gudmudsson 6 (Longstaff 65, 5); Wilson 6 (Aaronson 84), James 7 (Nmecha 65, 6); Calvert-Lewin 6.

What is even more impressive is that Bournemouth are doing it without Andoni Iraola at the helm, and under a manager in Marco Rose who was even feeling early grumblings of discontent from sections of the fanbase after failing to win any of their first six league games.

Now, it’s six wins in a row in all competitions. Sixteen goals scored, none conceded. Even for Bournemouth, who make the remarkable look normal, that’s quite something.

Not only that, they are doing it without influential midfielder Alex Scott, out with a hamstring injury, pulling the strings. When you have Ryan Christie and Tyler Adams keeping things ticking in the middle, with Justin Kluivert and Kroupi ahead of them, you barely even noticed.

Marco Rose was feeling early grumblings of discontent from sections of the fanbase after failing to win any of their first six league games

We’re approaching that time of year, with Halloween already upon us and Christmas coming into view, when the constant churn of January transfer rumours will soon become inescapable.

An early one doing the rounds is how Manchester United are ‘exploring a move’ for Calvert-Lewin.

Don’t fall for it, Dominic. He lost here but how different the afternoon could have gone had the ball not bounced on to his arm before going into the net. Even in defeat, this is still a club under Daniel Farke that’s stable, competent and moving in the right direction.

If United are really in the market for someone who knows where the net is, few are doing it with more ruthless efficiency than Bournemouth striker Evanlison, who made it four goals in as many games for the Cherries.

‘I just saw him said: “You are a real number 9”,’ said Bournemouth boss Marco Rose.

#1867. Why West Ham fans should welcome - and be wary of - Scott Parker appointment

Scott Parker is the frontrunner to succeed Nuno Espirito Santo, who was sacked as West Ham head coach on Tuesday morning with the club’s promotion hopes hanging in the balance.

West Ham were widely considered favourites to bounce straight back to the Premier League this season, but after six wins from their first 13 Championship games, they are down in eighth place.

Having recorded a £104.2million loss in the last financial year, the club are acutely aware of the financial imperative of returning to the top flight at the first opportunity and have moved swiftly to make a change in the dugout following successive home defeats to Southampton and West Brom.

Parker, a club legend who won three successive Player of the Year awards during a four-year stint in east London, is seen as someone who can not only get supporters back onside but has experience getting teams promoted from the Championship.

The 46-year-old has earned promotion to the Premier League on three separate occasions across spells with Fulham, Bournemouth and Burnley, but his success has not come without criticism.

His time at Fulham, who offered him his first senior managerial role in May 2019, was dominated by tensions with the board, and Parker openly criticised the club’s long-term structure and recruitment.

West Ham agree new manager appointment after Nuno sacking

West Ham confirm Nuno Espirito Santo sack decision as statement issued

Nuno under pressure as West Ham sent tumbling down Championship table

Discover a hidden island paradise in the Indian Ocean

Despite taking Fulham up from the Championship, Parker then struggled to build a competitive Premier League side and presided over a dispiriting relegation campaign, with his pragmatic style of play proving increasingly unpopular with supporters.

Parker left Fulham by mutual consent after their relegation in 2021 before swiftly taking charge at Bournemouth. While not direct rivals, the move left a bitter taste for some, with Bournemouth in direct competition with Fulham for promotion from the Championship.

Both teams went up automatically during the 2021/22 season. But while Fulham were able to stabilise under the guidance of Marco Silva, similar issues reared their head for Parker, and he was sacked four games into the season after questioning the direction and commitment of the club following a 9-0 defeat to Liverpool.

Parker’s comments, in which he said his team were "ill-equipped at this level", led Bournemouth’s then-owner Maxim Demin to hit back, stating that for the club to progress, everyone must “show belief in and respect for one another.”

Scott Parker is a manager with pedigree at this level but also plenty of baggage

West Ham will be aware of Parker’s history, including an ill-fated 67-day spell at Belgian side Club Brugge, and they will have made it clear during negotiations that he must secure promotion to secure his future.

After a toxic end to Nuno’s tenure, there will be a fair amount of goodwill for the former England international given his cult status at the club and his knowledge of the league.

The Championship is relentless, though, and results need to change quickly if West Ham are to keep pace with the top of the table and stop the chasing pack from gaining encouragement.

In Parker, West Ham believe they have a safe pair of hands who knows the club and knows how to get out of the Championship. Supporters are, however, bound to be more sceptical.

Parker’s vision for West Ham will almost certainly be built on defensive solidity, and with good reason. West Ham have conceded 18 goals in 13 league games this season, a rate of 1.4 goals per game.

Given the quality of the squad at his disposal, though, there will also be an expectation to entertain. West Ham, for all their struggles, have at times blown teams away this season, scoring in every game this term.

Parker is a manager with pedigree at this level but also plenty of baggage. West Ham can’t say they have not been warned.

#1866. Man United’s Roma comeback only matters if we back it up, says Carrick

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Michael Carrick believes Manchester United's dramatic 3-2 comeback win against Roma will only mean something if they can back it up.

The Red Devils were staring down the barrel of a fourth straight defeat as Matias Soule's 11th-minute opener and Donyell Malen's penalty had Gian Piero Gasperini's men 2-0 up at Old Trafford in Tuesday's Champions League encounter.

But Bruno Fernandes' spot-kick just before the hour had United back in the game, before Matheus Cunha scored twice in the 83rd and 86th minutes to complete a memorable fightback.

Not even a late red card for Cunha could take the gloss off as United stopped a nine-match winless run in all competitions.

The pressure has been seriously building on Carrick during that dismal run, but he was reluctant to view this win as a turning point just yet.

Speaking to Amazon Prime, Carrick – whose side host Aston Villa in the Premier League this weekend – said: "It's one game so it depends on what happens next. We've got to capitalise on that, but the boys showed an awful lot in the second half.

"This was right at that moment. It depends on what happens next. We've got to make the most of it, we've got to move forward, but I'm feeling a lot better about things.

"It's a win for us as a football club. To see the supporters go home happy is what we live for, to give them performances and nights like this so they can get back energised again.

"As a team, we've shown a lot of character to weather what we've had to. You find out a lot about each other. The players will find out things about me, I certainly do about them and their character, what it means to them and what they're prepared to put in."

— Manchester United (@ManUtd) November 3, 2026

Ten of United's 15 shots came in the second half, with 2.5 of their 2.7 total expected goals (xG) generated coming after the interval.

The Red Devils have won both of the last two Champions League home matches in which they have trailed by two-plus goals, also beating Atalanta 3-2 in October 2021, who were also managed by Gasperini.

Indeed, no team have won more Champions League games from two or more goals behind than United, with this their fourth time doing so (Real Madrid also four).

Carrick added: "It was a good game. I have to give a lot of credit to the players for starters, showing that character and quality when we needed it.

"This place does incredible things, magical things, and we spoke about it at half-time. I thought we grew into it a little bit in the first half after giving away the goals too easily.

"We spoke at half-time about how this place can change. It only takes one moment. The boys made every little bit of every little opportunity really and were fantastic in the end."

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

William Saliba handed Arsenal a huge boost by taking part in the final training session before the Champions League match against Slavia Prague.

The Frenchman has not played a single minute since he limped off after half an hour of France's World Cup semi-final against Spain.

Saliba was sent to see specialists on that back injury and while it was decided that surgery was not necessary, an extended period of rest has been required.

His recovery has gone well and Saliba has been back on the grass in recent weeks, going through individual training drills.

That has now been stepped up significantly, with Saliba understood to have to been back in first-team training on Monday.

The 25-year-old came through that without any issues and he was involved again on Tuesday morning, as the Arsenal squad trained in front of the media.

Mikel Arteta and his players will fly out to Prague later in the day ahead of facing Slavia Prague on Wednesday night.

It remains to be seen whether Saliba is included in that travelling squad, with Arsenal understandably cautious over his return to action.

The Gunners face Hull on Saturday before then having two weeks off for the November international break, allowing Saliba further time on the training pitch to build his fitness.

Saliba's return will leave Arteta with a serious selection headache heading into another hectic period.

Ezri Konsa, signed in the summer to cover for Saliba's absence, has been superb alongside Gabriel and probably Arsenal's best player so far this season.

The England international's strong form will allow Arsenal to ease Saliba back into action without taking significant risks with his fitness.

#1863. Man Utd next manager: Unai Emery to Old Trafford latest as fresh update emerges on Carrick replacement

By Lewis Blain | 03 Nov 2026 07:07

Manchester United continue to admire Aston Villa manager Unai Emery as they consider potential alternatives should Michael Carrick leave Old Trafford.

However, convincing the Spaniard to abandon his successful project at Villa Park could prove extremely difficult, with questions over how much authority he would receive in Manchester.

Eddie Howe and Julian Nagelsmann are also emerging as leading contenders, potentially giving the Red Devils several alternative options in their managerial search.

According to TEAMtalk, United decision-makers still highly regard Emery, and the club continues to explore potential replacements for Carrick behind the scenes.

The Spaniard has transformed Aston Villa into top-four contenders and guided them to Europa League success, establishing significant influence over the club's footballing operations.

That control has been central to his achievements, and Villa would be expected to fight hard to retain their manager if United formalised their interest.

Although the opportunity to take charge of one of Europe's biggest clubs could appeal to Emery, sources believe the level of authority available at Old Trafford would be a major stumbling block.

At Villa, Emery has been allowed considerable freedom over his methods and decision-making. United's structure and expectations are different, potentially making the role less attractive than it initially appears.

United are understood to be preparing for different scenarios despite publicly backing Carrick, with Emery remaining among the names held in high regard internally.

Former Newcastle United boss Howe is also heavily linked, with director of football Jason Wilcox reportedly favouring him. Meanwhile, director of recruitment Christopher Vivell is believed to prefer Nagelsmann.

Emery would be an impressive appointment on paper, but United may be wasting valuable time pursuing a manager who has little obvious reason to leave Villa.

He has built a successful project at Villa Park, enjoys considerable control and has established the club as a regular competitor for major honours.

Moving to Old Trafford would mean taking on a rebuilding job at a club that has struggled with managerial instability for more than a decade. There is no guarantee he would receive the same influence that has helped him thrive in Birmingham.

United should therefore concentrate on more realistic alternatives, with Howe potentially offering an attractive option given his Premier League experience and previous success at Newcastle.

Nagelsmann also deserves serious consideration, particularly if Vivell can convince the club's hierarchy that he is the right long-term appointment.

Emery's reputation makes him an understandable target, but United need a manager who genuinely wants the job and can work within their structure. On the available evidence, Howe and Nagelsmann may be more realistic options.

#1862. Where to watch Manchester United vs Roma: TV channel and live stream for Champions League today

The Standard's journalism is supported by our readers. If you click links to other sites on this page, we will earn commission.

Manchester United host Roma in the Champions League tonight as Michael Carrick desperately seeks an end to their woeful winless run.

The beleaguered Man Utd boss may now have only two games left to save his job, with a further review expected during the November international break, following Sunday’s home clash with Aston Villa in the Premier League.

Though his side delivered a much-improved first-half display against Chelsea at Stamford Bridge on Saturday, the wheels then swiftly fell off in familiarly chaotic fashion as Lisandro Martinez was dismissed in a 2-0 loss - United’s third in a row and fourth in the last five matches.

They have gone nine matches without a victory for the first time since the 1988/89 season to spark genuine concern over a potential relegation battle, having not won at all since their last Champions League home fixture - the 4-0 drubbing of Azerbaijani debutants Sabah FK on September 10.

But, having lost away at Atletico Madrid and Como since then to slip to 21st in the league phase table, they can expect a much sterner challenge from Roma, who continue to thrive despite a lengthy injury list that has seen them travel to Old Trafford with only 17 available outfield players.

The Giallorossi are in strong form under Gian Piero Gasperini and sit third in Serie A, still unbeaten and four points adrift of leaders Inter Milan after 10 games having won four of their last five matches across all competitions including Saturday’s 5-2 demolition of struggling Udinese.

Roma brushed aside Slovan Bratislava 4-0 in their last Champions League outing, having also been edged out by Real Madrid in a seven-goal thriller and drawn with Fenerbahce to sit 15th.

Carrick will hope to invoke the spirit of 2007, when he scored twice for United in a memorable 7-1 home trouncing of Roma in the Champions League quarter-finals.

TV channel and live stream: Unlike most Champions League fixtures, tonight’s game is not being shown live in the UK on TNT Sports.

Instead, it will be broadcast by Amazon Prime Video, who still have the first pick of one Tuesday night match up until the semi-finals.

Coverage begins at 6:30pm GMT ahead of an 8pm kick-off at Old Trafford, presented by Gabby Logan and featuring punditry from former Man United trio Wayne Rooney, Nicky Butt and Ashley Young.

#1861. Kevin Nisbet's lack of cool proved so costly for Aberdeen at Hampden... and underlines why he's not a man for the big occasion

By CALUM CROWE, SCOTTISH DEPUTY CHIEF SPORTS WRITER

Published: 18:27 EDT, 31 October 2026 | Updated: 18:32 EDT, 31 October 2026

In the build-up to this Premier Sports Cup semi-final, Aberdeen captain Kevin Nisbet spoke about the players needing to step up and deliver.

On a woeful run of form as they arrived at Hampden, and with huge pressure mounting on Stephen Robinson, Nisbet insisted the players owed the manager a performance and a result.

Just to take the heat off as much as anything else. With 76 minutes on the clock in this tense and cagey affair with Rangers, Nisbet had a golden opportunity.

With the score locked at 0-0, Stuart Armstrong fed a pass into Nisbet’s path and the ball was crying out to be struck first time.

Nisbet could probably see the whites of Ivor Pandur’s eyes. In the context of the game, it was as good a chance as Aberdeen could have hoped for.

But his finish was absolutely awful. Nisbet hesitated when he should have pulled the trigger straight away, allowing Olwethu Makhanya to make a block.

Aberdeen striker Kevin Nisbet reflects on a golden chance to fire Aberdeen ahead at Hampden

On such moments are cup semi-finals won and lost. Just seven minutes later, at the other end of the pitch, Ryan Naderi prodded home from close range to send Rangers through to the final.

Nisbet will surely be haunted by his miss. He has scored 13 goals this season. For all Aberdeen’s struggles, some have even touted him for a Scotland recall.

But he is not up to scratch at the top level. In some respects, he finds himself in the same boat as Lawrence Shankland.

Any time Shankland has been given an opportunity with Scotland, he hasn’t really taken it. Particularly in the World Cup in the summer.

Nisbet is a decent enough striker at Scottish Professional Football League level. But in the big moments in big games, he’s not good enough.

It was a chance he had to take. In the end, Aberdeen were left to rue what might have been as Rangers, who were poor for much of the game, edged through to the final.

All in all, this is a defeat which just piles more pressure on Stephen Robinson. His team did not play poorly but they did not win.

Nisbet took too long with the ball and allowed Olwethu Makhanya the chance to block his shot

There is no sense in trotting out excuses about being competitive and unlucky. Aberdeen were not unlucky.

They had a glorious chance to go in front late in the game and their captain wasted it. That is not misfortune. It is profligacy.

Robinson and his players now face a huge game against Hibs at Pittodrie next Saturday.

With the international break just around the corner, a time when clubs invariably change manager once the rot has set in, it could well be last-chance saloon for Robinson.

#1860. Crystal Palace make decision over Jean-Philippe Mateta red card appeal before Liverpool

Crystal Palace have lodged an appeal against the red card awarded to Jean-Philippe Mateta during their 2-0 defeat to Tottenham last Saturday.

Mateta was sent off in the 13th minute, following a VAR review, for a studs-up challenge on Micky van de Ven as the pair contested for a loose ball at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.

Referee Michael Oliver originally awarded Mateta a yellow card but upgraded his decision after being sent to the monitor to have a second look at the challenge.

With Palace down to 10 men, Spurs took control of the game and sealed a comfortable victory after goals in either half from Archie Gray and Jan Paul van Hecke.

Mateta landed on top of Van de Ven’s right ankle with his studs up as he chased a pass into space, and Oliver deemed the 29-year-old to have used “full forceful contact” as he explained his decision inside the stadium.

Palace’s view, though, is that Mateta’s challenge was accidental, and they argue that the French international had his eyes on the ball and did not see Van de Ven coming.

Mateta currently faces a three-match suspension, but Palace hope the decision is either overturned or his ban reduced.

Pierre Sage, who is under increasing pressure to turn things around at Palace, has only recently welcomed Mateta back into the fold after a hamstring injury and will desperately want his star striker back available.

If Mateta’s ban is upheld, he would miss this weekend’s home game against Liverpool, as well as crunch fixtures against newly promoted teams Coventry and Hull.

He will, however, be available for selection when Palace host Hoffenheim and Real Sociedad in the Europa League.

#1859. Real Madrid: how Franco Mastantuono is faring on loan at Fiorentina

By Axel Clody | 03 Nov 2026 07:08

Franco Mastantuono has finally been getting consecutive opportunities in European football. After a first year of ups and downs at Real Madrid, the young Argentine was loaned to Fiorentina this season and has played in all of the club’s games.

The high point of his spell, which began in August, has been the hat-trick against Venezia in the fourth round of Serie A, a 4-2 comeback win that made him the youngest Argentine player to score three times in Europe’s top five leagues. The first two goals were very much in the right winger’s style: cutting inside onto his left foot and placing the finish.

That result, however, was the only time the Florence side managed to win in Serie A. Fiorentina’s campaign has produced six defeats and two draws, which is why they sit on the edge of the relegation zone.

Mastantuono has not been involved in a goal since, even though he remains the team’s main attacking protagonist. One of the reasons lies in the young player’s biggest challenge so far in Italy, which he admitted himself in an interview shortly after arriving in the country.

Responsible for a third of his team’s league goals, the 19-year-old forward carries the responsibility of being the ‘owner’ of the attacking department in the side managed by Paolo Vanoli. He is always sought out on the wing for an individual move and delivers: he is the leader in ground duels won in the whole of Serie A (48, along with two other players) and third in successful dribbles, 18, alongside Nico Paz.

‘I am always looking to attack, going at opponents and showing personality’ - he explained his profile to the newspaper Gazzetta dello Sport on 4 September.

Thanks to his ability to win individual duels, he also constantly puts himself in a position to shoot, and is third in that statistic in the league too (33, the leader in the Fiorentina squad). He also provides passes for his team-mates’ shots (17 in all, 17th in the league and top in the squad).

The Argentine generates a lot of attacking play, that is undeniable, but the finishing of moves has almost always been negative. He has attempted 33 shots but only nine have been on target. ‘I need to improve in many things, including my efficiency in front of goal,’ he admitted, also to Gazzetta.

Another feature of his game, dribbling, also has issues that hamper Fiorentina and kill the team’s attacks. Mastantuono often wins a one-on-one and, instead of passing the ball, tries another, which makes him lose it.

His success rate in dribbles and ground duels is below half of those attempted (43% and 48% respectively). Among all Serie A players, he is second for possession losses, with 20. Manager Vanoli has already identified the issue, praising the youngster as the only one capable of setting the team’s tempo.

‘He is a talent who needs to be put at the service of the team and must improve his understanding of when to dictate the team’s rhythm. He is the only one who can do that. I told him that, in Italy, we are good at noticing when a player wants to dribble. He needs to improve in one-on-one situations and understand that, if he is double-marked, there will always be a team-mate free. And that means playing as a team’ - he said on 23 October.

This, however, is still common for Franco Mastantuono’s age. It is a natural maturing process. He still looks a very promising youngster, to the same extent as when he emerged at River Plate. He does not see much fairness in the criticism he receives.

‘People demand a lot of me. I understand, I know what they expect of me. Many times they are hard on me, but I try to make the most of it. [...] I do not complain about criticism.

I am a footballer and I understand that. But people talk about things that are outside my control. I just do my job and always try to do it well’ - he told TyC Sports in early October.

Mastantuono is answering some of that criticism on the pitch and, after the frustration of missing the World Cup because of his few minutes at Real Madrid, he was part of Argentina’s latest call-up. The forward, like Nico Paz and other youngsters, will be the future of Argentina in a new era without Lionel Messi and other experienced players.

#1858. Liverpool confirm Ryan Gravenberch injury blow as Andoni Iraola names squad for Champions League clash

Liverpool have been dealt a new injury blow as Ryan Gravenberch will miss the Champions League showdown against Fenerbahce.

Gravenberch has cemented himself as a regular in Liverpool’s midfield since the autumn international break, starting five of the seven matches across all competitions.

Gravenberch was expected to be in contention for Liverpool against Fenerbahce on Wednesday, but it has since been revealed that the Dutchman will not be making the trip to Turkey.

“He will instead remain at the AXA Training Centre to undergo treatment with the club’s medical team.”

As such, Gravenberch joins Hugo Ekitike, Conor Bradley, Giovanni Leoni and fellow Dutchman Jeremie Frimpong as the five Liverpool injury absentees against Fenerbahce.

Iraola issued an update on the Dutchman on Tuesday: "It is a day to day thing.

“The fracture healed, it is about the pain. He has some discomfort. It is going to be something every day we will ask him how he is."

Wataru Endo and Federico Chiesa, meanwhile, are unavailable due to not being named in the club’s squad list for the Champions League this season.

It remains to be seen if Gravenberch will be fit to face Crystal Palace at the weekend, though he has a battle on his hands to regain a midfield spot from Trey Nyoni.

“The thinking is that he's playing very well and we trust him," Iraola told Sky Sports pre-match of his decision to drop Gravenberch in favour of Nyoni against Arsenal.

#1857. Chivu still striving for consistency after Inter’s victory over Feyenoord

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Cristian Chivu insisted that consistency would be key to achieving what Inter are trying to build this season following their victory over Feyenoord in the Champions League.

Inter arrived into Tuesday's clash at Stadion Feijenoord on the back of a 3-1 defeat to AC Milan in the Derby della Madonnina, which was their first Serie A loss of the season.

But they responded with a 3-0 win over Feyenoord, with Yann Bisseck, Francesco Pio Esposito and Piotr Zielinski all on target against their Eredivisie opponents.

Chivu's side took the lead in the eighth minute when Bisseck picked out the bottom left corner before Esposito's header struck the crossbar and found its way past Tjark Ernst.

Zielinski added to Inter's advantage nine minutes after the restart as the Serie A giants registered their 87th win in the Champions League, drawing level with rivals Milan for the joint-second most of any Italian club, only Juventus have more (118).

Inter also remain unbeaten across their 14 Champions League meetings with Dutch sides (W11 D3), with this 3-0 win being their biggest against a Dutch club in the competition.

Cesc Fabregas' Como are up next in their next Serie A outing, and Chivu is hoping the confidence-boosting win over Feyenoord gives his team the momentum they need to get back to winning ways in the league.

"Consistency is what brings results, it gives you self-confidence and belief in what you are doing, it is what we are looking for at this moment," Chivu told Sky Sport Italia, as quoted by Football Italia.

"This game gives us a big boost of confidence in what we are building, so we know football can take you down some strange paths, but you must be able to react and get back onto the right path."

RETURNING TO MILANO WITH THREE POINTS IN THE https://t.co/vkWHVXvwoA

Inter had been criticised for their bad starts in recent matches, with this the first time they had taken the lead as early as the eighth minute since August.

Bisseck's strike saw him score his first goal in the Champions League (27th appearance), becoming just the second German player to score for Inter in the competition, after Robin Gosens against Barcelona in October 2022.

It was assisted by Djed Spence, who registered his first goal involvement in any club competition since April 2025, ending a 58-game run without a goal contribution. He also became the first English player to either score or assist for Inter in the Champions League.

And Chivu believes Inter were "the best version of ourselves" against Feyenoord, adding: "We have certain values, we understand certain things and put them on the pitch.

"That doesn't mean we haven't done well so far this season.

"We tried to be the best version of ourselves, it worked with organisation, intensity and everything we needed for a strong performance in a stadium that is not easy to play in.

"We always have discussions after every game, whether it goes well or badly, we try to correct errors and build on our strengths.

"Sometimes it goes better than others, perhaps we understood what wasn't going on as well.

"The Inter world, the club owners, the fans, we are all aware of the values of these players who want to fly the flag high. That has never been in doubt."

#1854. Jose Mourinho identifies key Arsenal star as 'dream' Real Madrid target - and it's not Declan Rice

By Lewis Blain | 03 Nov 2026 07:33

Real Madrid are keeping a close eye on Arsenal defender Riccardo Calafiori, with Jose Mourinho identifying the Italian as a 'dream' addition to his squad.

The 24-year-old has become an important figure under Mikel Arteta since arriving in a £42m deal from Bologna in 2024, attracting admiration from one of Europe's biggest clubs.

However, the Gunners are in a strong contractual position and have no intention of allowing their defender to leave easily.

Mourinho considers Calafiori his preferred left-back target, with Real Madrid's recruitment staff also sharing their admiration for the Italian international, as per recent reports.

The LaLiga heavyweights have already made initial enquiries about his situation and are weighing up a move next summer, having also been credited with an interest in Martin Zubimendi in recent months.

However, it is the Italy international now on their radar, with his versatility a major attraction, having demonstrated his ability to operate both at left-back and centrally. Madrid believe those qualities could offer Mourinho valuable options across the defence.

Manchester City's Josko Gvardiol is another player admired by the Spanish giants, but Calafiori is understood to be their first-choice option.

Arsenal, however, are determined to retain the defender, whose contract at the Emirates runs until 2029. The Gunners are planning to discuss a new deal with Calafiori in 2027, once they have prioritised extensions for Jurrien Timber, Martin Odegaard and Declan Rice.

Arsenal should have absolutely no interest in entertaining Madrid's advances for Calafiori, who has developed into one of Arteta's most important players.

Initially signed as a centre-back, the Italian has flourished at left-back, with Gabriel and William Saliba's partnership allowing him greater freedom to contribute further forward.

His start to the 2026-27 campaign has been particularly impressive. He scored in the opening minute of the Community Shield against Manchester City, registered assists against Coventry City and Aston Villa, and pipped several alternatives to Arsenal's Player of the Month award for August.

Calafiori offers far more than defensive reliability, combining aggressive forward runs, quality crossing and the ability to drive through opposition pressure.

At 24, he also has plenty of room to develop further, making him an important part of Arsenal's long-term plans.

Mourinho's admiration is understandable, but Arsenal have no reason to weaken their defence by selling a player who has become such an effective part of Arteta's system.

A new contract should be the priority rather than entertaining a potential transfer.

#1853. Manchester United vs Roma 'set for disruption' amid planned fan protests

Manchester United’s Champions League clash with Roma tonight could be facing disruption.

The Red Devils are looking to snap their nine-game winless run at Old Trafford this evening, but they may have to wait for kick-off with a planned supporters’ protest.

One fan group - the Stretford Enders - has planned to hand out 4,000 green and gold balloons while the Champions League anthem plays around the stadium just before kick-off.

It is thought to be a protest directed at the club’s ownership, the Glazer family and INEOS, with the former overseeing a sharp decline of footballing success in their 21 years of stewardship.

The protests have not been promoted on social media, but reports leaked out in The i and The Athletic ahead of the game.

There was also thought to be plans for a banner to read “No new stadium, we want new owners”, but that will not be shown as UEFA did not sanction it in time for the match, according to The i’s report.

It is believed that a similar protest is planned for this weekend’s Premier League encounter with Aston Villa.

United sit 20th in the Champions League table after two defeats and a victory on their return to Europe’s top table.

That came against minnows Sabah at Old Trafford, before heavy losses at Atletico Madrid and Como.

Further defeats by Bournemouth and Chelsea have thrown manager Michael Carrick’s position into serious question, although the head coach has so far survived the sack, with it being reported that his position will be reassessed during the upcoming November international break.

#1852. RANGERS 1 ABERDEEN 0: Ryan Naderi the Hampden hero as Light Blues squeeze past dogged Dons to reach final

Published: 16:41 EDT, 31 October 2026 | Updated: 18:41 EDT, 31 October 2026

Ryan Naderi is developing the happy knack of turning up in the right place at the right time for Rangers. And, by Jove, how they needed him to deliver something to break the deadlock in this one and book a spot in the Premier Sports Cup final back at Hampden next month.

Derek McInnes’ side weren’t as bad at the national stadium as they were midweek in scraping a 2-2 draw away to Hearts, but they certainly weren’t all that good. Aberdeen turned up to frustrate them last night and succeeded for the large part, making a number of notable chances themselves.

There’s an obligation to drop in some kind of pun about Hallowe’en in this account of what went down between these two sides, so let's discuss how Dons’ captain Kevin Nisbet must have spent last night suffering nightmares following his own personal horror show just 14 minutes from time.

With the game back hanging in the balance in the wake of a strong period of Rangers pressure, Stephen Robinson’s side broke forward in numbers and, even after Nisbet had failed to find substitute Mitchy Ntelo with a pass, the ball was picked up by Stuart Armstrong and fed back into the skipper’s path on the right-hand side of the box.

He had to smash it first-time. Hard and low across the keeper. Inexplicably, for a guy who does know how to find the net and has done it plenty of times throughout his career, he took a touch and allowed Olwethu Makhanya the opportunity to get across and put in a crucial block.

In that instant, you wondered if the Dons’ big chance had come and gone. Naderi provided the answer just seven minutes later.

Rangers striker Ryan Naderi celebrates his late semi-final winner at Hampden Park

Rangers boss Derek McInnes enjoys the moment at full-time as his side are through to the final

The Czech internationalist endured a grim start to the season as a lone frontman, but has come into his own since being deployed beside Kevin Kelsy and shown that precious ability to score goals that really change things, really matter.

He scored the winner at Celtic Park in September, of course, as well as a home winner against Motherwell. Last time out against St Johnstone, his second-half effort to notch the second goal of what ended up a 4-0 romp was expertly timed as his team-mates had failed to wake up at the start of the second 45 and looked like they might fall flat on their faces.

Once again, he rode to the rescue here, reading the play, making a run, getting into space and finishing from close-in for his eighth of the campaign. The kind of bread-and-butter goal you want your strikers to score.

A cross in from the left from Rangers’ best player Badredine Bouanani, turning up on the wrong wing for some reason, was cleared by Connor Ronan to substitute Dan Neil 25 yards out.

His short pass to James Penrice resulted in a low shot into the area and Naderi timed his run perfectly to ghost in and convert from close range.

It was a sickening blow to under-pressure Robinson and his players. They had dug in really well, pulled off the game plan nicely and kept themselves in it throughout. Their display belied the league form that has put the manager’s job on the line ahead of next Saturday’s teatime visit of Hibernian.

It all counts for nothing in the end, though. As they reflect on events in Mount Florida, they will know that they came up against a Rangers side that most definitely dominated possession — and probably deserved the win in the end — but was vulnerable at times and failed to function as McInnes would have wanted.

The Ibrox boss pulled something of a surprise in his starting line-up by dropping vice-captain Neil and putting left-back Penrice in beside skipper-for-the-night Nico Raskin. It didn’t really work, though.

Listen, those guys weren’t exactly the core of the problem. A lot of the time, the ball wasn’t even being played through midfield, but the switch-up just didn’t feel like it worked. The balance wasn’t right.

For most of the first half, in particular, not very much was right about Rangers. They had plenty of the ball but Aberdeen set up in a 5-3-2 formation and kept them quiet while managing to create good chances of their own on the counter-attack.

Rangers were too slow. Not creative enough. Everything truly positive and dangerous they did went through Badredine Bouanani on the right, but there has to be infinitely more variation in their play rather than just getting it to the on-loan Algerian and hoping those quick feet of his can work some magic.

It was heartbreak for Aberdeen's Nicky Devlin as they fell just short in the semi-final

When he was brought in from German side VfB Stuttgart, the chat was that the management team saw him as an ideal weapon to break down teams playing a low block. He has the ability to beat a man, play in tight spots, have a shot.

However, there’s got to be more about Rangers than that. In this game, as with the 2-2 midweek draw with Hearts at Tynecastle, there just wasn’t enough in the way of fluent, purposeful play. They’ve looked nothing like the side that blew St Johnstone away last weekend with some exhilarating football and that must be a worry for McInnes.

By this stage of the season, they should be starting to find their stride, develop more in the way of consistency.

It took Rangers 44 minutes, for example, to fashion a shot on target. Naturally, it came from Bouanani, a low effort from a central position being saved low to his right by Aberdeen goalkeeper Marius Muller.

Up until that point, the better of the opportunities had fallen to the Dons. Midway through the opening period, Raskin played a pass wide to Dujon Sterling that carried just too much jeopardy.

Nesta Guinness-Walker nipped in to steal possession and then took the ball for a run all the way into the final third before releasing a decent low effort which Ibrox No1 Ivor Pandur had to save to his left.

With ten minutes of the half to play, Nisbet then sent a header wide from a great position after moving onto a cross from Brad Lyons.

At that stage, all Rangers had to shout about was an appeal for a penalty turned down on the 16-minute mark when Dons striker Ayoub Mouloua clearly handled the ball in his own area under pressure from Manny Fernandez.

Referee Ryan Lee didn’t give the award with VAR John Beaton backing up that call. It was controversial and no mistake.

Towards the end of the first half, however, it looked like things might be starting to click for McInnes’ men. Naderi put a header just over from a Raskin cross after getting in behind Jack Milne and Min-su Kim, massively disappointing again and eventually replaced by Djeidi Gassama, sliced an effort wide directly in front of goal.

Yet, it remained stodgy for Rangers after the restart. In the wake of Naderi just failing to get on the end of a low shot from Bouanani at the back post, a deflected Nisbet shot at the other end had to be saved low and smartly by Pandur.

Kelsy missed a sitter just after the hour when putting a header miles wide from a brilliant Bouanani cross and Muller had to block a shot from the Algerian wide man with his right boot as Rangers enjoyed their most dangerous and insistent period of the match.

It didn’t last, but Nisbet dallied when it mattered while Naderi just let his instinct take control for a sharp little conversion from that Penrice effort.

McInnes now has his first shot at silverware as Rangers manager pending and that’s what he wanted going into this game.

However, he needs to find a way to get this team slicker, tighter, more joined-up. More relentless. More focused. More composed in key areas.

As if a reminder of that was needed, it came in time added-on when Armstrong picked up the ball at the edge of their box and bent a fine effort just wide of Pandur’s left-hand post.

So near and yet so far. The story of Aberdeen’s night, really. A night where a big chance definitely existed, but just couldn’t be taken.

#1851. Mikel Arteta confirms major Arsenal injury boost in new William Saliba update

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Mikel Arteta has confirmed William Saliba is ready to make his Arsenal return after coming through a behind-closed-doors friendly without any setbacks.

Saliba has not played since he was forced off in France's World Cup semi-final defeat to Spain.

A serious back injury has required a significant period of rest, after specialists advised in the summer that surgery was not required.

Saliba is back in full training and he has travelled with the Arsenal squad for their Champions League match against Slavia Prague on Wednesday.

"He's in a really good place," Arteta said on Tuesday.

"The process and the timings and the manner that the injury has been dealt with, especially the feelings that Willy has been having along the way, they have been very, very positive.

"His evolution has been as expected, which is not always the case. He feels really comfortable.

Arsenal are expected to be cautious with Saliba's return to competitive action, particularly with Ezri Konsa impressing alongside Gabriel so far this season.

However, Arteta played down the suggestion that he will drip-feed Saliba his minutes to get up to speed, warning the defender that he expects him to be available to play a full role for the team.

"Now he's in. He's in like anybody else. All the preparation has been done to make sure all the load and all the steps have been done to minimise the risk.

"He's in a really good place, he's built the capacity that we needed. Now it's about giving him minutes.

"He's a centre-back. When that's the case, it's not like an attacking midfielder or a No9 you can change. A centre-back normally has to be able to play 90 minutes.

#1850. Aston Villa transfer news: Unai Emery handed huge January transfer boost over £33m midfield target

By Lewis Blain | 03 Nov 2026 07:52

Aston Villa could have an opportunity to strengthen their midfield in January, with Galatasaray reportedly prepared to listen to offers for former target Gabriel Sara.

The Brazilian has attracted interest from several Premier League clubs, including Unai Emery's side, after impressing since leaving Norwich City in 2024.

With the Turkish giants now seemingly willing to negotiate, Villa could have a realistic opportunity to secure a long-standing transfer target.

According to reports in Brazil (via Sport Witness), Newcastle United, Everton and Brighton & Hove Albion are all also interested in signing Sara, alongside Villa, ahead of the January transfer window.

The 27-year-old previously spent two seasons at Carrow Road, establishing himself as one of the Championship's standout midfielders before joining Galatasaray in 2024.

His performances in Turkey have continued to attract attention, with Napoli and AS Roma also reportedly keeping in contact with his representatives.

Galatasaray were reluctant to consider a departure during the summer, when Villa were seeking a replacement for the departed Youri Tielemans, but their stance has now softened ahead of January.

It is believed that the Turkish champions are prepared to negotiate offers starting at €40m (£33m), although reports in Turkey suggest a fee closer to €35m (£30m) could potentially be enough.

While there is no guarantee that Villa or any of the interested clubs will meet Galatasaray's valuation, the willingness to discuss a sale now represents an encouraging development.

Galatasaray's £33m asking price would represent a significant mid-season investment for Villa, although the possibility of negotiating closer to £30m could make the deal slightly more attractive.

Emery needs greater depth in his squad, particularly in central midfield, where additional quality and competition could prove valuable across the second half of the season.

Sara's previous Championship experience means he already understands English football, while his development in Turkey suggests he could return to the Premier League as a more complete midfielder.

At 27, he would also offer a balance of experience and longevity, rather than being purely a long-term investment.

Villa will face stiff competition from the Magpies and the Toffees, but Galatasaray's changing stance gives Emery a genuine opportunity to revisit his past interest.

If the price can be brought down, Sara could represent an attractive January addition for a Villa side looking to maintain its competitiveness across multiple fronts.

#1849. Flick thrilled to end Barcelona’s clean-sheet drought against Aston Villa

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Hansi Flick said the most impressive aspect of Barcelona's 3-0 win over Aston Villa in the Champions League was the performance of his defenders to earn a rare clean sheet.

Barcelona returned to winning ways in the competition at the Camp Nou on Tuesday, with Lamine Yamal's seventh-minute strike laying the foundations for their triumph.

Yamal capitalised on Joao Gomes' risky pass across his own goal before picking out the bottom-left corner, which proved to be a record-breaking strike.

The 19-year-old became the teenager with the most goals in Champions League history (14), surpassing the previous record, set by Real Madrid's Kylian Mbappe (13).

And two goals in 12 minutes after the break from Barcelona captain Raphinha sealed the win, but it was at the other end where Flick felt his team deserved the most praise.

Barcelona picked up their first clean sheet in the Champions League since a 4-0 win over Borussia Dortmund in April 2025, ending a run of 18 games without one, while they have now won 11 of their last 13 home games in the competition against English clubs (D2).

They limited Unai Emery's team to an expected goals (xG) total of just 0.72 from their nine attempts, with only one of those forcing Joan Garcia into making a save.

"The best thing about the match? The clean sheet. I'm very happy with that because we defended a very good attack like Aston Villa's," Flick told reporters.

"Of course, it was important. They are a great team. We defended well, and we were happy with what we saw in defence.

"Everyone gave their maximum to finish with a clean sheet and we scored our goals. We're pleased."

A great win at home, Hansi! https://t.co/V1qqYCM81G

— FC Barcelona (@FCBarcelona) November 4, 2026

Barcelona have now failed to score in just one of their previous 20 home games in the Champions League (W15 D2 L3), netting 65 goals in that time (3.3 per game).

The Blaugrana have also had at least five big chances in each of their last three Champions League games for the first time since December 2020.

It was a result that saw Barcelona inflict Villa's joint-heaviest defeat in major European competition, having also lost by three goals to Royal Antwerp in September 1975 (1-4) and Inter in November 1990 (0-3), both in the UEFA Cup.

And Villa's downfall was from their own making after Gomes' mistake for Yamal's goal. No Premier League side has committed more errors leading to goals in all competitions this season than the Villans (seven, level with Sunderland).

Flick, however, said that Barcelona's opener was something they had worked on, explaining: "This is our idea of how we want to play football.

"We try to press them high, so that they make mistakes. We had this moment, were in the right position, and we pressed them well, and they made this mistake and we used it."

Flick was also on hand to explain his decision behind replacing Rodri for Marc Bernal at half-time, with the Barcelona boss citing a slight injury problem for the Spaniard.

"We took him off at half-time because he felt some muscular pain. It'll need to wait until Wednesday before we examine that and find out more," Flick said.

Ashley Young has lambasted Lisandro Martinez ahead of Manchester United’s Champions League clash with Roma.

The centre-back was not acknowledged by his manager as he trudged off at Stamford Bridge, despite issuing an apology a few days after he had made his public comments on the club’s recruitment strategy.

Former United man Young believes that his old employers need to “get rid” of the defender, whose contract expires at the end of the season.

#1847. Cardinale: “Milan were at the top of the world, and we’re going to bring them back there”

AC Milan owner Gerry Cardinale spoke to CBS Sports before the derby win over Inter, pledging to bring the club back to the summit of football.

On Halloween night, the Rossoneri ensured that Inter’s derby nightmare continued as Milan won their fourth consecutive victory in the fixture, extending the unbeaten run against the Nerazzurri to eight meetings in the process.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

All of the damage was done in the first half. Christian Pulisic struck in the fourth minute with a header, Adrien Rabiot scored from a corner six minutes later, Alessandro Bastoni halved the deficit and then Diego Moreira converted a lovely free-kick to reopen the two-goal advantage.

In the end, 3-1 is how it would stay, securing a memorable win. Cardinale spoke with the CBS panel in the build-up to kick-off at San Siro last night and he shed a bit more light on his plans for the Rossoneri moving forward. His words are via MilanNews.

“Well, first of all, this stadium… As an American, I can say that a stadium like this is something you never see anywhere else. Tonight, it’s going to light up. There’s something different about this derby tonight than in the past.

“There’s an electricity here that I’ve never felt before. You’ll see nearly 80,000 people literally shaking this structure. It’s going to be truly incredible.”

“It is. You know, when we bought the club four years ago, I started working on this right away. And part of what we’re trying to do here is bring the best of America to Italian soccer, and specifically to AC Milan.

“It’s extraordinary: most people didn’t think we could accomplish all this, or even get to this point. Not only did we announce the stadium this week, but we also announced the largest naming rights deal in history. I think it’s a wonderful thing for Italian soccer.

“The message to everyone is that we’re coming back. Italian soccer truly deserves to be at the top again, and we’ll do everything we can through AC Milan to make that happen.”

“There’s a connection between us. We’re two guys from Pennsylvania trying to make their way and understand Italy. He’s ‘Captain America’, but he’s also my franchise player. I couldn’t be more thrilled to have him with us.

“It’s a true partnership with him. He’s a leader, and his presence on the court makes all the difference in the world. You’ve seen it this year: when he steps on the court, he completely changes the game.”

Why is AC Milan and winning with Milan so important to you?

“I remember George Steinbrenner telling me about twenty years ago, ‘Don’t get too emotionally involved in all this; don’t go into the locker room, don’t do those things’. But in this case, I got emotionally involved.

“For me, it became a personal issue. And I don’t know what it is: maybe it’s just that… look around, listen. This means so much to the people of Milan, it has a huge impact on them, and I feel a huge responsibility.

“AC Milan were at the top of the world, and we’re going to bring them back there. This will probably be one of the greatest things I’ll do in my career.”

“It’s something multigenerational. This stadium is an icon. Look around, look at these people: this means everything to them. All of this carries with it an enormous amount of responsibility, it almost makes your wrists tremble.

“The best thing I can do is do my job well to help this club win, because victory spreads to the whole community. Listen… can you hear? That’s the Curva. You don’t see anything like it in America, it’s truly special.”

What’s your favourite detail of the new stadium?

“What we tried to do with the new stadium was to live up to the name and tradition of this facility. This is San Siro, but it is also ‘La Scala del Calcio’, the opera house of football.

“When you look at the design of the new stadium, those majestic, slender lines on the exterior recall the grand drapes and curtains of La Scala. It is our tribute to the history of this city.”

How did you manage to unblock the stadium situation?

“It’s been an incredible collaboration, a true partnership with our president Paolo Scaroni and the mayor. It’s extraordinary because everyone told me it’s impossible to build a stadium here in Italy. The last major stadium built in Italy was in 2011 in Turin, with about 40,000 seats.

“The extraordinary thing about our project is that it will be a 75,000-seat stadium, and we expect to have it completed before the 2032 European Championships. It will be a great thing for all of Italy.”
